§ 2. The Board of Advisors shall, in consultation with the Administrator of Parks, Recreation and Cultural Affairs, develop and propose to the Mayor a plan for the use, development, maintenance, management and operation of Sailors' Snug Harbor.

§ 3. The Board shall use all practical means to keep the public informed of its deliberations and before proposing its plan for the Harbor to the Mayor, shall hold a public hearing thereon.

§ 4. The Administrator of Parks, Recreation and Cultural Affairs shall, from time to time, report on the use, development, operation and management of Sailors' Snug Harbor and shall consult with the Board with respect to the same.

§ 5. This Order shall take effect immediately.

ABRAHAM D. BEAMAN, Mayor

title: TELEPHONE REDUCTIONS
full_text:
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 48

DECEMBER 9, 1975

TELEPHONE REDUCTIONS

Whereas, The City of New York is currently in a fiscal crisis which mandates curtailment of programs in areas where financial economies may be realized; and

Whereas, The total annual telephone expenditure made by The City of New York is deemed an area in which considerable economies can be realized; and

Whereas, The Public Service Commission has recently authorized a further increase in the charges allowable for telephone service; and

Whereas, There has been a significant reduction in the number of employees on the City payroll; and

Whereas, The Municipal Services Administration has demonstrated financial economies by developing policies and programs designed to effect substantial telephone savings in its administration; and

Whereas, There exists a need to realize telephone savings in all City agencies.

Now, therefore, by the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. All agencies are to immediately reduce their telephone equipment expenditures, as reflected in the financial plan for fiscal year 1975-1976 as approved by the Emergency Financial Control Board (Code 402), by not less than ten (10) per cent. Each agency shall, within thirty (30) days of the date of this Executive Order, furnish a detailed report to the Office of Management and Budget showing the methods used to accomplish these savings. Such methods shall not include relocations or other alterations that incur charges.

§ 2. The Municipal Service Administrator is hereby charged with the duty and responsibility of immediately developing plans, procedures, priorities and policies for achieving the proper, efficient and most economical use of the telephone systems in all agencies of The City of New York whose telephone expenditures are chargeable to the Municipal Services Administration budget and shall promulgate rules, regulations and orders for the implementation thereof. The Administrator is further vested with the authority and charged with the duty of enforcing and implementing any such rules, regulations and orders.

§ 3. All affected departments and agencies are directed to fully cooperate, assist and immediately implement all policies and orders of the Municipal Services Administrator or his designated representatives, pursuant to this Executive Order.

§ 4. The Municipal Services Administrator shall render periodic reports to the Mayor indicating the policies, implementation, effectiveness and savings achieved as a result of this program.

§ 5. All non-mayoral governmental agencies are urged to implement comparable cost reductions and are invited to participate in any plans, procedures, priorities and policies developed as a result of this Executive Order.

§ 6. The New York Telephone Company has agreed to cooperate in the implementation of equipment expenditure reductions and shall coordinate their efforts with
the Municipal Services Administrator and the Office of Management and Budget.
Upon completion of the equipment reduction program, the New York Telephone
Company has consented to continue examining the communication network and shall
make further recommendations regarding increasing efficiency and economies.

§ 7. This Executive Order shall take effect immediately.

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.

title: DELEGATION OF AUTHORITY TO FIRST DEPUTY MAYOR 1
full_text:
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 49

JANUARY 22, 1976

DELEGATION OF AUTHORITY TO FIRST DEPUTY MAYOR

Whereas, The City of New York may, from time to time, enter into agreements with the Municipal Assistance Corporation for The City of New York; and

Whereas, John E. Zuccotti, First Deputy Mayor, is fully familiar with the facts necessary to enter into such agreements.

Now, therefore, by virtue of the power vested in me as Mayor and pursuant to Section three of the City Charter, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. John E. Zuccotti, First Deputy Mayor, is hereby delegated the authority to act for, on behalf of and at the direction of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to Article 10 of the Public Authorities Law, as amended (the "Act"), including, but not limited to, full power to execute for, on behalf of and at the direction of the Mayor any agreement between the City and the Municipal Assistance Corporation for The City of New York pursuant to Section 3038 of the Act, any certificate pursuant to Section 3037 of the Act and any other document in connection with the Act.

§ 2. The exercise of functions, powers and duties by the First Deputy Mayor for, on behalf of and at the direction of the Mayor pursuant to this Executive Order shall not require the consent in writing of the Mayor or any other officer of the City.

§ 3. Executive Order No. 39 dated September 8, 1975, is hereby revoked, provided, however, that nothing in this Executive Order shall be construed to affect the validity of any act performed pursuant to such Executive Order and prior to the date hereof.

§ 4. This Executive Order shall take effect immediately and remain in effect until revoked by a subsequent Executive Order.

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 50

JANUARY 16, 1976

AMENDMENT OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 36

DATED AUGUST 28, 1975

Whereas, The City of New York recognizing the need to improve the quality and delivery of youth services to assist youth development and to prevent and reduce juvenile delinquency; and

Whereas, the City is required to conform to the statutes and administrative rules of the State of New York in order to receive and utilize the maximum allocation of funds available for youth services; and

Whereas, steps are currently being taken by The City of New York to effect a decentralization of youth services by redistributing the functions of the Youth Services Agency and thereby improving the delivery of such services; and

Whereas, it is necessary and desirable to amend Executive Order No. 36, dated August 28, 1975, so as to decentralize youth services.

Now, therefore, by the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. The support staff of the New York City Youth Board shall herein-after be referred to as the New York City Youth Bureau and all references to the Youth Board staff contained in Executive Order No. 36, dated August 28, 1975, are hereby deleted and replaced by the term "Youth Bureau".

§ 2. Section 6 of the Executive Order No. 36 dated August 28, 1975, is hereby amended to read as follows:

"§ 6. To implement policies approved by the Mayor and to develop better coordination of service delivery, a Youth Operations Panel is hereby established consisting of the heads of the following agencies: Department of Recreation, Criminal Justice Coordinating Council, Special Services for Children, Police Department, Department of Employment, Office of Neighborhood Services, Board of Education, Department of Health, Department of Probation, the Administrative Judge of the Family Court and the Office of Management and Budget."

§ 3. Section 10 of Executive Order No. 36 is hereby amended to read as follows:

"§ 10. Certain services formerly administered by the Youth Services Agency are assigned to the City agency primarily responsible for coordinating such services, as follows:

(a) The youth employment programs are hereby transferred to the Department of Employment;

(b) The recreation support services are hereby transferred to the Department of Recreation;

(c) Youth outreach personnel of the Youth Services Agency are hereby transferred to the Office of Neighborhood Services for the purpose of developing a City-Wide Community outreach program, except those outreach personnel which are hereby transferred to the Bureau of Special Services for Children of the Department of Social Services to assist the delinquency prevention and court diversion programs of that Bureau.

(d) The contractual expenditures for youth services now administered by the Youth Services Agency, shall be administered by the Youth Bureau in conjunction with the City agencies responsible for handling those services. The staff of the Youth Bureau shall review all contracts and develop policies for the equitable allocation of such contracts.

§ 4. There shall be a new section added to Executive Order No. 36, which shall be numbered Section 11 and read as follows:

"§ 11. Necessary and essential Youth Services Agency personnel are hereby transferred to the City agencies assuming the service functions enumerated in Section 10. Such transfers shall be consistent with civil service requirements and be based upon the needs of those agencies to operate those services."

§ 8. This Order shall take effect immediately if not taken by July 1, 1978, or by its adoption if earlier. ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.

§ 5. Surrendering City-Owned Property to Board of Estimate Jurisdiction

Each agency is to submit to the Board of Estimate prompt notification of all surrenders of improved or unimproved properties as soon as such properties are no longer required for agency functions.

§ 6. Releasing Space to the Department of Real Estate

Each agency is to submit to the Commissioner of Real Estate prompt notification of all releases of City-owned or leased space as soon as such space is no longer required for agency functions.

§ 7. Regular Reporting of Scheduled Vacancies

Each agency is to submit to the Commissioner of Real Estate a listing of City-owned or leased properties which are scheduled to be vacated in the following twenty-one (21) month period. The reports are to be submitted not later than April 1 and October 1 of each year. The first report is to be submitted not later than April 1, 1976 for the twenty-one (21) month period April 1, 1976 to December 31, 1977.

§ 8. Regular Reporting of Proposed Retention of Space not now in use or Underutilized

Each agency is to submit to the Commissioner of Real Estate reports on City-owned or leased properties assigned to the agency which are not now in use, or which are underutilized, but which the agency wishes to retain for future use. Substantial justification for neither surrendering nor releasing these properties must be included in the reports. The reports are to be submitted not later than April 1 and October 1 of each year. The first reports are to be submitted not later than April 1, 1976.

§ 9. Submission of Space Requests by Mayoral Agencies

Executive Order No. 19, dated July 29, 1974 and entitled "Submission of Space Requests by Mayoral Agencies" is hereby repealed.

§ 10. Effective Date

This Executive Order shall take effect immediately.

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.

title: ESTABLISHMENT OF PROCEDURES FOR CENTRALIZED DIRECTION OF TITLE X ACTIVITIES
full_text:
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 51

FEBRUARY 4, 1976

ESTABLISHMENT OF PROCEDURES FOR CENTRALIZED DIRECTION
OF TITLE X ACTIVITIES.

Whereas, Federal funds are granted to various agencies under Title X of the Public Works and Economic Development Act of 1965, as amended, for the purposes of relieving unemployment by providing job opportunities; and

Whereas, It is necessary that the City be enabled to alleviate losses of vital public services, and properly utilize available funds to meet City needs; and

Whereas, These objectives can best be implemented by providing for centralized direction of Title X activities and direct reporting to the Office of the Mayor,

Now, therefore, under the powers vested in me by law, it is hereby ordered that;

Section 1. Title X Coordinator.

All Title X activities shall be coordinated by the Commissioner of the Department of Employment of the Human Resources Administration who shall report directly to the First Deputy Mayor.

§ 2. Title X Committee.

There is hereby established a Title X Committee which shall be composed of a representative of the First Deputy Mayor, and representatives of the Office of Management and Budget, the Department of Employment of the Human Resources Administration, the Department of Personnel, the Law Department and the Office of Labor Relations.

§ 3. Functions and Duties of the Title X Coordinator.

a. The Title X Coordinator, in consultation with the Title X Committee, shall be responsible for overall supervision and review of Title X programs. The duties of the Title X Coordinator shall include, but not be limited to:

1. Monitoring and evaluation of the operation of Title X programs conducted in the various agencies.

2. Centralized reporting of Title X program activities.

b. The Title X Coordinator, in consultation with the Title X Committee, shall report on Title X operations in all agencies to the First Deputy Mayor.

§ 4. Additional Functions and Duties of the Members of the Title X Committee.

The agencies represented on the Title X Committee shall be responsible for those aspects of Title X operations as relate to the jurisdiction of their respective agencies. The Committee shall meet at the request of the Title X Coordinator or of any of the member agencies.

§ 5. Employment Under Title X Programs.

a. Department of Employment

1. The Department of Employment shall be responsible for ensuring eligibility under federal requirements of all Title X participants.

2. The Department of Employment shall be responsible for all recruitment under Title X from among the unemployed except where laid off City employees are being employed.

b. Department of Personnel

1. The Department of Personnel shall be responsible for ensuring eligibility under Civil Service requirements.

2. The Department of Personnel shall be responsible for directing the recall of laid off City employees by the various agencies.

§ 6. Agency Title X Operations.

a. All agencies shall comply with directives relating to the operation of Title X programs which are issued by the Title X Coordinator or by Title X Committee member agencies. This shall include, but not be limited to, providing such information and data concerning Title X operations as may be requested by the Title X Coordinator.

§ 7. Title X Grant Applications and Subcontracts.

a. Grant Applications.

No grant applications shall be made by any agency for Title X funding until the following procedures have been complied with:

1. Submission to the Title X Committee of the federal funding proposal.

2. Review of such proposal by the Title X Committee and the Title X Coordinator.

3. Submission to the First Deputy Mayor by the Title X Coordinator of the recommendations of the Title X Coordinator, the Title X Committee and the particular agency concerning the federal funding proposal.

4. Approval by the First Deputy Mayor of such proposal.

b. Subcontracts.

Prior to entering into subcontracts with federal funds provided under Title X, agencies shall obtain the approval of the Title X Coordinator in consultation with the Title X Committee.

§ 8. Other Public Agencies.

The Title X Coordinator, in consultation with the Title X Committee, shall coordinate City X activities with those of the other public agencies which operate Title X programs in The City of New York.

§ 9. Effective Date.

This order shall take effect immediately.

f19-25

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.

title: DIRECTOR OF CIVIL PREPAREDNESS
full_text:
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 53
MARCH 5, 1976
DIRECTOR OF CIVIL PREPAREDNESS

Whereas, It is a matter of necessity that The City of New York be prepared in the event of a natural or man-made disaster, to deal with any emergencies that may arise; and

Whereas, The functions of the Office of Civil Defense were transferred to the Police Department by Executive Order No. 38, dated August 29, 1975, and the Police Commissioner was appointed interim coordinator of the functions of Emergency Services—Civil Preparedness by that Order; and

Whereas, In order to achieve better coordination of these functions, it is necessary and

desirable for the Police Commissioner to direct the Civil Defense activities of The City of New York.

Now, therefore, by the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. The Police Commissioner is hereby appointed as the Director of Civil Preparedness.

§ 2. The Police Commissioner, as the Director of Civil Preparedness, shall be responsible to the Mayor and shall serve as the local Director of Civil Defense, with the powers of a local Director of Civil Defense under the Laws of 1951, Chapter 784, as amended.

§ 3. The Office of Emergency Services—Civil Preparedness, as referred to in Executive Order No. 38, dated August 29, 1975, is hereby re-designated as the Office of Civil Preparedness and the functions of the Office of Emergency Services—Civil Preparedness, as set forth in Executive Order No. 38, are hereby transferred to the Office of Civil Preparedness.

§ 4. This Order shall take effect immediately.

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.

title: UTILIZATION OF REAL PROPERTY
full_text:
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 54

MARCH 16, 1976

UTILIZATION OF REAL PROPERTY

Whereas, It is the policy of The City of New York to utilize its resources in the most effective and efficient manner in providing its required services; and

Whereas, Continuing pressures on the City budget require that all avenues of improving the utilization of its resources be examined; and

Whereas, The surrender by agencies of surplus City-owned vacant land, public structures, and/or the release of unoccupied or under utilized space within such structures aids our economy efforts by permitting the sale and return to the tax rolls or reassignment of such space to other agencies now housed in rental space; and

Whereas, The release by agencies of unoccupied or underutilized space in leased properties aids our economy efforts by permitting the renegotiation of existing leases or reassignment of such space to other agencies requiring additional space or moving from higher cost rental space; and

Whereas, The revised Charter of The City of New York assigns to the Municipal Service Administration extensive powers and duties in the acquisition, selling, leasing and managing of utilization of space; and

Whereas, As a result of an analysis of the present information system and reporting procedures for the utilization of space made by the Office of Management and Budget, such agency recommends that certain management practices be established.

Now, therefore, by the authority vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1: Role of the Commissioner of Real Estate

The Commissioner of Real Estate is hereby designated as the space manager for The City of New York with the authority and responsibility to carry out all functions with respect to the assignment of space.

All requests for space are to be submitted to the Commissioner. After the determination of the availability of agency funds for agency requests for space by the Office Management and Budget, the Commissioner is hereby empowered to be the final decision maker on all assignments of space, including the determination of the actual amount and location of space. These requests for space may include requests for new space, requests for renewal of existing space and requests for rearrangement of space whether made by the agency or recommended by the Bureau of Space Management of the Department of Real Estate. The Commissioner's decisions are final and binding.

§ 2. Bureau of Space Management

The Department of Real Estate is to expand its Bureau of Space Management. The functions of the unit are:

(a) To develop and undertake comprehensive and continuing programs to manage utilization of space owned or leased by the City.

(b) To establish space allocation standards.

(c) To conduct surveys of space utilization.

(d) To ensure full and proper utilization of all space owned or leased by the City.

(e) To ensure that space is properly designed to meet the functional requirements of the requesting agency at a reasonable cost considering both space allocation and improvement.

(f) To analyze and recommend to the Commissioner of Real Estate appropriate disposition of all agency requests for space.

(g) To establish and maintain current records of the utilization of all space owned or leased by the City.

(h) To supervise and approve all alterations of space leased by the City.

(i) To provide guidance to the agencies in accomplishing the objectives of this Executive Order.

§ 3. Agency Space Utilization Control and Information System

Each agency is to establish and maintain a space utilization control and information system. The objectives of the system are:

(a) To provide current basic data on agency space utilization.

(b) To ensure that space is being used for the intended purpose and in conformity with the space allocation standards established by the Department of Real Estate.

(c) To review agency requests for additional space or changes in present space arrangements.

Further, each agency is to designate a Space Management Coordinator to cooperate with the Commissioner of Real Estate in implementing space management programs. In order to provide rapid and smooth communication and progress, each agency is to authorize its Coordinator to respond fully and promptly, without further agency approvals, to all requests for data on space utilization from the Commissioner of Real Estate.

§ 4. Analysis of Present Usage of Space

Each agency is to conduct an analysis of its present usage of City-owned and leased space, with a view towards consolidation or rearrangement to achieve optimum space utilization under current conditions.

(a) Specific criteria, as established by the First Deputy Mayor, are to be applied in the evaluation of agency space utilization.

(b) Properties may be classified only as: Fully utilized and necessary for agency functions; scheduled to be vacated; or underutilized but deemed necessary for future agency functions.

(c) Any unneeded City-owned vacant buildings or land identified by this analysis are to be surrendered to the Board of Estimate. Any unneeded space within occupied City-owned buildings identified by this analysis is to be released to the Department of Real Estate. Properties thus surrendered will be sold or made available to other City agencies by the Department of Real Estate. Space thus released will be made available to other City agencies by the Department of Real Estate.

(d) Any unneeded leased space identified by this analysis is to be released to the Department of Real Estate. Space thus released will be made available to other City agencies or the lease renegotiated by the Department of Real Estate.

(e) The results of this analysis are to be reported through the reports specified in Sections 7 and 8 of this Executive Order.

title: DELEGATION OF POWERS OF THE FINANCE BOARD
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 55

MARCH 29, 1976

DELEGATION OF POWERS OF THE FINANCE BOARD

WHEREAS, the Mayor of the City of New York, pursuant to
Section 8, subdivision c, of the City Charter, possesses the
powers of the Finance Board of the City; and

WHEREAS, the Local Finance Law, by various of its provisions, authorizes the Finance Board to delegate certain of its powers to the Comptroller of the City of New York.

NOW, THEREFORE, pursuant to the powers vested in me by the
City Charter and the Local Finance Law, it is hereby resolved
and ordered as follows:

Section 1. A. The Comptroller is hereby delegated the
following powers of the Finance Board:

1. Pursuant to Section 30.00 of the Local Finance Law, the power to authorize the issuance of bond anticipation notes, tax anticipation notes, revenue anticipation notes or urban renewal notes of the City or the renewals thereof,

2. Pursuant to Section 50.00 of the Local Finance Law, the power to prescribe the terms, form and contents of every or any type of bond or note of the City; and

3. Pursuant to Section 56.00 of the Local Finance Law, all powers and duties which are vested in the Finance Board pursuant to Sections 57.00, 58.00, 59.00, 60.00, 62.00 and 63.00 of the Local Finance Law, and any other powers and duties which the Finance Board may have pertaining or incidental to the sale and issuance of obligations of the City.

B. The powers hereby delegated shall be subject to any limitations imposed by any applicable law, including the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, and such powers shall be exercised in accordance with Section 2 hereof.

g 2. A. The following definitions shall apply herein:

1. "Obligations" means bonds and notes of the City.

2. "Long-Term Obligations" means serial bonds and sinking fund bonds or corporate stock certificates of the City issued in definitive form.

3. "Interim Long-Term Obligations" means bonds of the City issued pursuant to Section 62.00 of the Local Finance Law, pending the printing or engraving and delivery of corresponding Long-Term Obligations.

B. Obligations shall be executed in the following manner:

1. The seal of the City shall be impressed upon or the facsimile seal of the City imprinted upon each Obligation, and each Obligation shall be attested by the City Clerk or by the person duly authorized to act in his stead in accordance with Section 32, subdivision b, of the City Charter.

2. Each Long-Term and each Interim Long-Term Obligation shall be executed in the name of the City by the Mayor and the Comptroller with their respective manual or facsimile signatures; each Obligation other than a Long-Term or Interim Long-Term Obligation shall be executed by the Comptroller or by such Deputy Comptroller as is duly authorized by the Comptroller to execute such Obligation with his manual or facsimile signature.

C. Obligations shall be issued in the following denominations:

1. Obligations other than Long-Term and Interim Long-Term Obligations shall be issued in denominations to be determined by the Comptroller.

2. Long-Term Obligations issued in coupon form shall be issued in the denomination of one thousand ($1,000) or five thousand ($5,000) dollars; Long-Term Obligations issued in registered form shall be issued in any denomination which is an integral multiple of one thousand ($1,000) dollars.

3. One Interim Long-Term Obligation may correspond to several corresponding Long-Term Obligations and in such case, the denomination of such Interim Long-Term Obligation shall not be in excess of the aggregate denominations of such corresponding Long-Term Obligations.

§ 3. The delegation by Robert F. Wagner, the then Mayor, exercising the powers of a Finance Board, to the Comptroller, dated November 21, 1963, is hereby revoked, provided, however, that nothing in this Executive Order shall be construed to affect the validity of any act performed pursuant to such delegation prior to the date hereof.

§ 4. This Executive Order shall take effect immediately and remain in effect until revoked by a subsequent Executive Order.

ABRAHAM D. BEAME
MAYOR

title: CONTROL OF OVERTIME AND PART-TIME HOURS
full_text:
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 56

APRIL 2, 1976

CONTROL OF OVERTIME AND PART-TIME HOURS

Whereas, The City of New York is currently in a fiscal crisis which mandates economies in every area of governmental operations and expenditures; and

Whereas, The payment of overtime to employees is an expenditure which must be curtailed in order to achieve necessary economies; and

Whereas, Situations could arise in which inordinate amounts of overtime paid to employees in their final year of service totally disproportionate to that received in prior years, would result in severely inflated costs to The City of New York; and

Whereas, Part-time employees who are eligible to receive pension benefits upon retirement from service could, by working an inordinate number of hours immediately prior to retirement, seriously inflate costs for The City of New York; and

Whereas, It is necessary and desirable to control any abuses which might arise in these areas.

Now, therefore, by the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. Each agency head shall be directly responsible for assuring that the allocation of overtime is controlled in such a manner as to achieve the most economy and eliminate the possibility of abuse.

§ 2. Authorization to work overtime compensable in cash shall be evenly distributed, where practicable, within each agency or agency subdivision, among all those employees who are eligible to perform the overtime work required. No authorization shall be granted to an employee to work overtime compensable in cash in excess of 5 percent of the base salary received by the employee during the preceding 12 month period unless such authorization is signed by the agency head or deputy to whom the agency head has granted authorization power.

§ 3. Monthly reports shall be filed by each agency head with the Office of Management and Budget, detailing the distribution of authorized overtime each month by individual employee name, social security number, title, date of birth, length of service, current base salary and amount of overtime compensation received during the preceding 12 calendar

months grouped by bureau, institution or program within the agency. Such reports shall also set forth any and all special circumstances which made it necessary to authorize cash overtime during the month to any employee in excess of the 5 percent limitation imposed by this Order. Requests for approval of Certificates of the Mayor submitted to the Office of Management and Budget, covering the payment of overtime will not be approved unless all the overtime for which payment is requested has been previously reported in these monthly reports. All such reports shall be received by the Office of Management and Budget no later than the 15th day of each succeeding month.

§ 4. Each employee who is working for The City of New York in more than one position in the same or different agencies must reapply for a Certification of Compatability of Dual Employment in accordance with Personnel Policy and Procedure Bulletin No. 6-70 of March 13, 1970, within 60 days of the date of this Order.

§ 5. A part-time employee shall not receive compensation from The City of New York in excess of 1,000 hours during any 12 month period unless authorized in writing by the head of an agency by which he or she is employed.

§ 6. Each agency head shall file monthly reports with the Office of Management and Budget, detailing the number of hours worked by each part-time employee of the agency and the rate of hourly compensation received by such employee; a cumulative total of the hours and rates received by each part-time employee for the preceding 12 month period; and an indication of what other City agencies, if any, employ each part-time employee. This report shall also set forth any and all special circumstances which made it necessary to authorize any part-time employee to work in excess of the 1,000 hour limitation imposed by this Order. These reports shall be received by the Office of Management and Budget no later than the 15th day of each succeeding month.

§ 7. Each agency shall maintain its records regarding overtime and part-time hours and compensation in good order and shall be subject to periodic audits by the Office of Management and Budget.

§ 8. This Order shall take effect immediately.

a16-22

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 57

APRIL 12, 1976

AMENDMENT OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 62
DATED FEBRUARY 5, 1968
AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 56
DATED FEBRUARY 1, 1972

Whereas, The Urban Design Council created by Executive Order No. 62, dated February 5, 1968, as amended by Executive Order No. 56, dated February 1, 1972, has recommended certain changes in the composition of the Council; and

Whereas, It is necessary and desirable to amend said Executive Order.

Now, therefore, by the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. Sections 3 and 5 of Executive Order No. 62, dated February 5, 1968, as amended by Executive Order No. 56, dated February 1, 1972, are hereby amended to read as follows:

"§ 3. *Composition.* The Urban Design Council shall consist of not less than ten nor more than twenty individuals. They shall be appointed by the Mayor, with due consideration for their understanding of the problems of urban design and their capacity for giving clear, effective advice. They shall serve at the pleasure of the Mayor and without compensation."

§ 5. *Procedure.* All actions of the Urban Design Council shall be by a majority of those present, with a quorum of six required. In other respects, the Council shall establish its own rules of procedure, provided it shall meet at least once a month, considering July and August a single month."

§ 2. This Order shall take effect immediately.

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.

title: OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH PLANNING TASK FORCE
full_text:
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 58

MAY 6, 1976

OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH PLANNING TASK FORCE

Whereas, The City of New York, as an employer, is concerned with providing a safe and healthful working environment for its employees and with preventing personal injuries to its employees; and

Whereas, Federal legislation involves the City in various occupational safety and health requirements; and

Whereas, A City-wide effort is required to assure consistency in rules, regulations and contracts and compliance with federal, state and local laws; and

Whereas, The New York State Industrial Commissioner has been directed by the Legislature to determine the types of coverages and the specific occupational safety and health requirements needed for public employees and to develop and recommend a specific plan; and

Whereas, A central management team is necessary to efficiently and adequately work with the State Department of Labor.

Now, therefore, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. An Occupational Safety and Health Planning Task Force is hereby created consisting of the Director of Construction who shall serve as Chairman, the Commissioner of Health, the Director of Management and Budget, the Director of the Department of Personnel, the Corporation Counsel and the Director of the Office of Labor Relations, each of whom may, in writing, designate a representative to serve on the task force in his stead.

§ 2. The duties of the task force shall be:

(a) to act as the City's liaison with the State Department of Labor in safety and health matters, with particular reference to chapter seven hundred fifty-six of the laws of nineteen hundred seventy-five or any subsequent bills or laws on the subject of public employee occupational safety and health;

(b) to conduct and supervise a survey of current safety and health rules, regulations, conditions and needs of the City's employees and

(c) to submit recommendations to the Mayor for changes, improved procedures, regulations and legislation in the area of public employee safety and health.

§ 3. All agencies shall extend their full cooperation to the task force to the extent that required personnel shall be reassigned by such agencies temporarily to assist the task force in performing its duties. Each agency also shall designate a staff member at policy level to serve as liaison with the task force and to cooperate in expeditiously furnishing such information, data, reports, surveys, studies, etc., and such personnel and resources as may be requested by the Chairman.

§ 4. All agencies shall cooperate and comply fully with the directives issued by the Occupational Safety and Health Planning Task Force.

§ 5. This Order shall take effect immediately.

m28-j4

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.

Whereas, A central management team is necessary to efficiently and adequately work with the State Department of Labor.

Now, therefore, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. An Occupational Safety and Health Planning Task Force is hereby created consisting of the Director of Construction who shall serve as Chairman, the Commissioner of Health, the Director of Management and Budget, the Director of the Department of Personnel, the Corporation Counsel and the Director of the Office of Labor Relations, each of whom may, in writing, designate a representative to serve on the task force in his stead.

§ 2. The duties of the task force shall be:

(a) to act as the City's liaison with the State Department of Labor in safety and health matters, with particular reference to chapter seven hundred fifty-six of the laws of nineteen hundred seventy-five or any subsequent bills or laws on the subject of public employee occupational safety and health;

(b) to conduct and supervise a survey of current safety and health rules, regulations, conditions and needs of the City's employees and

(c) to submit recommendations to the Mayor for changes, improved procedures, regulations and legislation in the area of public employee safety and health.

§ 3. All agencies shall extend their full cooperation to the task force to the extent that required personnel shall be reassigned by such agencies temporarily to assist the task force in performing its duties. Each agency also shall designate a staff member at policy level to serve as liaison with the task force and to cooperate in expeditiously furnishing such information, data, reports, surveys, studies, etc., and such personnel and resources as may be requested by the Chairman.

§ 4. All agencies shall cooperate and comply fully with the directives issued by the Occupational Safety and Health Planning Task Force.

§ 5. This Order shall take effect immediately.

OFFICE OF THE MAYOR

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 59

MAY 7, 1976

ESTABLISHMENT OF PROCEDURES FOR
THE CENTRALIZED COORDINATION AND
DIRECTION OF THE MEDICAID PROGRAM

Whereas, New York City expenditures for Medical Assistance under the Medicaid program now total more than $1.9 billion annually, and the total level of expenditures has increased rapidly since the program was established; and

Whereas, It is necessary to reduce the City's expenditures for Medical Assistance substantially in order to comply with the New York City Financial Plan; and

Whereas, To reduce expenditures while continuing effective service to the needy requires coordination of the efforts of the Human Resources Administration, the Department of Social Services, the Department of Health, the Department of Mental Health and Mental Retardation Services, the Office of Management and Budget and the Office of the Comptroller, as well as extensive cooperation between City, State and Federal Governments; and

Whereas, It is necessary to modernize and consolidate the City's administration of the Medicaid program to provide appropriate services consistent with control of expenditures, and to respond to changing managerial and legal requirements; and

Whereas, Changes in the Medicaid program affect a broad range of City services and coordination is required to permit full assessment of the impact of any action; and

Whereas, These objectives are best implemented by providing for centralized co-ordination and direction of the City's Medicaid program and direct reporting to the Office of the Mayor.

Now, therefore, under the powers vested in me by law, it is hereby ordered that:

Section 1. Medicaid Coordinator

All Medicaid activities shall be coordinated by a Medicaid Coordinator who shall be the Human Resources Administrator/Commissioner of Social Services.

§ 2. Medicaid Task Force

There is hereby established a Medicaid Task Force which shall have as its Chairman the Medicaid Coordinator and which shall have as its Vice-Chairman the Commissioner of health or their respective designees, and which shall also include a representative of the First Deputy Mayor, the Office of the Comptroller, the Office of Management and Budget, the Department of Mental Health and Mental Retardation Services and the Health and Hospitals Corporation.

§ 3. Functions and Duties of the Medicaid Coordinator and the Medicaid Task Force

The Medicaid Coordinator shall be responsible for overall supervision and review of the Medicaid program. The duties of the Medicaid Coordinator, in consultation with the Vice-Chairman of the Medicaid Task Force and with the Medicaid Task Force, shall include, but not be limited to:

a. Monitoring and projecting all Medicaid expenditures.

b. Monitoring and evaluation of all activities involved in Medicaid administration.

c. Review of all proposals for change in the Medicaid program and the development of specific recommendations for the revision of operating procedures.

d. Development of proposals and implementation plans for changes in the organization or the benefits or benefit structure of the Medicaid program to improve services or administration or to reduce costs.

e. Direction and coordination of all efforts to meet the requirements of the New York City Financial Plan as that relates to Medicaid expenditures.

f. Coordination of all Medicaid activities which involve the State or Federal governments, including, but not limited to, contract negotiations, requests for administrative approval of proposed actions and recommendations with respect to legislation.

g. Centralized reporting on the Medicaid program to the Office of the Mayor.

§ 4. Additional Functions and Duties of the Members of the Medicaid Task Force

The agencies represented on the Medicaid Task Force shall be responsible for those aspects of Medicaid operations which relate to the jurisdiction of their respective agencies. The Medicaid Coordinator shall be responsible for dissemination of information to members of the Medicaid Task Force. The Medicaid Task Force shall meet at the request of the Medicaid Coordinator or the Vice-Chairman of the Medicaid Task Force.

§ 5. Executive Director of the Medicaid Task Force

There is hereby established the position of Executive Director of the Medicaid Task Force who shall be appointed by and responsible to the Medicaid Coordinator. The Executive Director of the Medicaid Task Force shall be responsible for preparing such information, data, analyses, recommendations or other materials as are required by the Medicaid Coordinator.

§ 6. Medicaid Operations

All agencies shall cooperate with the Medicaid Coordinator and the Medicaid Task Force, and shall provide such information and data concerning Medicaid operations as may be requested by the Medicaid Coordinator, the Medicaid Task Force or the Executive Director of the Medicaid Task Force. No actions shall be taken by any agency which significantly affect the operations of the Medicaid program, until these actions have been reviewed and approved by the Medicaid Coordinator who shall consult with the Medicaid Task Force. All agencies shall comply with directives of the Medicaid Coordinator with respect to actions required to comply with the New York City Financial Plan as applicable to the Medicaid program.

§ 7. Effective Date

This order shall take effect immediately.

j10-16

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor

title: CONSERVATION OF ENERGY RESOURCES
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 60

May 28, 1976

CONSERVATION OF ENERGY RESOURCES

WHEREAS, the costs of energy resources, i. e., electricity, steam, natural gas and fuel oil, have risen manifold in the City of New York, thereby causing serious economic harm to the economy of City government; and

WHEREAS, there is a pressing need to reduce the costs of said energy resources required by the City of New York; and

WHEREAS, there is a need to reduce wasteful, uneconomical and unnecessary uses of energy, to reduce the rate of growth of energy consumption and to prudently conserve energy resources; and

WHEREAS, as a result of an analysis of the present information system and reporting procedures for electrical energy made by the Municipal Energy Conservation Program, the Municipal Service Administration recommends that certain management practices be established for all energy resources; and

WHEREAS, conservation of energy resources require

expanded authority and technical capability within City
government.

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor
of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. The Municipal Service Administrator is hereby charged with the authority and responsibility to develop, promote and implement in all Mayoral agencies of the City of New York policies, programs and procedures to conserve and to improve efficiency in the use of energy resources, i. e., electricity, steam, natural gas and fuel oil. The Administrator shall establish guidelines for such programs that will have an immediate and substantial effect in reducing the rate of growth of energy demand and in minimizing the adverse economic impact of increasing energy consumption.

2. Each agency is directed to cooperate, assist and implement fully all directives of the Municipal Service Administrator pursuant to this Order.

3. Each agency shall establish and maintain an energy resources control and data information center. The center shall be responsible for liaison with the Municipal Service Administrator as he requires, including:

a. a tabulation by month of the cost of, and the quantity of, the energy resource consumed for each facility under the jurisdiction of the agency for fiscal 1972-73 through fiscal 1976-77.

b. a list of planned facilities which will be in use or surrendered by the agency for fiscal 1976-77 and fiscal 1977-78, the location of such facilities, and the anticipated consumption of energy resources to be utilized in the proposed or surrendered facilities.

§ 4. Each agency shall, within twenty (20) days after the date of this Order, submit a plan to the Municipal Service Administrator specifying the energy conservation policies and practices which it will employ to decrease energy consumption by minimum goals of five (5) percent reduction in the consumption of electricity and twenty-five (25) percent reduction in the consumption of steam, natural gas and fuel oil in fiscal 1976-77 as compared to fiscal 1975-76.

§ 5. The Municipal Service Administrator shall, within forty (40) days after the date of this Order, review each agency's plans, shall determine the adequacy of the measures proposed by the agency and shall revise the plan, where necessary.

§ 6. The Municipal Service Administrator may prescribe such rules as may be necessary or appropriate to carry out his authority under this Order.

§ 7. The Municipal Service Administrator shall report periodically to the Mayor on the operation of the

program. Such report shall include an estimate of the
energy conservation achieved, the degree of agency participation
and achievement, and a description of innovative conservation
programs undertaken by individual agencies.

§ 8. The Municipal Service Administrator shall develop and implement a long term plan for energy conservation with respect to buildings owned or leased by the City and its agencies. Such plan shall include:

a. Mandatory thermal efficiency standards and insulation requirements,

b. Mandatory lighting efficiency standards,

c. Restrictions governing the hours and conditions of operation,

d. Thermostat controls,

e. Plans for replacing or altering equipment to meet such standards, and

f. Programs of education to promote energy conservation in public buildings and structures.

§ 9. For each succeeding fiscal year, each agency shall by November 1st submit a plan to the Municipal Service Administrator specifying the energy conservation policies and practices it will employ for the coming fiscal year. After reviewing and modifying the plan, where necessary, the Administrator shall, at the earliest practicable date, set an energy conservation goal for each agency for the coming fiscal year.

§ 10. Executive Order No. 29, dated April 16, 1975, and Executive Order No. 46, dated November 13, 1975, are hereby superseded.

§ 11. This Executive Order shall take effect immediately.

title: QUARTERLY ALLOCATION AND PERSONNEL CEILING CONTROL SYSTEMS
full_text:
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 61

JUNE 30, 1976
QUARTERLY ALLOCATION AND PERSONNEL CEILING CONTROL SYSTEMS

Whereas, The New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York requires that all liabilities, obligations and disbursements of the City and covered organizations be in accordance with the Financial Plan approved by the Emergency Financial Control Board; and

Whereas, The New York City Charter empowers and charges the Mayor with the responsibility of administering the Expense Budget for the Fiscal Year 1977 (the "Budget") ; and

Whereas, The Terms and Conditions of the Budget provide that the Mayor may establish for any agency a quarterly allotment plan which may set forth for the quarter of the fiscal year during which it is to remain in effect (1) rates of expenditure for personal services; (2) ceilings on the total number of personnel; and (3) the total amount of funds to be spent by the agency during such quarter; and

Whereas, The Mayor has determined that the establishment of quarterly allocations and personnel ceilings for each agency is necessary in order to ensure compliance with the Financial Plan and the Budget.

Now, therefore, pursuant to the power vested in me by the provisions of Section 123 of the New York City Charter and a resolution of the Emergency Financial Control Board dated June 4, 1976, concerning reporting and control of covered organization revenues and expenses, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. Limitation on Agency Expenditures. The Budget appropriations of all agencies shall be expended in accordance with the quarterly allocations and personnel ceilings established pursuant to Section 2 of this Executive Order. The term "agency" as used in this Executive Order means any office, administration, department, division, board, bureau, commission, corporation, institution or other unit of government, including without limitation "covered organizations" as defined in the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, the expenses of which are paid in whole or in part from the City Treasury.

§ 2. Establishment of Quarterly Allocations and Personnel Ceilings.

Prior to the beginning of each quarter, or as otherwise required, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (sometimes hereinafter "OMB") shall:

a. Issue to each agency a Quarterly Allocation and Personnel Ceiling Statement for such quarter. Each such statement shall set forth for such quarter (i) an allocation for expenditures, by expenditure category; (ii) a personnel ceiling, by personnel category; and (iii) such related material as the Director of Management and Budget shall deem prudent to include. Amendments during the quarter to any Quarterly Allocation and Personnel Ceiling Statement may be issued by the Director of Management and Budget. As used herein, "quarter" shall mean the three-month period beginning on July 1, 1976, October 1, 1976, January 1, 1977 or April 1, 1977.

b. Simultaneously with issuance of the Quarterly Allocation and Personnel Ceiling Statement to each agency, OMB shall submit each such statement to the Office of the Comptroller. The Director of Management and Budget shall request the Office of the Comptroller to discontinue processing an agency's vouchers if the allocations or any category of such allocations set forth in any agency's Quarterly Allocation and Personnel Ceiling Statement shall be exceeded.

The Quarterly Allocations and Personnel Ceilings shall be based on a Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Plan, or the most recent Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Forecast for each agency.

§ 3. Establishment of a Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Plan

a. Each agency shall submit a proposed Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Plan to OMB.

b. Each agency shall submit a detailed estimate of payroll expenditure and the number of personnel on the payroll for each month of the Fiscal Year 1977 in such form and with such information as the Director of Management and Budget shall require. This information shall be consistent with the agency's proposed Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Plan.

c. The information in the proposed Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Plan will be reviewed by OMB. After review, OMB will issue an approved Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Plan to each agency.

§ 4. Establishment of the Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Forecasts

Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Forecasts shall be prepared as actual data are received concerning expenditures and personnel and in accordance with such other information as may become available. The Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Forecasts shall be adjusted in the third month of each quarter and may be adjusted during the quarter by the Director of Management and Budget to reflect the most current information consistent with the City's Financial Plan. The Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Forecasts will be based on actual experience and will reflect corrective action to assure continued performance to the City's Financial Plan.

§ 5. Monthly Reports to the Office of Management and Budget

After the end of each month, OMB will collect and analyze each agency's actual expenditure and personnel information for the month. This data will be obtained by the 15th of each month from:

a. A Monthly Expenditure Report issued by the Office of the Comptroller, which provides each agency's actual expenditure data.

b. A monthly Payroll Report, issued by the Office of the Comptroller, which provides actual payroll and personnel data for most agencies.

c. A Monthly Payroll and Personnel Calculation Report, which shall be prepared by each agency. This report will provide a detailed statement of actual payroll expenditures and personnel levels, along with revised estimates for future months. It will be the only source of payroll information for those agencies which process their own payroll.

Whereas, The New York City Charter empowers and charges the Mayor with the responsibility of administering the Expense Budget for the Fiscal Year 1977 (the "Budget") ; and

Whereas, The Terms and Conditions of the Budget provide that the Mayor may establish for any agency a quarterly allotment plan which may set forth for the quarter of the fiscal year during which it is to remain in effect (1) rates of expenditure for personal services; (2) ceilings on the total number of personnel; and (3) the total amount of funds to be spent by the agency during such quarter; and

Whereas, The Mayor has determined that the establishment of quarterly allocations and personnel ceilings for each agency is necessary in order to ensure compliance with the Financial Plan and the Budget.

Now, therefore, pursuant to the power vested in me by the provisions of Section 123 of the New York City Charter and a resolution of the Emergency Financial Control Board dated June 4, 1976, concerning reporting and control of covered organization revenues and expenses, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. Limitation on Agency Expenditures. The Budget appropriations of all agencies shall be expended in accordance with the quarterly allocations and personnel ceilings established pursuant to Section 2 of this Executive Order. The term "agency" as used in this Executive Order means any office, administration, department, division, board, bureau, commission, corporation, institution or other unit of government, including without limitation "covered organizations" as defined in the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, the expenses of which are paid in whole or in part from the City Treasury.

§ 2. Establishment of Quarterly Allocations and Personnel Ceilings.

Prior to the beginning of each quarter, or as otherwise required, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (sometimes hereinafter "OMB") shall:

a. Issue to each agency a Quarterly Allocation and Personnel Ceiling Statement for such quarter. Each such statement shall set forth for such quarter (i) an allocation for expenditures, by expenditure category; (ii) a personnel ceiling, by personnel category; and (iii) such related material as the Director of Management and Budget shall deem prudent to include. Amendments during the quarter to any Quarterly Allocation and Personnel Ceiling Statement may be issued by the Director of Management and Budget. As used herein, "quarter" shall mean the three-month period beginning on July 1, 1976, October 1, 1976, January 1, 1977 or April 1, 1977.

b. Simultaneously with issuance of the Quarterly Allocation and Personnel Ceiling Statement to each agency, OMB shall submit each such statement to the Office of the Comptroller. The Director of Management and Budget shall request the Office of the Comptroller to discontinue processing an agency's vouchers if the allocations or any category of such allocations set forth in any agency's Quarterly Allocation and Personnel Ceiling Statement shall be exceeded.

The Quarterly Allocations and Personnel Ceilings shall be based on a Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Plan, or the most recent Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Forecast for each agency.

§ 3. Establishment of a Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Plan

a. Each agency shall submit a proposed Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Plan to OMB.

b. Each agency shall submit a detailed estimate of payroll expenditure and the number of personnel on the payroll for each month of the Fiscal Year 1977 in such form and with such information as the Director of Management and Budget shall require. This information shall be consistent with the agency's proposed Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Plan.

c. The information in the proposed Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Plan will be reviewed by OMB. After review, OMB will issue an approved Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Plan to each agency.

§ 4. Establishment of the Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Forecasts

Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Forecasts shall be prepared as actual data are received concerning expenditures and personnel and in accordance with such other information as may become available. The Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Forecasts shall be adjusted in the third month of each quarter and may be adjusted during the quarter by the Director of Management and Budget to reflect the most current information consistent with the City's Financial Plan. The Monthly Expenditure and Personnel Forecasts will be based on actual experience and will reflect corrective action to assure continued performance to the City's Financial Plan.

§ 5. Monthly Reports to the Office of Management and Budget

After the end of each month, OMB will collect and analyze each agency's actual expenditure and personnel information for the month. This data will be obtained by the 15th of each month from:

a. A Monthly Expenditure Report issued by the Office of the Comptroller, which provides each agency's actual expenditure data.

b. A monthly Payroll Report, issued by the Office of the Comptroller, which provides actual payroll and personnel data for most agencies.

c. A Monthly Payroll and Personnel Calculation Report, which shall be prepared by each agency. This report will provide a detailed statement of actual payroll expenditures and personnel levels, along with revised estimates for future months. It will be the only source of payroll information for those agencies which process their own payroll.

title: ESTABLISHMENT OF THE OFFICE OF DEVELOPMENT
full_text:
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 63

JULY 26, 1976

ESTABLISHMENT OF THE OFFICE OF DEVELOPMENT

Whereas, During the last nine years, five (5) of the special mayoral development offices in the Executive Office of the Mayor have had broad common objectives to plan, expedite and implement public, private and joint public and private redevelopment of specified areas of the City. These offices are:

The Office of Midtown Planning and Development
The Office of Lower Manhattan Development
The Office of Jamaica Planning and Development
The Office of Downtown Brooklyn Development
The Upper Manhattan Planning and Development Office

and

Whereas, The concept of special development offices within the Executive Office of the Mayor has been successful in encouraging overall planning and implementation of numerous projects within the areas of their jurisdiction; and

Whereas, The five special development offices have worked toward implementing the plans for the specific areas through the various agencies within the City government, including:

The development of planning goals, zoning amendments and project review through the City Planning Commission.

The development of new and modified transportation and related facilities through the Transportation Administration and its associated departments.

The development of new and renovated housing through the Housing and Develop-ment Administration.

The development and expansion of commercial and industrial activities and facilities through the Economic Development Administration.

The improvement of the delivery of municipal services through the Office of Neighborhood Services.

The development and promotion of recreational and cultural facilities and pro-grams in conjunction with the Parks, Recreation and Cultural Affairs Administration; and

Whereas, Over these years certain common development procedures, techniques and expertise have evolved within the staff of the special development offices which are applicable to nearly all special development projects, including the use of special zoning districts to guide the growth and change of specific local commercial and commercial and residential areas; the designation, policy management and project management of specific urban renewal projects; sponsorship, designation and lease negotiations with public and private developers to implement specific development projects; the planning, preliminary design and implementation of major transit improvements, including subway stations and large scale transit malls; and

Whereas, The City's fiscal situation has made it vital that commercial, institutional and residential development be aided in every way possible to encourage the use of private initiative and private funds in a constructive partnership with government; and

Whereas, A single, unified Office of Development is the vehicle best suited to maximize

the development potential of key areas of the City and utilize the resources and skills of the aforementioned five offices.

Now, therefore, by virtue of the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. Office of Development

There is established in the Executive Office of the Mayor the Office of Development, which shall be headed by a Director who shall be appointed by and serve at the pleasure of the Mayor. The Office of Development shall supersede the five planning and development offices and shall coordinate planning, development and implementation strategies for the areas of five (5) previously existing development offices—

(a) Lower Manhattan

(b) Downtown Brooklyn

(c) Greater Jamaica

(d) Upper Manhattan

(e) Special projects in midtown Manhattan under the coordination of the Mayor's Midtown Action Office,

(f) and in such other areas as shall be assigned from time to time by the Deputy Mayor for Planning.

§ 2. Powers and Duties of the Director

The Director shall assume all the powers and responsibilities now vested in the directors of the Office of Lower Manhattan Development, Downtown Brooklyn Development, Jamaica Planning and Development and Upper Manhattan Planning and Development and, in addition, shall have the following powers and duties with respect to planning and development:

a. Under the supervision of the Deputy Mayor for Planning and in consultation with the Chairman of the City Planning Commission, the Administrators of the Housing and Development Administration, the Economic Development Administration and the Transportation Administration shall advise the Mayor with respect to economic and community development plans, activities and programs.

b. To work closely with the various private individuals, organizations and community groups concerned with the development of the specific areas designated to promote and raise support for such development and to create and assist quasi public and not-for-profit vehicles to further such development.

c. On behalf of the Mayor, to have full responsibility to direct and coordinate the activities of City agencies to make feasible and expedite economic and community development plans, activities and programs, including present and future redevelopment plans in the designated areas.

d. To work with and advise task forces, including those presently constituted, considering revisions to policies and programs relative to the City's economic and community development, and to direct and coordinate City agencies in implementing revised development policies as they apply to the areas designated.

e. To coordinate activities, actions and plans with public authorities, state and federal governments.

f. To study and make recommendations with respect to design controls and zoning for the areas designated.

g. To review and make recommendations with respect to capital budget and expense items and development and service programs as they affect the areas designated.

h. To serve as liaison between the Mayor and City agencies, and between the City and private developers and organizations with regard to activities in or affecting the areas designated.

i. To hire staff personnel, designate advisors and advising groups and retain consultants, apply for and receive grants, loans and other forms of support, let contracts and leases, prepare and submit legislation and resolutions subject to all applicable regulations and after approval of the Mayor in connection with the performance of the foregoing.

j. To assist the Office of Neighborhood Services in improving the delivery of municipal services in designated areas.

§ 3. City agencies responsible for providing public improvements and services in the special designated areas, including the Economic Development Administration, the Housing and Development Administration, the Municipal Services Administration, the Parks and Recreation Administration, Cultural Affairs Administration, the Health Services Administration, the Environmental Protection Administration, the Transportation Administration, the Human Resources Administration, the Office of Neighborhood Services, Department of Civic Affairs and Public Events, the Fire Department and the Police Department shall cooperate with the Director of the Office of Development in the performance of his functions and duties as set forth herein. Each such agency shall keep the Office of Development advised of their ongoing and planned activities in the designated areas and shall coordinate such activities with those of the Office of Development. Upon the request of the Director, each such agency shall designate a staff member at policy level to be its liaison with the Office of Development and to cooperate in furnishing information and such available staff resources and professional services to the extent it is feasible to do so, as may be requested by the Director for performance of his functions and duties as set forth herein.

§ 4. The Office of Lower Manhattan Development, the Office of Jamaica Planning and Development, the Office of Downtown Brooklyn Development and the Upper Manhattan Planning and Development Office are hereby abolished and succeeded by the Office of Development.

§ 5. This Executive Order shall take effect immediately.

a9-13

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.

title: ESTABLISHMENT OF THE MAYOR'S MIDTOWN ACTION OFFICE
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 64

JULY 26, 1976

ESTABLISHMENT OF THE MAYOR'S MIDTOWN ACTION OFFICE

Whereas, The Offices of Midtown Planning and Development, Apparel Industry Planning and Development and the Midtown Task Force have had broad common objectives to improve conditions in the vital Midtown area og the Borough of Manhattan; and

Whereas, The concept of special development offices within the executive office of the Mayor has been successful in encouraging overall planning and implementation of numerous improvement projects within the areas of their jurisdiction; and

Whereas, Over these years, certain common procedures, techniques and expertise have evolved within the staff of the Office of Apparel Industry Planning and Development, Midtown Planning and Development and the Midtown Task Force which are applicable to nearly all improvement projects in Midtown Manhattan; and

Whereas, The City's fiscal situation has made it urgent that commercial institutional and residential development be aided in every way possible to encourage the use of private initiative and private funds in a constructive partnership with government; and

Whereas, The Mayor has undertaken a multi-faceted improvement program in Midtown Manhattan involving physical improvements, municipal service delivery and law enforcement; and

Whereas, A single, unified Mayor's Midtown Action Office is best suited to coordinate the aforementioned improvement program for Midtown Manhattan.

Now, therefore, by virtue of the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. *Mayor's Midtown Action Office*

There is established in the Executive Office of the Mayor, the Mayor's Midtown Action Office which shall be headed by a Director who shall be appointed by and serve at the pleasure of the Mayor. The Mayor's Midtown Action Office shall supersede the Offices of Apparel Industry Planning and Development, Midtown Planning and Development and the Midtown Task Force, and shall coordinate municipal services and planning and physical development strategies in the area of Manhattan from 59th Street on the north to 14th Street on the south.

§ 2. *Powers and Duties of the Director*

The Director shall assume all the powers and responsibilities now vested in the directors of the Offices of Apparel Industry Planning and Development, Midtown Planning and Development and the Midtown Task Force and, in addition, shall have the following powers and duties:

a. on behalf of the Mayor, to have full responsibility to direct and coordinate the activities of City agencies to make feasible and expedite improved municipal service delivery and economic and community development plans, activities and programs in Midtown Manhattan;

b. in consultation with the Chairman of the City Planning Commission, the Administrators of the Housing and Development Administration and the Economic Development Administration shall advise the Mayor with respect to economic and community development plans, activities and programs as they affect Midtown Manhattan;

c. to work closely with the various private individuals, organizations and community groups concerned with the condition and development of Midtown Manhattan, to promote and raise support to improve such conditions and encourage such development and to create and assist quasi-public and not-for-profit vehicles to further the above;

d. to work with and advise task forces, including those presently constituted, considering revisions to policies and programs relative to the City's economic and community development as they affect Midtown Manhattan;

e. to coordinate its activities, actions and plans with public authorities, state and federal governments;

f. to study and make recommendations with respect to design controls and zoning for Midtown Manhattan;

g. to review and make recommendations with respect to capital budget and expense items and development and service programs as they affect Midtown Manhattan;

h. to serve as liaison between the Mayor and City agencies, and between the City and private developers and organizations with regard to activities in or affecting Midtown Manhattan;

i. to hire staff personnel, designate advisors and advising groups and retain consultants, apply for and receive grants, loans and other forms of support, let contracts and leases, prepare and submit legislation and resolutions subject to all applicable regulations in connection with the performance of the foregoing.

§ 3. City agencies responsible for providing public improvements and services in Midtown Manhattan, including the Economic Development Administration, the Housing and Development Administration, the Municipal Services Administration, the Parks and Recreation Administration, Cultural Affairs Administration, the Health Services Administration, the Environmental Protection Administration, the Transportation Administration, the Human Resources Administration, the Office of Neighborhood Services, Consumer Affairs Department, Department of Civic Affairs and Public Events, the Fire Department and the Police Department shall cooperate with the Director of the Office of Development in the performance of his functions and duties as set forth herein. Each such agency shall keep the Director advised of their ongoing and planned activities in the designated areas and shall coordinate such activities with those of the Mayor's Midtown Action Office.

Upon the request of the Director, each such agency shall designate a staff member at policy level to be its liaison with the Mayor's Midtown Action Office and to cooperate in furnishing information and such available staff resources and professional services to the extent feasible, as may be requested by the Director for performance of his functions and duties as set forth herein.

§ 4. The Office of Apparel Industry Planning and Development, the Office of Midtown Planning and Development and the Midtown Task Force are hereby abolished.

§ 5. This Order shall take effect immediately.

a9-13

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.

d. to work with and advise task forces, including those presently constituted, considering revisions to policies and programs relative to the City's economic and community development as they affect Midtown Manhattan;

e. to coordinate its activities, actions and plans with public authorities, state and federal governments;

f. to study and make recommendations with respect to design controls and zoning for Midtown Manhattan;

g. to review and make recommendations with respect to capital budget and expense items and development and service programs as they affect Midtown Manhattan;

h. to serve as liaison between the Mayor and City agencies, and between the City and private developers and organizations with regard to activities in or affecting Midtown Manhattan;

i. to hire staff personnel, designate advisors and advising groups and retain consultants, apply for and receive grants, loans and other forms of support, let contracts and leases, prepare and submit legislation and resolutions subject to all applicable regulations in connection with the performance of the foregoing.

§ 3. City agencies responsible for providing public improvements and services in Midtown Manhattan, including the Economic Development Administration, the Housing and Development Administration, the Municipal Services Administration, the Parks and Recreation Administration, Cultural Affairs Administration, the Health Services Administration, the Environmental Protection Administration, the Transportation Administration, the Human Resources Administration, the Office of Neighborhood Services, Consumer Affairs Department, Department of Civic Affairs and Public Events, the Fire Department and the Police Department shall cooperate with the Director of the Office of Development in the performance of his functions and duties as set forth herein. Each such agency shall keep the Director advised of their ongoing and planned activities in the designated areas and shall coordinate such activities with those of the Mayor's Midtown Action Office.

Upon the request of the Director, each such agency shall designate a staff member at policy level to be its liaison with the Mayor's Midtown Action Office and to cooperate in furnishing information and such available staff resources and professional services to the extent feasible, as may be requested by the Director for performance of his functions and duties as set forth herein.

§ 4. The Office of Apparel Industry Planning and Development, the Office of Midtown Planning and Development and the Midtown Task Force are hereby abolished.

§ 5. This Order shall take effect immediately.

a9-13

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.

title: INTERAGENCY COMMITTEE ON MINORITY BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 65

JULY 27, 1976

INTERAGENCY COMMITTEE ON MINORITY BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT

Whereas, There has been established within the Economic Development Administration of The City of New York an office of Minority Business Enterprise; and

Whereas, A major objective of that office is to involve City government in the stimulation and promotion of minority business development; and

Whereas, It is important that City agencies engaging in the procurement of goods and services for The City of New York coordinate their efforts to achieve greater participation by minority businesses.

Now, therefore, by the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. There is hereby established an Interagency Committee on Minority Business Development.

§ 2. The Committee shall consist of the Economic Development Administrator, Commissioner of Purchase or their duly designated representatives and policy level officials from each City agency regularly involved in the procurement of goods and services for The City of New York.

§ 3. The interagency Committee on Minority Business Development shall develop:

a. Systems and procedures to assure adequate responsiveness by The City of New York to the needs of minority businesses.

b. Better communication between The City of New York and minority business enterprises to make known the City's desire to receive bids on goods and services to be purchased on a competitive basis.

c. Methods to encourage increased participation by minority contractors and sub-contractors in the economic development of the City.

§ 4. This Order shall take effect immediately.

a9-13

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.
