Approval granted herein will be considered a directive for the agency to begin site approval (if required) and/or preliminary design.

(2) In the case of those projects requiring *ACQUISITION OF A SITE*, the site shall be selected in accordance with the provisions of Sections 227 and 197c of the Charter subsequent to preliminary scope approval, but prior to final scope approval by the Office of Management and Budget.

* See Exhibit "A"

(3) Upon completion of preliminary design for final scope approval, the agency shall submit preliminary plans, specifications and estimates of cost to the Office of Management and Budget for review, and written approval within 30 days of receipt. If the documentation is deemed acceptable, the Office of Management and Budget shall issue a certificate of approval for *FINAL SCOPE APPROVAL*, which will include approval of:

(a) Preliminary plans and specifications.

(b) Construction cost limitations including contingencies.

Approval granted herein shall be considered a directive for the agency to begin final design.

(4) Upon completion of final design, the agency shall submit final plans, specifications and estimate of cost to the Office of Management and Budget for review and approval. Within 30 calendar days after receipt, the Office of Management and Budget shall either approve or disapprove of the final plans in writing. If the final plans are deemed acceptable, the Office of Management and Budget shall issue a certificate of *FINAL DESIGN APPROVAL* which will include approval of:

(a) Final plans and specifications

(b) Modified construction cost limitation if required

(c) All interfund agreement implementation requirements for supervision of construction by agency or consultant contract and fee for supervision of construction if said work is to be performed by consultant.

Approval granted herein shall be considered authorization to advertise for bids and award contracts subject to provisions of Section 233 of the New York City Charter and in accordance with all other applicable executive orders, Certificate Standards (CS), and statutes provided that the amount of bids received plus 2 per cent does not exceed the issued cost limitation. Should the amount exceed the previously issued cost of limitation, a request for an increased cost limitation shall be submitted to the Office of Management and Budget for approval within 30 days.

For all approved projects, agencies must submit a monthly expenditure plan (warrant basis). The Office of Management and Budget will issue a certificate to the Comptroller reflecting this plan and authorizing the encumbrance of these funds.

B. CAPITAL PROJECT APPROVAL PROCEDURE (NON-CONSTRUCTION PROJECTS)

For those projects not requiring design or construction, the following procedures should be adhered to:

(1) After inclusion in the adopted Budget, the agency shall prepare a "scope" of work for submission to the Office of Management and Budget.

(2) The scope shall describe the nature of the work or items to be purchased—i.e., the reason for the expenditure—and the required amount.

(3) The Office of Management and Budget shall review the scope and within 60 calendar days either reject or approve thereof. If rejected, the Office of Management and Budget shall furnish the Commissioner with written explanation for said disapproval.

(4) If deemed acceptable, a certificate shall be issued approving of said scope and amount of expenditure.

C. CAPITAL CONSTRUCTION PROJECTS INVOLVING DEPARTMENTAL LABOR AND MATERIAL

(1) Prior to (or concurrent with) Capital Budget adoption, a certificate of approval from the Office of Management and Budget will be filed with the Comptroller and involved agencies incorporating a comprehensive Interfund Agreement for each agency which will delineate the maximum schedule of construction work to be carried out by said agency using "In-House" personnel. This schedule, while identifying the maximum universe of potential work including the materials therefor, will limit the total dollar value of said work to be earned by said agency to a pre-determined amount consistent with that budgeted for the agency for said fiscal year.

(2) Upon inclusion of subject projects in the adopted Capital Budget, the following approval steps shall be followed:

(a) A written definitive *Final Project Scope*, including drawings as necessary, shall be prepared in accordance with applicable approved standards and submitted to the Office of Management and Budget for approval.

The Office of Management and Budget shall, within 60 calendar days after receipt of the scope, either approve or disapprove thereof. If the scope is found acceptable, the Office of Management and Budget shall issue a certificate of approval for *FINAL SCOPE AND DESIGN APPROVAL* which will include approval of:

(1) Scope and design

(2) Construction Cost earnable by involved agency for said work.

(3) Activation of said work items under the terms and conditions of the previously approved Interfund Agreement.

Approval granted hereunder will be considered a directive for the agency to begin work subject to provisions of Section 233 of the New York City Charter.

Attached is a schematic flow chart highlighting key milestones and areas of agency responsibility.

This Executive Order shall take effect immediately and remain in effect until revoked by a subsequent Executive Order.

013-19

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.

EXHIBIT "A"—INTERFUND AGREEMENT

A comprehensive Interfund Agreement will be developed for each agency. This document will delineate the maximum schedule of work and services to be provided by said agency. While identifying the maximum universe of potential design and construction work an agency is authorized to pursue during the fiscal year the schedule will LIMIT THE TOTAL DOLLAR VALUE OF FEES TO BE EARNED BY SAID AGENCY IN THE DEFINED FISCAL YEAR TO a predetermined amount consistent with the amount of funds budgeted for the agency for said fiscal year. Each preliminary scope approval, (as well as final design approvals), will activate a particular work element and concomitant fee portion of said previously approved comprehensive Interfund Agreement. It is anticipated that sufficient preliminary scope and/or final design approvals will be issued in a fiscal year to activate (implement) sufficient fees to fully meet the annual amount budgeted for the agency in the prior certificate of approval for the comprehensive Interfund Agreement.

Prior to (or concurrent with) Capital Budget adoption, a certificate of approval from the Office of Management and Budget will be filed with the Comptroller and the relevant agencies incorporating the agreement. EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 96

DECEMBER 7, 1977

DESIGNATION OF THE EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICE AS THE
COORDINATING AGENCY FOR EMERGENCY MEDICAL CARE FOR
THE CITY OF NEW YORK

Whereas, The Emergency Medical Service of the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation was established to provide pre-hospital emergency services; and

Whereas, The Emergency Medical Service is the primary provider of pre-hospital emergency medical care in New York City, and is charged with providing safe, expeditious transportation to the medical facility best equipped to render appropriate care, without regard to any patient's ability to pay; and

Whereas, The Emergency Medical Service maintains a central Medical Emergency Communications and Control Center for the purposes of dispatching ambulances; and

Whereas, The New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation has received funds from the United States Department of Health, Education and Welfare to establish a coordinated emergency medical service system; and

Whereas, The maintenance of a coordinated, high quality emergency medical services system is essential to the preservation of the life and health of the residents of New York City.

Now, therefore, by the power vested in me as the Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. *Designation of Coordinating Agency*

The Emergency Medical Service of The New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation shall be the coordinating agency for The City of New York for all pre-hospital services in the event of medical emergencies.

§ 2. *Duties of the Emergency Medical Service*

The duties of the Emergency Medical Service shall include:

(a) the operation of ambulance services and funding of ambulances to be operated under contract;

(b) the operation of a central dispatching system which shall direct all responses to requests for emergency ambulance services and which shall incorporate all ambulances operated or funded by The City of New York or the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation, as well as such other voluntary and proprietary ambulances as shall choose to participate and be accepted for participation by the Emergency Medical Service;

(c) the establishment of programs for assuring the provision of high quality treatment, administered by qualified personnel, at the scene of a medical emergency;

(d) the establishment and direction of plans for the provision of transportation services and vital on-site care in the event of a medical disaster;

(e) such other and further duties and responsibilities necessary to the proper functioning of the Emergency Medical Service.

§ 3. *Duties of the Board of Health*

Nothing herein shall abridge the authorities and duties of the Board of Health in the event of great and imminent peril to the public health as specified in Chapter 22, Section 563 of the New York City Charter.

§ 4. *Effective Date*

This Order shall take effect immediately.

d21-28

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.

OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 1

JANUARY 1, 1978

BY THE POWER VESTED IN ME AS MAYOR OF THE CITY OF NEW YORK,
it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. All Executive Orders in effect on December 31, 1977, are hereby continued, except to the extent set forth in Section 9 of Executive Order No. 2 issued concurrently herewith.

§ 2. All Executive Orders in effect on December 31, 1977, and continued by this Order designating by name officials holding office in the government of the City to perform functions set forth in such Executive Orders are hereby modified to the extent that such functions shall be performed by the persons holding such offices pursuant to my direction.

§ 3. The head of the Council Against Poverty, the Title X Coordinator established by Executive Order No. 51 of February 4, 1976, and the heads of the constituent agencies administering Community Development program funds (with respect to those funds) shall hereafter report directly to the Mayor.

§ 4. All executive orders, administrative orders, labor relations orders and personnel orders shall hereafter be signed by the Mayor.

EDWARD I. KOCH, Mayor.

*Statement by Mayor Edward I. Koch*

To preserve continuity in the operation of government, I have today continued the effectiveness of virtually all the Executive Orders issued by prior Mayors. This does not mean, how-ever, that I am approving the content or substance of all those orders. To the contrary, I am
ordering my Counsel to make a complete review of the entire group of Executive Orders. Those
which do not reflect the policy of my Administration will be changed.

In addition, some of the orders deal with the structure and organization of the Govern-ment, which I intend to modify. For example, the structure of the management and budget
functions must conform to my Administration's arrangements. Thus, the continuation of orders
should not create any expectations that the status quo will be maintained. Furthermore, obsolete
orders may be repealed and certain offices abolished.

title: DEPUTY MAYORS
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 2

JANUARY 1, 1978

DEPUTY MAYORS

BY THE POWER VESTED IN ME AS MAYOR OF THE CITY OF NEW YORK,
it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. There shall be seven Deputy Mayors. One of them shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Management, one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Intergovernmental Relations, one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Personnel and Labor Relations, one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Policy, one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Economic Development, one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Finance, and one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Criminal Justice.

§ 2. The Deputy Mayor for Management shall:

(a) Supervise and coordinate the operations of all administrations, departments, boards and agencies, except as otherwise provided in this Order or as the Mayor may direct.

(b) Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Board of Education and the Board of Higher Education of The City of New York.

(c) Represent the Mayor when so directed on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

(d) Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§ 3. The Deputy Mayor for Intergovernmental Relations shall:

(a) In the absence of the Mayor from sessions of the Board of Estimate act on behalf of the Mayor at such sessions of the Board of Estimate.

(b) Act on behalf of the Mayor with respect to all Federal, State and local legislative matters affecting the City; direct the activities of the Mayor's legislative representative, the Albany office, and the Washington, D.C. office; represent the Mayor before Congressional and State legislative committees, maintain liaison with the Office of the President and all Federal departments and agencies thereof, the Office of the Governor and all State departments and agencies thereof, the Board of Estimate and the City Council; and supervise the activities of the New York City Commission for the United Nations and for the Consular Corps.

(c) Serve as the Mayor's representative on and maintain liaison with regional bodies and intergovernmental agencies operating within the New York metropolitan region.

(d) Maintain liaison with the United States Conference of Mayors, the National League of Cities, the New York State Conference of Mayors and other similar bodies.

(e) Represent the Mayor when so directed by the Mayor on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

(f) Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§ 4. The Deputy Mayor for Personnel and Labor Relations shall:

(a) Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Department of Personnel and the Office of Municipal Labor Relations; conduct all labor negotiations to which the City is a party; represent the Mayor and act on his behalf in connection with all labor negotiations in which the City has an interest, including, but not limited to, negotiations conducted by or on behalf of all public benefit corporations located within the City, the Board of Education and the Board of Higher Education of The City of New York.

(b) Represent the Mayor when so directed on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

(c) Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§ 5. The Deputy Mayor for Policy shall:

(a) Advise and assist the Mayor on matters of City policy.

(b) Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Health and Hospitals Corporation of The City of New York.

(c) Represent the Mayor when so directed by the Mayor on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

(d) Perform the duties specifically referred to in Section 7 of the New York City Charter and other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§ 6. The Deputy Mayor for Economic Development shall:

(a) Head the economic development program, supervise and coordinate the efforts to foster the economic growth of the City.

(b) Direct the operations of the Office for Economic Development.

(c) Represent the Mayor when so directed by the Mayor on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

(d) Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§ 7. The Deputy Mayor for Finance shall:

(a) Supervise and coordinate the City's fiscal operations, including the operations of the Office of Management and Budget.

(b) Act on behalf of and at the direction of the Mayor in exercising and carrying out the functions, powers and duties vested in or imposed upon the Mayor by the New York State Municipal Assistance Corporation Act, the Municipal Assistance Corporation for the City of New York Act and the New York State Financial Emergency Act for The City of New York.

(c) Act on behalf of and at the direction of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to Article 10 of the Public Authorities Law, as enacted by Chapters 168 and 169 of the Laws of 1975 as from time to time amended (hereinafter called the Act), including, but not limited to, full power to execute for, on behalf of, and at the direction of the Mayor any agreement pursuant to Section 3038 of the Act between The City of New York and the Municipal Assistance Corporation for The City of New York, any certificate pursuant to Section 3037 of the Act, and any other document in connection with the Act. The exercise of functions, powers and duties for, on behalf of and at the direction of the Mayor by such Deputy Mayor pursuant to this delegation shall not require the consent in writing of the Mayor or any other official of the City.

(d) For the purposes of Article 2, Section 9 of the Public Officers Law, notwithstanding the temporary inability of the Mayor to exercise such functions, powers and duties as he may have pursuant to the Act, by reason of sickness or otherwise, or his absence from the City, the delegation established by subdivision (c) of this Section 7 shall devolve upon the Deputy Mayor for Finance.

(e) Act for, on behalf of and at the direction of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York City
Seasonal Financing Act of 1975, Public Law 94-143, as the same may be from time to time
amended, and a credit agreement made thereunder as of December 30, 1975 by and among
the United States of America on the one hand and the State of New York, The City of
New York and the New York State Emergency Financial Control Board on the other
hand, including, but not limited to, full power to execute for, on behalf of, and at the direction of the Mayor, any document pursuant to such agreement and any agreement, amend-ment to agreement or other document pursuant to such law. The exercise of functions,
powers and duties for, on behalf of and at the direction of the Mayor by such Deputy Mayor
pursuant to this delegation shall not require the consent in writing of the Mayor or any
other official of the City.

Represent the Mayor when so directed by the Mayor on any board, committee,
commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

(g) Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§ 8. The Deputy Mayor for Criminal Justice shall:

(a) Serve as the coordinator of criminal justice provided by Section 13 of the New York City Charter.

(b) Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Department of Correction, Police Department and Department of Probation.

(c) Represent the Mayor when so directed by the Mayor on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

(d) Perform such other duties as the Mayor shall direct.

§ 9. References in Executive Orders to First Deputy Mayor are hereby amended to refer to the appropriate Deputy Mayor. The reference in Section 2 of Executive Order No. 43 of October 14, 1975 to "four Deputy Mayors" is hereby amended to refer to "seven Deputy Mayors." Executive Orders No. 2 of January 1, 1974, No. 40 of September 25, 1975, No. 49 of January 22, 1976, No. 71 of September 16, 1976, and No. 73 of October 20, 1976 are hereby revoked. Nothing in Executive Order No. 1 or this Executive Order shall be construed to affect the validity of any act performed prior to January 1, 1978 pursuant to such Executive Orders hereby revoked.

j9-13

EDWARD I. KOCH, Mayor.

title: DISCRIMINATION ON ACCOUNT OF SEXUAL ORIENTATION OR AFFECTIONAL PREFERENCE
full_text:
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 4

JANUARY 23, 1978

DISCRIMINATION ON ACCOUNT OF SEXUAL
ORIENTATION OR AFFECTIONAL PREFERENCE

Whereas, It has been the longstanding policy of The City of New York to prohibit discrimination by its administrations, agencies, departments and commissions on account of race, creed, color or national origin; and

Whereas, This policy has been expanded in recent years to prohibit discrimination against other groups on the basis of non-job related criteria.

Now, therefore, by the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. There shall be no discrimination by any City administration, agency, department, commission or other official entity, or any official representative thereof, on account of sexual orientation or affectional preference in any matter of hiring or employment, housing credit, contracting, provision of services, or any other matter whatsoever.

§ 2. Executive Order No. 71 of April 2, 1968, as amended by Executive Order No. 23 of August 24, 1970, is hereby further amended to delete the phrase "race, creed, color, national origin, sex or age," in the preamble of said Executive Order No. 71, as amended, and in the first sentence of Paragraphs (1) and (2) of subdivision (a) of section 2 thereof, and to substitute in each instance the phrase "race, creed, color, national origin, sex, age, sexual orientation or affectional preference".

All applicable regulations, rules, programs and guidelines shall be modified to take account of this Order. Nothing, however, in this Order shall be construed to authorize or require affirmative efforts regarding hiring, employment, housing, credit, contracting, provision of services or other matters covered hereby or to authorize or require any review or statistical analysis of the composition of a work force or other class of person affected hereby.

§ 3. The City Commission on Human Rights in accordance with the provisions of Chapter one, title B, section B1-5.0 of the Administrative Code shall receive and investigate complaints of violations of this Order and shall issue a report thereon to the Mayor, the Personnel Director of The City of New York and the administrative head of the City administration, agency, department, commission or other official entity involved, along with a recommendation for any corrective action which the Commission on Human Rights deems necessary and proper.

§ 4. This Order shall take effect immediately.

EDWARD I. KOCH, Mayor.

The City Commission on Human Rights in accordance with the provisions of Chapter one, title B, section B1-5.0 of the Administrative Code shall receive and investigate complaints of violations of this Order and shall issue a report thereon to the Mayor, the Personnel Director of The City of New York and the administrative head of the City administration, agency, department, commission or other official entity involved, along with a recommendation for any corrective action which the Commission on Human Rights deems necessary and proper.

§ 4. This Order shall take effect immediately.

ESTABLISHMENT OF A SOUTH BRONX COORDINATING COUNCIL

title: ESTABLISHMENT OF A COMMUNITY BOARD ASSISTANCE UNIT AND A COMMUNITY LIAISON UNIT
full_text:
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 6

FEBRUARY 8, 1978

ESTABLISHMENT OF A COMMUNITY BOARD ASSISTANCE UNIT
AND A COMMUNITY LIAISON UNIT

Section 1. There is hereby established within the Office of the Mayor a Community Board Assistance Unit and a Community Liaison Unit. Each Unit shall be headed by a director who shall be appointed by and serve at the pleasure of the Mayor.

§ 2. The Community Board Assistance Unit shall be responsible for coordinating the activities of City agencies with respect to the implementation and operation of the provisions of the Charter of the City of New York concerning community boards, district service cabinets and district managers, including, but not limited to, responsibility for:

(a) coordinating (i) the establishment of coterminous service districts by designated agencies and (ii) the assignment by each such agency of a managerial official with operating or line authority over agency programs, personnel and facilities to the district service cabinet, in accordance with Sections 2704 and 2705 of the Charter;

(b) designing and implementing, in conjunction with the Mayor's Office of Operations, a new format for the Mayor's Management Report and Supplemental Management Report which includes, insofar as practicable, schedules of agency service goals, performance measures and actual performance relative to goals, for each local service district in accordance with Section 12 of the Charter;

(c) coordinating with agencies statements for community service districts in accordance with and to the extent required by Section 2707 of the Charter;

(d) designing and implementing, in conjunction with the Office of Management and Budget, a system which reflects proposed agency budget data on a local service district or community district basis in accordance with Sections 112 and 218 of the Charter;

(e) maintaining a continuous liaison with community boards, district service cabinets and district managers in order to bring to the attention of the Mayor and other appropriate City officials significant problems arising in connection with the activities or operations of such organizations and to propose solutions to such problems;

(f) establishing, in conjunction with the Department of Personnel, appropriate personnel guidelines for community board employees in accordance with the Civil Service Law and regulations; and

(g) providing training and technical assistance for implementation of the appropriate Charter provisions to community boards, district service cabinets, district managers and City agencies.

§ 3. The Community Liaison Unit shall be responsible for maintaining a liaison with community groups in order to bring to the attention of the Mayor and other appropriate City

officials issues and problems of concern to communities, including, but not limited to, responsibility for the following:

(a) coordinating and expediting the activities of community-based groups, including without limitation civic, block and neighborhood groups, when said activities are consistent with Mayoral policy;

(b) coordinating such other community liaison activities as the Mayor may direct; and

(c) representing the Mayor at community meetings when requested to do so by the

Mayor.

§ 4. All appropriate City agencies, including without limitation the Police Department, the Department of Parks Recreation, the Department of Sanitation, the Human Resources Administration, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development, the Department of Buildings, the City Planning Commission, the Department of Health, the Department of General Services, the Office of Management and Budget, the Department of Personnel, and the Department of Environmental Protection, are directed to cooperate with the Units established hereby in order to carry out the objectives of the Charter and of this Order.

§ 5. The Office of Service Coordination is hereby abolished, and the Units established hereby shall succeed to the functions and duties heretofore exercised by such Office, to the extent the same are continued by this Order.

§ 6. This Order shall take effect immediately.

f23-m1

EDWARD I. KOCH, Mayor.

title: BOARD OF INQUIRY INTO UNDERGROUND SEWER EXPLOSIONS
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 11

APRIL 14, 1978

BOARD OF INQUIRY INTO UNDERGROUND SEWER EXPLOSIONS

By the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. *Board Established.* A Board of Inquiry (hereinafter called the Board) into the underground sewer explosions which occurred on March 24, 1978 in the South Bronx is hereby established. The Board shall consist of the Deputy Mayor for Management, who shall act as Chairman, the Police Commissioner, the Fire Commissioner, the Commissioner of Investigation, the Environmental Protection Commissioner and the Corporation Counsel.

§ 2. *Scope of Inquiry.* The Board shall make diligent inquiry into the circumstances surrounding the underground sewer explosions to determine the causes of these injurious events and which persons or organizations bear responsibility for them. The Board shall inquire into the extent to which local, state and federal government agencies have jurisdiction over the operation and management of the sewer system and whether such agencies have properly discharged their duties in connection with the underground sewer explosions. The Board shall make such reports, recommendations and proposals as it deems proper.

§ 3. *Conduct of Inquiry.* The Board, or its staff at the direction of the Board, shall make such inquiries, conduct such investigations and hold such public and private hearings and take such other measures as the members deem appropriate to its inquiry. For such purposes the Board shall have power to take testimony under oath and to require and to enforce by subpoena the attendance of witnesses and the production of documents. The Board shall make reports to the Mayor at such times as the Mayor may direct.

§ 4. *Staff and Expenses.* The Board may appoint such employees and incur such expenses as may be necessary to its inquiry.

§ 5. *Effective Date.* This Executive Order shall take effect immediately.

a21-27

EDWARD I. KOCH, Mayor.

By the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. *Board Established.* A Board of Inquiry (hereinafter called the Board) into the underground sewer explosions which occurred on March 24, 1978 in the South Bronx is hereby established. The Board shall consist of the Deputy Mayor for Management, who shall act as Chairman, the Police Commissioner, the Fire Commissioner, the Commissioner of Investigation, the Environmental Protection Commissioner and the Corporation Counsel.

§ 2. *Scope of Inquiry.* The Board shall make diligent inquiry into the circumstances surrounding the underground sewer explosions to determine the causes of these injurious events and which persons or organizations bear responsibility for them. The Board shall inquire into the extent to which local, state and federal government agencies have jurisdiction over the operation and management of the sewer system and whether such agencies have properly discharged their duties in connection with the underground sewer explosions. The Board shall make such reports, recommendations and proposals as it deems proper.

§ 3. *Conduct of Inquiry.* The Board, or its staff at the direction of the Board, shall make such inquiries, conduct such investigations and hold such public and private hearings and take such other measures as the members deem appropriate to its inquiry. For such purposes the Board shall have power to take testimony under oath and to require and to enforce by subpoena the attendance of witnesses and the production of documents. The Board shall make reports to the Mayor at such times as the Mayor may direct.

§ 4. *Staff and Expenses.* The Board may appoint such employees and incur such expenses as may be necessary to its inquiry.

§ 5. *Effective Date.* This Executive Order shall take effect immediately.

title: COUNCIL ON THE ENVIRONMENT
full_text:
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 13

MAY 9, 1978

COUNCIL ON THE ENVIRONMENT

BY VIRTUE OF THE POWER VESTED IN ME AS MAYOR OF THE CITY OF NEW YORK, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. There is hereby continued in the Office of the Mayor the Council on the Environment of New York City (hereinafter called the Council). The Council shall promote environmental concern among New Yorkers and develop solutions to the environmental problems of the City.

§ 2. The Council shall be composed of not less than 15 or more than 35 members. Members shall be appointed by the Mayor for a term of two years. A vacancy occurring other than by expiration of a term shall be filled by the Mayor for the remainder of the term. Members of the Council serving presently shall continue to serve until the expiration of their respective terms.

§ 3. The membership of the Council shall include representatives of agencies concerned with protecting the environment. At least three-quarters of the members shall be individuals who do not, at the time of their appointment, hold public office or employment. The members of the Council shall serve without compensation.

§ 4. The Chairman of the Council shall be designated by the Mayor from among members of the Council and shall be a resident of the City of New York.

§ 5. The duties and powers of the Council shall include the following:

(a) to confer with appropriate City, State, Federal and private agencies concerned with protecting the environment for the purpose of considering, developing and improving environmental protection programs and policies and for the purpose of securing funds to support the activities of the Council;

(b) to conduct research and to operate programs for pollution control and other environmental protection purposes;

(c) to sponsor conferences and to prepare and publish reports;

(d) to encourage joint activities among the various agencies concerned with the protection of the environment; and

(e) to advise the Mayor on matters concerning the protection of the environment and to perform such other functions as the Mayor may direct.

§ 6. City agencies responsible for matters concerning the protection of the environment shall cooperate with the Council with respect to its function under this Order.

§ 7. The Council shall submit an annual report of its activities to the Mayor.

§ 8. No expense shall be incurred by the Council for personnel, equipment or otherwise, unless funds sufficient to pay for such expenses have been previously obtained from sources other than City tax levy funds.

§ 9. Executive Order No. 57 of 1972 is hereby revoked.

§ 10. This Order shall take effect immediately.

m22-26

EDWARD I. KOCH, Mayor.

full_text:
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 15

JULY 17, 1978

EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICE COUNCIL

BY THE POWER VESTED IN ME AS MAYOR OF THE CITY OR NEW YORK, IT
is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Council Established. The Emergency Medical Service Council (hereinafter called the Council) is hereby established.

§ 2. Members. (a) The Council shall be composed of five members appointed by the Mayor. The health services administrator shall be a member and shall serve as chairman of the Council. Two members shall be health care professionals with substantial experience in emergency care; and two members shall be representatives of the general public and shall not be providers of health care.

(b) The members of the Council, other than the chairman, shall serve for a term of two years, except as follows. Two initial members of the Council, including one professional member and one public member, shall serve for a term ending December 31, 1979. Two initial members of the Council, including one professional member and one public member, shall serve for a term ending December 31, 1980.

(c) Vacancies shall be filled by the Mayor for the remainder of a member's term.

§ 3. *Purposes.* (a) The Council shall consider and advise the Mayor on matters concerning the establishment and operation of a unified City-wide emergency medical service system, including the Health and Hospitals Corporation ("HHC"), proprietary, voluntary and other health care providers, to ensure the effective and efficient provision of ambulance, paramedical, emergency room, back-up and other emergency medical services to the people of New York City.

(b) The Council shall review and advise the Mayor on all complaints and disputes concerning the emergency medical service system, including any which concern the participation of a health care provider in the system.

(c) The Council shall undertake such studies, make such recommendations and take such other actions as it may deem proper.

(d) The Council shall consult with the Emergency Medical Services System Advisor Council and the Regional Emergency Medical Services Council and other appropriate agencies organizations and persons.

(e) The Council shall submit an annual report of its activities to the Mayor.

§ 4. *Action by the Council.* (a) The presence of the chairman, one professional member and one public member shall constitute a quorum.

(b) The Council shall act by affirmative vote of three members.

§ 5. *Staff and Expenses.* (a) Members of the Council shall serve without compensation, but may be reimbursed for reasonable and necessary expenses incurred in the performance of their duties.

(b) Subject to the approval of the Council, a City employee shall be appointed by the Mayor to serve as the full-time director of the Council. The director shall serve at the pleasure of the Mayor.

title: COMMISSIONER OF INVESTIGATION, INSPECTORS GENERAL AND STANDARDS OF PUBLIC SERVICE
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 16

JULY 26, 1978

COMMISSIONER OF INVESTIGATION, INSPECTORS GENERAL
AND STANDARDS OF PUBLIC SERVICE

BY THE POWER VESTED IN ME AS MAYOR OF THE CITY OF NEW YORK,
it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Responsibilities of Commissioner. The Commissioner of Investigation (herein-after called the Commissioner) shall have general responsibility for the investigation and elimination of corrupt or other criminal activity, conflicts of interest, unethical conduct, misconduct and incompetence (i) by City agencies, (ii) by City officers and employees, and (iii) by persons regulated by, doing business with or receiving funds directly or indirectly from the City (here-inafter called persons dealing with the City), with respect to their dealings with the City. For these purposes the Commissioner shall: (a) assist agency heads in establishing and maintaining standards of conduct together with fair and efficient disciplinary systems; (b) direct the activities of the Inspectors General of all agencies of the City; (c) conduct background investigations of employees to be appointed to or holding positions of responsibility; (d) receive complaints and information from the public with respect to City agencies, officers, and employees, as well as persons dealing with the City, and to take appropriate action with respect to such complaints; (e) undertake any investigation or study of the affairs, functions, accounts, methods, personnel or efficiency of any agency; and (f) act as liaison with federal, state and local law enforcement and regulatory agencies concerning all matters within the scope of this Order.

§ 2. Responsibility of Agency Heads. All agency heads shall be responsible for establishing, subject to review for completeness and inter-agency consistency by the Commissioner, written standards of conduct for the officials and employees of their respective agencies and fair and efficient disciplinary systems to maintain those standards of conduct.

§ 3. Responsibilities of Inspectors General.

(a) All agencies shall have an Inspector General who shall report directly to the respective agency head and to the Commissioner and be responsible for maintaining standards of conduct as may be established in such agency under this Order. Inspectors General shall be responsible for the investigation and elimination of corrupt or other criminal activity, conflicts of interest, unethical conduct, misconduct and incompetence within their respective agencies.

(b) Except to the extent otherwise provided by law, the employment or continued employment of all existing and prospective Inspectors General and members of their staffs shall be subject to complete background investigations and approval by the Department of Investigation.

§ 4. Investigations.

(a) Within the scope of the general responsibility of the Commissioner set forth in Section 1 of this Order, the Commissioner shall have authority to examine, copy or remove any document prepared, maintained or held by any agency except those documents which may not be so disclosed according to law. Inspectors General shall have the same authority in their respective agencies.

(b) The Commissioner and, with the approval of the Commissioner, the Inspectors General and any person under the supervision of the Commissioner or the Inspectors General, may require any officer or employee of the City to answer questions concerning any matter related to the performance of his or her official duties or any person dealing with the City, concerning such dealings with the City, after first being advised that neither their statements nor any information or evidence derived therefrom will be used against them in a subsequent criminal prosecution other than for perjury or contempt arising from such testimony. The refusal of an officer or employee to answer questions on the condition described in this paragraph shall constitute cause for removal from office or employment or other appropriate penalty. Beginning September 1, 1978 all contracts, leases, licenses or other agreements entered into or issued by the City shall contain a provisions approved as to form by the Corporation Counsel permitting the City to terminate such agreement or to take other appropriate action upon the refusal of a person dealing with the City to answer questions in relation to such agreements on the condition of testimonial or use immunity described in this paragraph.

(c) Every officer or employee of the City shall cooperate fully with the Commissioner and the Inspectors General. Interference with or obstruction of an investigation conducted by the Commissioner or an Inspector General shall constitute cause for removal from office or employment or other appropriate penalty.

(d) Every officer and employee of the City shall have the affirmative obligation to report, directly and without undue delay, to the Commissioner or an Inspector General any and all information concerning conduct which they know or should reasonably know to involve corrupt or other criminal activity or conflict of interest, (i) by another City officer or employee, which concerns his or her office or employment, or (ii) by persons dealing with the City, which concerns their dealings with the City. The knowing failure of any officer or employee to report as required above shall constitute cause for removal from office or employment or other appropriate penalty.

(e) Upon receipt of any information concerning corrupt or other criminal activity or conflict of interest related to his or her agency, the Inspector General of such agency shall report directly and without undue delay such information to the Department of Investigation, and shall proceed in accordance with the Commissioner's directions.

(f) No officer or employee other than the Commissioner, an Inspector General, or an officer or employee under their supervision, shall conduct any investigation concerning corrupt or other criminal activity or conflicts of interest without the prior approval of the Commissioner or an Inspector General.

§ 5. Formal Disciplinary Proceedings.

(a) Within six months of the effective date of this Order, the Inspector General of each agency shall be responsible for the preparation and prosecution of all formal administrative proceedings, including removal and other disciplinary proceedings for misconduct or incompetence, initiated by such Inspector General or any other person authorized by the agency head to initiate such proceedings on behalf of the agency. The Inspector General or an attorney-designee (including attorneys of the Department of Investigation) shall prosecute such matters. Any agency head may for good cause apply to the Commissioner for the modification or waiver of any provision of this paragraph.

(b) The Inspector General of an agency may, with the approval of the agency head, remove an agency head from office without the timely service of formal charges.

(c) Officers or employees of the City convicted of a crime relating to their office or employment, involving moral turpitude or which bears upon their fitness or ability to perform their duties or responsibilities, shall be removed from an office or employment, absent compelling mitigating circumstances set forth in writing by the head of the employing agency. Proof of said conviction, as a basis for removal or other disciplinary action, must be established in accordance with applicable law.

§ 6. Informal Disciplinary Proceedings.

(a) Each agency head shall, with the advice of the Commissioner, establish appropriate reporting requirements, disposition standards and other administrative procedures for informal disciplinary proceedings to permit the fair and expeditious resolution of minor violations of the standards of conduct established by such agency head under this Order, without prejudice to any rights provided to officers or employees of the City by law or by contract.

(b) Informal disciplinary proceedings may be undertaken on the following conditions:

(i) the employee or official who is the subject of such proceedings shall consent to accept a predetermined penalty upon a finding of cause in lieu of the filing or formal disciplinary

charge; and (ii) the record and result of the informal disciplinary proceedings shall be expunged from all permanent personnel or employment files of the subject official or employee after one year in which such person has not been penalized as a result of any subsequent formal or informal disciplinary proceedings.

(c) The Inspector General of each agency shall be notified of the disposition of all informal disciplinary proceedings.

§ 7. Background Investigations.

(a) The Department of Investigation shall conduct background investigations of all persons to be appointed to or employed in positions with salary rates equal to or greater than the minimum rate of the Management Pay Plan or any successor plan, whether or not the person is to become a member of such plan.

(b) Background investigations need not be made under this Order with respect to the appointment or employment of persons for positions with salary rates equal to or greater than the minimum rate of the Management Pay Plan or any successor plan where such person is to be appointed to a permanent civil service position in the competitive class.

(c) The Mayor or any agency head may in the public interest direct that the appointment, employment or assignment of any person be subject to a background investigation by the Department of Investigation.

(d) The appointment or employment of any person requiring background investigations under this Order shall be made subject to the completion of such investigation and a determination by the appointing authority that the appointee has the appropriate qualifications, is free from actual or potential conflicts of interest and is one in whom the public trust may be placed.

(e) All prospective appointees and employees subject to background investigation under this Order shall comply with all procedures established by the Commissioner for such purpose, including the completion of a background questionnaire and full disclosure of financial holdings and relationships.

(f) Background investigations conducted under this Order shall include the collection of all available criminal history information relating to the prospective appointee, which shall be considered in accordance with applicable law.

(g) The making by a person of an intentional false or misleading statement in connection with a background investigation required under this Order, or otherwise failing to comply with the background investigation procedures established by the Commissioner, may constitute cause for removal from office or employment or other appropriate penalty.

§ 8. Dissemination of Information.

(a) All agency heads shall distribute to each officer and employee of their respective agencies within 90 days of the effective date of this Order and to each officer and employee appointed thereafter, a statement prepared by the Commissioner explaining the responsibilities of the Commissioner, Inspectors General, agency heads and all City officers and employees under this Order.

(b) Knowledge of the responsibilities of the Commissioner of Investigation and the Inspectors General and of relevant provisions of Articles 195 and 200 of the Penal Law, the City Charter, the Code of Ethics and this Order shall constitute an employment responsibility which every officer and employee is expected to know and to implement as part of their job duties and is to be tested in promotional examinations beginning January 1, 1979.

### § 9. Regulations and Procedures.
The Commissioner may establish such regulations, procedures and reporting requirements with respect to Inspectors General or as may be otherwise necessary or proper to fulfill the Commissioner's responsibilities under this Order and other applicable law. The Inspectors General may, with the approval of the Commissioner and the respective agency heads, establish such regulations and procedures as may be necessary or proper to fulfill their responsibilities under this Order and other applicable law.

### § 10. Waiver of Provisions.
Any agency head may for good cause apply to the Commissioner for the modification of waiver of any provision within the jurisdiction of the Commissioner under this Order.

### § 11. Construction with Other Laws.
Nothing in this Order shall be deemed to limit the powers and duties of the Commissioner, the Department of Investigation, the Department of Personnel, the Office of Municipal Labor Relations or any other agency under the City Charter or as may be otherwise provided by law.

### § 12. Preservation of Rights.
Nothing in this Order shall be deemed to limit the rights of any person under law or contract.

### § 13. Revocation of Executive Orders.
Executive Order No. 21, dated August 19, 1970, Executive Order No. 21, dated October 17, 1974, and Personnel Policy and Procedure No. 715-77, dated February 15, 1977 are hereby revoked.

### § 14. Effective Date.
This Order shall take effect immediately.

EDWARD I. KOCH, Mayor.

(i) the employee or official who is the subject of such proceedings shall consent to accept a predetermined penalty upon a finding of cause in lieu of the filing or formal disciplinary

charge; and (ii) the record and result of the informal disciplinary proceedings shall be expunged from all permanent personnel or employment files of the subject official or employee after one year in which such person has not been penalized as a result of any subsequent formal or informal disciplinary proceedings.

(c) The Inspector General of each agency shall be notified of the disposition of all informal disciplinary proceedings.

§ 7. Background Investigations.

(a) The Department of Investigation shall conduct background investigations of all persons to be appointed to or employed in positions with salary rates equal to or greater than the minimum rate of the Management Pay Plan or any successor plan, whether or not the person is to become a member of such plan.

(b) Background investigations need not be made under this Order with respect to the appointment or employment of persons for positions with salary rates equal to or greater than the minimum rate of the Management Pay Plan or any successor plan where such person is to be appointed to a permanent civil service position in the competitive class.

(c) The Mayor or any agency head may in the public interest direct that the appointment, employment or assignment of any person be subject to a background investigation by the Department of Investigation.

(d) The appointment or employment of any person requiring background investigations under this Order shall be made subject to the completion of such investigation and a determination by the appointing authority that the appointee has the appropriate qualifications, is free from actual or potential conflicts of interest and is one in whom the public trust may be placed.

(e) All prospective appointees and employees subject to background investigation under this Order shall comply with all procedures established by the Commissioner for such purpose, including the completion of a background questionnaire and full disclosure of financial holdings and relationships.

(f) Background investigations conducted under this Order shall include the collection of all available criminal history information relating to the prospective appointee, which shall be considered in accordance with applicable law.

(g) The making by a person of an intentional false or misleading statement in connection with a background investigation required under this Order, or otherwise failing to comply with the background investigation procedures established by the Commissioner, may constitute cause for removal from office or employment or other appropriate penalty.

§ 8. Dissemination of Information.

(a) All agency heads shall distribute to each officer and employee of their respective agencies within 90 days of the effective date of this Order and to each officer and employee appointed thereafter, a statement prepared by the Commissioner explaining the responsibilities of the Commissioner, Inspectors General, agency heads and all City officers and employees under this Order.

(b) Knowledge of the responsibilities of the Commissioner of Investigation and the Inspectors General and of relevant provisions of Articles 195 and 200 of the Penal Law, the City Charter, the Code of Ethics and this Order shall constitute an employment responsibility which every officer and employee is expected to know and to implement as part of their job duties and is to be tested in promotional examinations beginning January 1, 1979.

### § 9. Regulations and Procedures.
The Commissioner may establish such regulations, procedures and reporting requirements with respect to Inspectors General or as may be otherwise necessary or proper to fulfill the Commissioner's responsibilities under this Order and other applicable law. The Inspectors General may, with the approval of the Commissioner and the respective agency heads, establish such regulations and procedures as may be necessary or proper to fulfill their responsibilities under this Order and other applicable law.

### § 10. Waiver of Provisions.
Any agency head may for good cause apply to the Commissioner for the modification of waiver of any provision within the jurisdiction of the Commissioner under this Order.

### § 11. Construction with Other Laws.
Nothing in this Order shall be deemed to limit the powers and duties of the Commissioner, the Department of Investigation, the Department of Personnel, the Office of Municipal Labor Relations or any other agency under the City Charter or as may be otherwise provided by law.

### § 12. Preservation of Rights.
Nothing in this Order shall be deemed to limit the rights of any person under law or contract.

### § 13. Revocation of Executive Orders.
Executive Order No. 21, dated August 19, 1970, Executive Order No. 21, dated October 17, 1974, and Personnel Policy and Procedure No. 715-77, dated February 15, 1977 are hereby revoked.

### § 14. Effective Date.
This Order shall take effect immediately.

EDWARD I. KOCH, Mayor.

title: NEW YORK CITY CONSTRUCTION CONTRACTS
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 17

JULY 26, 1978

NEW YORK CITY CONSTRUCTION CONTRACTS

BY THE POWER VESTED IN ME AS MAYOR OF THE CITY OF NEW YORK, IT
is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Prior Executive Order. Executive Order No. 89, dated July 21, 1977, is hereby
amended to add the following provision as Section 4-a:

§ 4-a. This Order shall not apply to any construction contract in the amount of $250,000 or less.

§ 2. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately

EDWARD I. KOCH, Mayor.

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 89

JULY 21, 1977

INFORMATION REGARDING APPRENTICESHIP PROGRAMS AND HEALTH, WELFARE AND PENSION PLANS TO BE SUBMITTED WITH EACH BID ON NEW YORK CITY CONSTRUCTION CONTRACTS.

Whereas, The payment to employees of prevailing wages and benefits pursuant to Section 220 of the Labor Law by contractors engaged in public works has been a subject of serious concern to the City; and

Whereas, In order to protect the public interest and the welfare of the employees in the payment of prevailing wages and benefits, it is desirable and necessary to provide safeguards and adopt certain procedures to insure compliance with the provisions of Section 220.

Now, therefore, by the power vested in me as the Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. Every construction contract, including those involving alterations, repairs, or rehabilitation, to which any mayoral or non-mayoral agency is a part, or the payment of which will be made in whole or in part from City funds, shall require that the following information be submitted with every bid thereon which shall be made a part of the bid documents for all such contracts and sworn to by the bidder:

a. Information regarding the bidder's past utilization of apprentices on New York City contracts.

b. The bidder's intention to utilize apprentices on the contract for which the bid is submitted.

c. Information regarding the bidder's health and welfare program.

d. Information regarding the bidder's pension plan.

§ 2. If the low bidder indicates that he was a non-participant in an approved apprentice-ship program and either used apprentices on prior New York City contracts or intends to use apprentices on this contract, the agency head shall convene a Board of Responsibility to determine whether the contract should be awarded to that low bidder.

§ 3. If the low bidder indicates that he does not provide a participating health and welfare program or a registered pension plan, the agency head may not award the contract to that low bidder. However, if the low bidder indicates that he is a self-insured provider of such a program or plan, the agency head shall convene a Board of Responsibility to determine whether the contract should be awarded to that low bidder.

§ 4. The Board of Responsibility is to consist of the agency head, Comptroller and Corporation Counsel or their duly designated representatives.

§ 5. This Executive Order shall take effect immediately.

a2-8

ABRAHAM D. BEAME, Mayor.

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 19

SEPTEMBER 7, 1978

REAL PROPERTY TAX ASSESSMENTS

By the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. *Evaluation of Real Property*—With a view to satisfying the requirements of the Real Property Tax Law as amended by the Laws of 1978, chapter 476, the Finance Department, the Tax Commission, and the Real Property Assessment Department, insofar as each has jurisdiction over real property assessments in the City, shall file all necessary applications with the appropriate State agencies and take any and all steps necessary to move toward physical revaluation of all real property within the boundaries of the City at 100 per cent of full value.

full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 20

SEPTEMBER 8, 1978

ESTABLISHMENT OF THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT COMMITTEE TO
COORDINATE THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT PROGRAM

By virtue of the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby
ordered:

Section 1. *Committee Established*—There is established in the Office of the Mayor the Community Development Committee (hereinafter called the Committee) which shall consist of the following members:

(a) the Chairman of the City Planning Commission, who shall serve as the Executive Director of the Committee;

(b) the Special Advisor to the Mayor with overall responsibility for liaison with communities;

(c) the Deputy Mayor for Policy;

(d) the Deputy Mayor for Management;

(e) the Deputy Mayor for Intergovernmental Relations;

(f) the Deputy Mayor for Economic Policy and Development;

(g) the Counsel to the Mayor;

(h) the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (hereinafter called OMB);

(i) the Commissioner of Housing Preservation and Development;

(j) the Director of the Community Board Assistance Unit;

(k) the President of the City Council; and

(l) such other City officials as may be designated from time to time by the Mayor.

§ 2. *Responsibilities of the Committee*—(a) The Committee shall be responsible for making recommendations to the Mayor on all policies, procedures and programs related to the Community Development Block Grant Program (hereinafter called the CD Program) established pursuant to the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974.

(b) The Committee shall be responsible for establishing guidelines for the development of the annual application, including the three-year plan and the one-year program budget, for the CD Program.

§ 3. *Responsibilities of the Executive Director*—(a) The Executive Director shall have overall responsibility for the administration of the CD Program and for the coordination of the activities of all City agencies with respect to the CD Program.

(b) The Executive Director shall be responsible for reporting to the United States Depart-ment of Housing and Urban Development (hereinafter called HUD) on all aspects of the City's program.

(c) The Executive Director and the Department of City Planning (hereinafter called the DCP) shall serve as the City liaison with other governmental agencies and shall coordinate, with appropriate agencies, all other Community Development activities or programs as may emerge from federal legislation.

(d) The Executive Director and the DCP shall prepare the CD Program Budget and Application in conjunction with OMB to ensure proper coordination of the Community Development, Capital and Expense Budgets of the City.

(e) The Executive Director and the DCP shall develop neighborhood program plans, pursuant to HUD and local requirements for Neighborhood Strategy Area designations.

(f) The Executive Director and the DCP in consultation with the Department of Housing Preservation and Development and the New York City Housing Authority shall prepare the Housing Assistance Plan and prepare the performance evaluation relative thereto for the annual performance report.

(g) The DCP and OMB shall jointly review and process CD Program amendments in accordance with guidelines established by the Committee.

(h) The DCP shall provide mechanisms for citizen participation in the CD Program in compliance with federal, state and local guidelines and shall provide ongoing liaison with Community Boards and other interested groups and citizens.

§ 4. *Responsibilities of OMB*—(a) OMB shall have overall responsibility for coordinating program implementation, including but not limited to monitoring all agencies receiving Community Development funds (hereinafter called CD funds) to ensure timely execution of projects consistent with federal, state and City regulations; record keeping; program procedures; regular reporting on program implementation; program evaluation; and completion of environmental reviews.

(b) OMB shall be responsible for financial management of the CD Programs including but not limited to: drawdown of federal funds; monitoring obligations, expenditures and reallocation of CD funds; coordinating traditional OMB activities as they relate to the CD Program; and maintaining liaison with the Comptroller's Office.

(c) OMB and DCP shall jointly prepare the annual performance report including establishing evaluation criteria and performing program evaluations.

(d) OMB shall provide reports to the Committee on a regular basis, evaluating and monitoring the CD Program and giving the financial status of the CD Program.

§ 5. *Responsibilities of the City Planning Commission*—The City Planning Commission shall review and hold a public hearing on the CD Program and shall issue a report and recommendations. It shall review, hold public hearings and report on proposed amendments pursuant to guidelines established by the Committee.

§ 6. *Responsibilities of Other Agencies*—(a) Operating agencies expending CD funds shall be responsible for planning, implementing and operating projects under the CD Program in compliance with federal, state and City guidelines and policies.

(b) Operating agencies shall report to the Executive Director and the Committee, as well as to local community organizations, on a periodic basis or as required.

(c) Operating agencies shall participate in the preparation and review of environmental assessments for projects under their jurisdiction and pursuant to guidelines and funding allocations established by the Committee and the DCP.

§ 7. *Prior Administrative Order*—Administrative Order No. 37, dated August 4, 1977, is hereby revoked.

§ 8. *Effective Date*—This Order shall take effect immediately.

s20-26

EDWARD I. KOCH, Mayor.

title: ESTABLISHMENT OF THE OFFICE OF DIRECTOR OF CONSTRUCTION
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 24

OCTOBER 27, 1978

ESTABLISHMENT OF THE OFFICE OF DIRECTOR OF CONSTRUCTION
By virtue of the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby

ordered:
By virtue of the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby

ordered:

Section 1. Office of Director of Construction Established. There is established in the Office of the Mayor the Office of Director of Construction, headed by the Director of Construction (hereinafter called the Director).

§ 2. Construction Board Established. There is established in the Office of the Mayor a Construction Board consisting of the Director, who shall serve as Chairman, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (hereinafter called OMB), the Director of Operations, the Corporation Counsel and the Chairman of the City Planning Commission, or their delegates, and, with the agreement of the Comptroller, the Comptroller or his delegate. All rules and regulations and directives issued by the Director that involve the Comptroller's duties and responsibilities mandated by law and the fiscal policies and procedures that ensue from them or the budgetary policies of the OMB shall be submitted to the Comptroller or to OMB respectively prior to promulgation.

§ 3. Responsibilities of the Director. The Director shall establish procedures pursuant to Section 228(e) of the City Charter for all agencies with respect to the planning, design, processing, implementation and execution of all construction projects, including, but not limited to:

(a) the format, content, and level of detail required for programs to ensure adequate definition of project scope and the establishment of accurate cost estimates prior to project budgeting;

(b) the selection and evaluation of consulting architects, engineers, and construction managers and the review, in conjunction with the Corporation Counsel, of contract terms and conditions;

(c) the review of design drawings and project specifications to ensure rapid processing of documents, consistent with City construction standards;

(d) the preparation of documents for bid, advertising and award of contracts, processing of change orders, acceptance of completed projects, record retention and, where appropriate, termination of projects;

(e) the inspection of construction progress, evaluation of contractor performance, and the establishment of qualifications and standards for award of construction, architectural, engineering and planning contracts; and

(f) the monitoring and expedition of the processing of periodic and final payments to consultants and contractors in connection with construction projects.

§ 4. The Director shall require all agencies to prepare and submit periodic reports on the progress of all construction projects including construction schedules and explanations of any delays as required by Section 228(d) of the City Charter.

§ 5. The Director shall manage major construction projects when so directed by the Mayor. Where there is a multi-agency construction project, the Director shall designate the agency with prime responsibility for the project.

§ 6. The Director shall cooperate with the Director of OMB in establishing and maintaining a Management Information System covering the City's capital program.

§ 7. The Director shall identify all construction projects which have experienced or can reasonably be expected to experience serious delays and report to the Mayor on the causes thereof. The Director is authorized to direct the agency involved to take appropriate action to stop or minimize the delay or potential delay including, but not limited to, such actions as:

(a) requiring that contracts for construction, consultants or other services be enforced strictly;

(b) requiring that a default hearing be held; and

(c) revising contract procedures, vouchering and construction practices.

In addition, the Director may recommend to the Mayor that:

(a) budget modifications be made, and

(b) agency personnel be transferred from or reassigned to the project.

§ 8. The Director may conduct appropriate studies in price trends, construction materials, methods, management and bidding practices to obtain maximum advantage for the City in contracting.

§ 9. Subject to limitations of funding and in consultation with OMB, the Director shall be responsible for approving the use of private consulting services.

§ 10. The Director shall establish procedures to expedite the issuance of blanket certificates of funding covering all types of construction projects.

§ 11. The Director shall promulgate rules and regulations establishing goals, timetables and response times for all agencies involved with construction projects.

§ 12. The Director shall promulgate rules and regulations in conjunction with OMB setting forth procedures to implement Sections 232 and 233 of the City Charter.

§ 13. The Director shall serve as liaison with the Construction industry in New York City. He shall attempt to resolve problems which arise in connection with private construction work by bringing those problems to the attention of the appropriate operating agency for action and providing, where appropriate, assistance in their resolution. Such problems shall be acted upon expeditiously by each agency.

§ 14. The Director shall seek ways to increase the willingness of private contractors to do construction work for the City by meeting with representatives of the construction industry including the building trades on a regular basis.

§ 15. The Director shall consult with a committee or other advisory body established by the Mayor on the capital construction process of the City.

§ 16. All rules, regulations and directives issued by the Director under authority of this executive order shall be binding on all agencies.

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 24

OCTOBER 27, 1978

ESTABLISHMENT OF THE OFFICE OF DIRECTOR OF CONSTRUCTION
By virtue of the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby

ordered:
By virtue of the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby

ordered:

Section 1. Office of Director of Construction Established. There is established in the Office of the Mayor the Office of Director of Construction, headed by the Director of Construction (hereinafter called the Director).

§ 2. Construction Board Established. There is established in the Office of the Mayor a Construction Board consisting of the Director, who shall serve as Chairman, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (hereinafter called OMB), the Director of Operations, the Corporation Counsel and the Chairman of the City Planning Commission, or their delegates, and, with the agreement of the Comptroller, the Comptroller or his delegate. All rules and regulations and directives issued by the Director that involve the Comptroller's duties and responsibilities mandated by law and the fiscal policies and procedures that ensue from them or the budgetary policies of the OMB shall be submitted to the Comptroller or to OMB respectively prior to promulgation.

§ 3. Responsibilities of the Director. The Director shall establish procedures pursuant to Section 228(e) of the City Charter for all agencies with respect to the planning, design, processing, implementation and execution of all construction projects, including, but not limited to:

(a) the format, content, and level of detail required for programs to ensure adequate definition of project scope and the establishment of accurate cost estimates prior to project budgeting;

(b) the selection and evaluation of consulting architects, engineers, and construction managers and the review, in conjunction with the Corporation Counsel, of contract terms and conditions;

(c) the review of design drawings and project specifications to ensure rapid processing of documents, consistent with City construction standards;

(d) the preparation of documents for bid, advertising and award of contracts, processing of change orders, acceptance of completed projects, record retention and, where appropriate, termination of projects;

(e) the inspection of construction progress, evaluation of contractor performance, and the establishment of qualifications and standards for award of construction, architectural, engineering and planning contracts; and

(f) the monitoring and expedition of the processing of periodic and final payments to consultants and contractors in connection with construction projects.

§ 4. The Director shall require all agencies to prepare and submit periodic reports on the progress of all construction projects including construction schedules and explanations of any delays as required by Section 228(d) of the City Charter.

§ 5. The Director shall manage major construction projects when so directed by the Mayor. Where there is a multi-agency construction project, the Director shall designate the agency with prime responsibility for the project.

§ 6. The Director shall cooperate with the Director of OMB in establishing and maintaining a Management Information System covering the City's capital program.

§ 7. The Director shall identify all construction projects which have experienced or can reasonably be expected to experience serious delays and report to the Mayor on the causes thereof. The Director is authorized to direct the agency involved to take appropriate action to stop or minimize the delay or potential delay including, but not limited to, such actions as:

(a) requiring that contracts for construction, consultants or other services be enforced strictly;

(b) requiring that a default hearing be held; and

(c) revising contract procedures, vouchering and construction practices.

In addition, the Director may recommend to the Mayor that:

(a) budget modifications be made, and

(b) agency personnel be transferred from or reassigned to the project.

§ 8. The Director may conduct appropriate studies in price trends, construction materials, methods, management and bidding practices to obtain maximum advantage for the City in contracting.

§ 9. Subject to limitations of funding and in consultation with OMB, the Director shall be responsible for approving the use of private consulting services.

§ 10. The Director shall establish procedures to expedite the issuance of blanket certificates of funding covering all types of construction projects.

§ 11. The Director shall promulgate rules and regulations establishing goals, timetables and response times for all agencies involved with construction projects.

§ 12. The Director shall promulgate rules and regulations in conjunction with OMB setting forth procedures to implement Sections 232 and 233 of the City Charter.

§ 13. The Director shall serve as liaison with the Construction industry in New York City. He shall attempt to resolve problems which arise in connection with private construction work by bringing those problems to the attention of the appropriate operating agency for action and providing, where appropriate, assistance in their resolution. Such problems shall be acted upon expeditiously by each agency.

§ 14. The Director shall seek ways to increase the willingness of private contractors to do construction work for the City by meeting with representatives of the construction industry including the building trades on a regular basis.

§ 15. The Director shall consult with a committee or other advisory body established by the Mayor on the capital construction process of the City.

§ 16. All rules, regulations and directives issued by the Director under authority of this executive order shall be binding on all agencies.

§ 17. Executive Order No. 28 dated November 19, 1970, as amended by Executive Order No. 16 dated July 9, 1974, is hereby revoked.

§ 18. This Order shall take effect immediately.

n8-14

EDWARD I. KOCH, Mayor.
