THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 33

December 27, 1991

DEPUTY MAYORS

By the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. There shall be six Deputy Mayors. One shall be designated the First Deputy Mayor, one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development, one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Planning and Development, one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Intergovernmental Relations, one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Public Safety, and one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Health and Human Services.

§2. The First Deputy Mayor shall:

a. Supervise and coordinate the operations of all administrations, departments, agencies, boards, offices, committees, and commissions except as otherwise provided herein.

b. Supervise and coordinate the activities of the Mayor's Office of Operations.

c. Supervise and coordinate the preparation of the City's Revenue, Expense and Capital Budgets and the operations of the Office of Management and Budget.

d. Develop, supervise and coordinate policies and programs relating to personnel and management practices.

e. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Board of Education, the New York City School Construction Authority, the City University of New York, and the Metropolitan Transportation Authority.

f. Succeed to the powers and duties of the "Deputy Mayor - City Administrator of the City" under section 7384 of the Unconsolidated Laws (Chapter 1016 of the Laws of 1969).

g. Coordinate and facilitate implementation of the amendments to the New York City Charter added by vote of the electors at the general election held on November 7, 1989.

h. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not limited to, full power to execute for and on behalf of the Mayor, any agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.

i. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the Mayor, a certificate approving any borrowing of funds or pledge of assets or revenues by the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation which would require the approval of the Mayor pursuant to the "Memorandum of Agreement Between New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation and The City of New York Relating to Operating Expenditures by the Corporation", dated July 1, 1970.

j. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the City, Official Statements of the City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.

k. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

l. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution of contracts, franchises, revocable consents, deeds and satisfactions.

m. Perform any function, power or duty which the Mayor has (and is authorized to delegate) pursuant to New York City Charter sections 217, 219, and 344, and pursuant to Administrative Code section 5-304.

n. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§3. The First Deputy Mayor is hereby delegated the authority to perform all functions, powers or duties of the Mayor which the Mayor is authorized to delegate, in the event that the Mayor is unable to perform such functions, powers or duties for a reason specified in subdivision a of section 10 of the New York City Charter.

§4. The Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development shall:

a. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning and programs designed to implement and enhance the fiscal operations and financial and business management practices of the City.

b. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning, and programs designed to foster the economic growth of the City, including those relating to: commercial and industrial development; telecommunications; energy; foreign trade and investment; government regulation; film, theatre and broadcasting; air, land and sea freight; revenue enhancement; and tax policy and programs.

c. Supervise and coordinate the activities of the Departments of Finance, Employment, Telecommunications and Energy, and Business Services; and the Office of Film, Theatre, and Broadcasting.

d. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Tax Commission and the Industrial Loft Advisory Council.

e. Serve as Chairperson of the Development Funds Steering Committee, the Commercial Incentive Boundary Area Commission, and the Industrial and Commercial Incentive Board.

f. Coordinate the activities of the New York Convention and Visitors' Bureau, the Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation, the Economic Development Corporation, and the New York City Industrial Development Agency.

g. Direct and coordinate the activities of all administrations, departments, agencies, boards, offices, committees and commissions with respect to fiscal, telecommunications and energy policies, planning and programs.

h. Maintain liaison with the New York State Department of Economic Development, New York State Urban Development Corporation, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, the Power Authority of the State of New York, the New York State Public Service Commission, the New York State Municipal Assistance Corporation for the City of New York, the New York State Financial Control Board, the New York City Alliance for International Business, Ltd., and State and Federal agencies and executive offices with respect to matters of City fiscal operations, economic development, and energy and telecommunications policies and programs.

i. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not limited to, full power to execute for and on behalf of the Mayor, any agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.

j. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the Mayor, a certificate approving any borrowing of funds or pledge of assets or revenues by the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation which would require the approval of the Mayor pursuant to the "Memorandum of the Agreement Between New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation and The City of New York Relating to Operating Expenditures by the Corporation", dated July 1, 1970.

k. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the City, Official Statements of the City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.

l. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

m. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution of contracts, franchises, revocable consents, deeds and satisfactions.

n. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§5. The Deputy Mayor for Planning and Development

shall:

a. Supervise and coordinate all land use planning and development activities of the City.

b. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Departments of Environmental Protection, Cultural Affairs, Parks and Recreation, City Planning and Housing Preservation and Development; the Office of Housing Coordination; the Office of Environmental Coordination; and the Office of Special Projects and Events.

c. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the City Planning Commission; the Landmarks Preservation Commission; the Landmark Hardship Review Panel; the Art Commission; the Board of Standards and Appeals; the Loft Board; the Environmental Control Board; and the New York City Housing Authority.

d. Serve as Chairperson of the Waterfront Management Advisory Board.

e. Review the data analyses and estimates of the 1990 Census Project and maintain liaison with the United States Census Bureau and other Federal and State agencies regarding the 1990 Census.

f. Supervise and coordinate the activities of the Community Development Block Grant Application Program.

g. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not limited to, full power to execute for and on behalf of the Mayor, any agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.

h. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the Mayor, a certificate approving any borrowing of funds or pledge of assets or revenues by the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation which would require

the approval of the Mayor pursuant to the
"Memorandum of Agreement Between New York City
Health and Hospitals Corporation and The City of New
York Relating to Operating Expenditures by the
Corporation", dated July 1, 1970.

i. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the City, Official Statements of the City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.

j. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

k. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution of contracts, franchises, revocable consents, deeds and satisfactions.

l. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§6. The Deputy Mayor for Intergovernmental Affairs

shall:

a. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Office of City Legislative Affairs, the Office of State Legislative Affairs, and the Mayor's Office in Washington, D.C.

b. Act on behalf of the Mayor, either directly or through the Office of City Legislative Affairs, the Office of State Legislative Affairs, or the Mayor's Office in Washington, D.C., with respect to all City, State and Federal legislative matters affecting the City; direct the activities of the Mayor's legislative representatives in New York City, Albany, and Washington, D.C.; represent the Mayor before City Council, Congressional and State legislative committees; maintain liaison with the Office of the President and all Federal departments and agencies, the Office of the Governor and all State departments and agencies, and the City Council; and maintain liaison with the New York City Commission for the United Nations and Consular Corps.

c. Serve as the Mayor's representative, either directly or through the Offices of City and State Legislative Affairs, on, and maintain liaison with, regional bodies and intergovernmental agencies operating within the New York metropolitan region.

d. Maintain liaison, either directly or through the Mayor's Office in Washington, D.C., with the United States

Conference of Mayors, the National League of Cities,
the New York Conference of Mayors and other similar
bodies.

e. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Offices
of Minority Affairs, Asian Affairs, Hispanic Affairs,
and Veterans' Affairs; the Office for the Gay and
Lesbian Community; the Mayor's Voluntary Action
Center; the 1990 Census Project; the Community
Assistance Unit; the Commission on the Status of
Women; the City Volunteer Corps; the Community
Development Agency; and the City Commission on
Human Rights.

f. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Board of Elections; the Campaign Finance Board; the Voter Assistance Commission; the Districting Commission; and the Bicentennial Commission.

g. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not limited to, full power to execute any agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.

h. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the Mayor, a certificate approving any borrowing of funds or pledge of assets or revenues by the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation which would require the approval of the Mayor pursuant to the "Memorandum of Agreement Between New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation and the City of New York Relating to Operating Expenditures by the Corporation", dated July 1, 1970.

i. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the City, Official Statements of the City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.

j. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

k. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution of contracts, franchises, revocable consents, deeds and satisfactions.

1. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§7. The Deputy Mayor for Public Safety shall:

a. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning and programs regarding the criminal justice system.

b. Work with the First Deputy Mayor, in coordination with the Office of Management and Budget and the Office of Operations, to ensure the implementation of Mayoral policies regarding the criminal justice system.

c. Supervise inter-agency initiatives intended to improve the functioning and coordination of agencies involved in the criminal justice system, including the Departments of Police, Correction, Probation and Juvenile Justice, the Courts, and the District Attorneys.

d. Be responsible for the implementation of the Court Facilities Master Plan.

e. Oversee the activities of the Mayor's Arson Strike Force and the Office of Drug Abuse Policy.

f. Oversee the implementation of the City's major criminal justice management information systems.

g. Oversee the use of City funds for legal services to indigent defendants and the funding of programs that provide alternatives to incarceration and detention.

h. Be and perform the duties of the Coordinator of Criminal Justice as provided in section 13 of the New York City Charter.

i. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not limited to, full power to execute for

and on behalf of the Mayor, any agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.

j. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the Mayor, a certificate approving any borrowing of funds or pledge of assets or revenues by the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation which would require the approval of the Mayor pursuant to the "Memorandum of Agreement Between New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation and The City of New York Relating to Operating Expenditures by the Corporation", dated July 1, 1970.

k. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the City, Official Statements of the City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.

l. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

m. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution of contracts, franchises, revocable consents, deeds and satisfactions.

n. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§8. The Deputy Mayor for Health and Human Services

shall:

a. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning and programs regarding health and human services.

b. Work with the First Deputy Mayor, in coordination with the Office of Management and Budget and the Office of Operations, to ensure the implementation of Mayoral policies regarding health and human services.

c. Oversee implementation of all plans and programs for housing and assisting homeless individuals in New York City.

d. Supervise and coordinate the activities of the Departments of Youth Services, Health, and Mental Health, Mental Retardation and Alcoholism Services; the Department for the Aging; the Human Resources Administration; the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner; the Office of Homelessness and SRO Housing; the Office of Health Policy; the Office of Family and Children's Services; and the Office for People With Disabilities.

e. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation.

f. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 20 of the Public Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not limited to, full power to execute any agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.

g. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the Mayor, a certificate approving any borrowing of funds or pledge of assets or revenues by the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation which would require the approval of the Mayor pursuant to the "Memorandum of Agreement Between New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation and The City of New York Relating to Operating Expenditures by the Corporation", dated July 1, 1970.

h. Execute and deliver in the name and on behalf of the City, Official Statements of the City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.

i. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

j. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution of contracts, franchises, revocable consents, deeds and satisfactions.

k. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§9. Executive Order No. 6, dated March 12, 1990, and Executive Order No. 28, dated September 17, 1991, are hereby repealed.

§10. Section 1 of prior Executive Order No. 17, dated September 7, 1990, as amended by prior Executive Order No. 28, dated September 17, 1991, is amended to read as follows:

Section 1: **Office for People With Disabilities.** The New York City Mayor's Office for the Handicapped is hereby renamed the Mayor's Office for People With Disabilities. The Office shall report to

and be directly accountable to the Deputy Mayor for Health and Human Services. The Office shall be headed by a Director who shall be appointed by and serve at the pleasure of the Mayor.

§11. This Order shall take effect immediately.

David N. Dinkins
MAYOR

h. Be and perform the duties of the Coordinator of Criminal Justice as provided in section 13 of the New York City Charter.

i. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not limited to, full power to execute for

and on behalf of the Mayor, any agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.

j. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the Mayor, a certificate approving any borrowing of funds or pledge of assets or revenues by the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation which would require the approval of the Mayor pursuant to the "Memorandum of Agreement Between New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation and The City of New York Relating to Operating Expenditures by the Corporation", dated July 1, 1970.

k. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the City, Official Statements of the City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.

l. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

m. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution of contracts, franchises, revocable consents, deeds and satisfactions.

n. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§8. The Deputy Mayor for Health and Human Services

shall:

a. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning and programs regarding health and human services.

b. Work with the First Deputy Mayor, in coordination with the Office of Management and Budget and the Office of Operations, to ensure the implementation of Mayoral policies regarding health and human services.

c. Oversee implementation of all plans and programs for housing and assisting homeless individuals in New York City.

d. Supervise and coordinate the activities of the Departments of Youth Services, Health, and Mental Health, Mental Retardation and Alcoholism Services; the Department for the Aging; the Human Resources Administration; the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner; the Office of Homelessness and SRO Housing; the Office of Health Policy; the Office of Family and Children's Services; and the Office for People With Disabilities.

e. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation.

f. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 20 of the Public Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not limited to, full power to execute any agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.

g. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the Mayor, a certificate approving any borrowing of funds or pledge of assets or revenues by the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation which would require the approval of the Mayor pursuant to the "Memorandum of Agreement Between New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation and The City of New York Relating to Operating Expenditures by the Corporation", dated July 1, 1970.

h. Execute and deliver in the name and on behalf of the City, Official Statements of the City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.

i. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

j. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution of contracts, franchises, revocable consents, deeds and satisfactions.

k. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§9. Executive Order No. 6, dated March 12, 1990, and Executive Order No. 28, dated September 17, 1991, are hereby repealed.

§10. Section 1 of prior Executive Order No. 17, dated September 7, 1990, as amended by prior Executive Order No. 28, dated September 17, 1991, is amended to read as follows:

Section 1: **Office for People With Disabilities.** The New York City Mayor's Office for the Handicapped is hereby renamed the Mayor's Office for People With Disabilities. The Office shall report to

and be directly accountable to the Deputy Mayor for Health and Human Services. The Office shall be headed by a Director who shall be appointed by and serve at the pleasure of the Mayor.

§11. This Order shall take effect immediately.

David N. Dinkins
MAYOR

HIV HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES PLANNING COUNCIL
(Amendment of Executive Order No. 23, dated 1/18/91)

By the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is
hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. Prior Order Amended. Section 3 of Executive Order No.

23, dated January 18, 1991, is hereby amended to read as follows:

Section 3. Membership. (a) The Planning Council shall be appointed by the Mayor and shall consist of not less than 35 and not more than 45 members. The members of the Planning Council shall serve at the pleasure of the Mayor and from among them, the Mayor shall designate a Chairperson.

(b) The membership of the Planning Council shall include representatives of health care providers, community-based and AIDS service organizations, social service providers, mental health care providers, local public health agencies, hospital planning agencies or health care planning agencies, affected communities (including individuals with HIV/AIDS), non-elected community leaders, State government, grantees of categorical grants for early

intervention services under subpart II of part C of
the Ryan White Act and the lead agency of any
Health Resources and Services Administration
adult and pediatric HIV-related care
demonstration project operating in the area to be
served. At least one member of the Planning
Council shall represent separately each of these
specified categories.

(c) Twenty-five (25) percent of the positions on the Planning Council shall be allocated to individuals with HIV/AIDS.

(d) the Mayor also shall appoint one member
that is mutually acceptable to the Mayor and the
County Executives of Westchester, Rockland and
Putnam Counties to represent these political
subdivisions or Health Resources and Services
Administration grant recipients therein on the
Planning Council.

(e) The Planning Council shall also include as
members the Commissioner of Mental Health,
Mental Retardation, and Alcoholism Services of
the City of New York, the Commissioner of
Health of the City of New York, the
Administrator of the New York City Human
Resources Administration, the Director of the
Office of Management and Budget of the City of
New York, and the President of the Health and
Hospital Corporation, or their designees. Such
designees must be at least an Assistant
Commissioner or the equivalent of the agency.

(f) The Mayor shall designate alternates for
members of the Planning Council who serve as
individuals with HIV/AIDS to serve in the
member's place if as a result of his or her illness
the member cannot perform the duties of a
Planning Council member.

(g) With respect to all members of the Planning Council other than those enumerated in subsections (e) and (f), the Planning Council may determine that such members may designate an alternate to serve as a non-voting participant in the Planning Council on the occasion of the member's absence.

(h) There must be at least one member of the Planning Council from each of New York City's boroughs.

(i) The following shall serve as non-voting, ex officio representatives to the Planning Council: Director of Mayor's Office on Special Needs Housing, Director of Mayor's Office on Drug Abuse Policy, Commissioner of Human Rights of the City of New York, Commissioner of Aging of the City of New York, Director of Mayor's Office of Operations, a representative from the Mayor's Office for People with Disabilities, and a representative from the Mayor's Office on Homelessness and SRO Housing.

(j) In the event of a vacancy, the Planning Council may within thirty (30) days after the vacancy occurs recommend to the Mayor the names of three individuals who would satisfy the relevant qualifying criteria to fill that vacancy.

Section 2. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

title: MAYOR’S ADVISORY BOARD TO PROMOTE FAIR HOUSING
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 37

MAY 7, 1992

MAYOR'S ADVISORY BOARD TO PROMOTE FAIR HOUSING

WHEREAS, fair housing and fair lending is essential to the City's growth and
prosperity; and

WHEREAS, notwithstanding substantial efforts by the City to combat housing
discrimination, the residents of New York City still encounter barriers which limit equal
access to housing; and

WHEREAS, the Federal Fair Housing Act and State and City human rights
laws prohibit housing discrimination; and

WHEREAS, equal housing opportunity cannot be realized until the principles
of fair housing are fully accepted by the real estate and building industries, appraisal forms,
financial institutions, property owners' associations, local government officials, and citizens;
and

WHEREAS, in order to bring together all of the diverse segments of the City
to prevent housing discrimination, it is necessary to create an advisory board to promote fair
housing;

NOW THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New
York it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. **Creation of Advisory Board**

There is hereby established an Advisory Board to Promote Fair Housing ("Advisory Board") as successor to the NYC Fair Housing Task Force. The Advisory Board shall report to and be directly accountable to the Mayor.

Section 2. Membering of Advisory Board

a. The Advisory Board shall be chaired jointly by the Commissioners of the City Commission on Human Rights and of the Department of Housing Preservation and Development, or their designees.

b. The following City agencies and divisions of the Office of the Mayor shall participate in the Advisory Board: The Department of Finance, the Human Resources Administration, the Department for the Aging, the Mayor's Office for People with Disabilities, the Mayor's Community Assistance Unit, and the Mayor's Offices of Constituency Affairs. The New York City Housing Authority shall also be requested to participate in the Advisory Board.

c. The Advisory Board shall also include representatives of the banking or lending community, the real estate industry, fair housing or civil rights groups, and religious organizations appointed by the Mayor. Such members shall be appointed for a term of three years and shall serve without compensation.

d. The Speaker of the City Council shall be requested to appoint a representative of the City Council to participate in the Advisory Board.

Section 3. Functions of Advisory Board

The Advisory Board shall advise the Mayor with respect to all fair housing issues affecting the City and shall:

a. formulate and recommend policies and programs to further equal housing opportunity;

b. foster coordination among City, state and federal agencies, and other organizations and institutions, both public and private, with respect to fair housing activities;

c. promote public awareness and education relating to fair housing and make recommendations regarding the provision of information and referral services, and procedures for the speedy resolution of complaints concerning fair housing;

d. locate and utilize funding sources, both public and private, in order to assist in the implementation of the provisions of this Order;

e. assist the City Commission on Human Rights in promoting the enforcement of fair housing laws;

f. promote volunteer assistance so as to provide legal representation for fair housing complainants;

g. appoint a Resource Council to assist the Advisory Board in the design and implementation of a fair housing program. The Resource Council shall include representatives from the Office of Management and Budget, the Law Department, and the City Planning Commission, as well as persons in the private and not-for-profit sectors who possess expertise in promoting fair housing. The members of the Resource Council shall serve without compensation and at the pleasure of the Advisory Board;

h. compile data and statistics regarding fair housing in New York City and submit its findings to the Mayor; and

i. perform such other functions as the Mayor may direct.

Section 4. The heads of all City departments and agencies shall cooperate with and assist the Advisory Board.

Section 5. This Order shall take effect immediately.

title: THE NEW YORK CITY PROCUREMENT TRAINING INSTITUTE
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 38

JUNE 11, 1992

THE NEW YORK CITY PROCUREMENT TRAINING INSTITUTE

WHEREAS, the 1989 Charter amendments and the rules of the Procurement Policy Board adopted pursuant thereto have established a new, uniform system for the procurement of goods, services and construction by City agencies; and

WHEREAS, the Mayor, acting through the City Chief Procurement Officer, is responsible for coordination and implementation of the City's procurement function; and

WHEREAS, the training and professionalization of City agency procurement personnel is essential to fully implement this new procurement system, to improve purchasing decisions, and to produce savings to the City;

NOW THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. a. **Creation of the Institute.** There is hereby established a New York City Procurement Training Institute.

Section 2. **Functions of the Institute.** The functions of the Institute shall include:

a. establishing training and education programs for City personnel in professional skills necessary for procurement of goods, services and construction by City agencies, including but not limited to: City procurement policies and procedures, specification development, procurement methods,

negotiation techniques, cost and price analysis, procurement research, contract administration, and implementation of the requirements governing participation by minority-owned and woman-owned business enterprises in City procurement;

b. providing programs leading to professional certification of City procurement personnel in procurement management; and

c. developing educational materials regarding contracting ethics and promoting other efforts to instill standards of excellence in City procurement.

Section 3. Training Institute Board

a. The Institute shall be governed by a Board consisting of the Deputy City Personnel Director for Personnel Development of the Department of Personnel, who shall serve as Chair, the Director of the Mayor's Office of Contracts, and a member of the public having substantial expertise in procurement management to be appointed by the Mayor for a two-year term upon the recommendation of the Procurement Policy Board. Such public member shall serve without salary, except that he or she shall be entitled to reimbursement for actual and necessary expenses incurred in the performance of official duties as a member of the Institute Board and shall also receive a per diem allowance when rendering services for the Institute Board at a rate established by the Mayor.

b. The Institute Board shall have the following powers and duties:

1. to select a Training Institute Administrator who shall be responsible for the day-to-day activities of the Institute;

2. to adopt standards, policies and procedures to guide the Institute in all of its programs and activities;

3. to develop the curriculum for Institute training and education programs;

4. to establish the selection process for Institute contracts for the development of course materials and for instructors of courses offered by the Institute;

5. to evaluate the success of Institute training and education programs and the performance of Institute instructors; and

6. to develop other programs and professional development opportunities in furtherance of the purposes of this Order.

Section 4. **Agency Assistance.** The Department of Personnel shall assist the Institute in the administration of its training and education programs and shall award and administer all contracts for instructors and other services necessary for the Institute to conduct its activities. The Mayor's Office of Contracts shall identify attendees for Institute training and education programs, assess training needs for city personnel, and coordinate the activities of the Institute with existing training and education programs conducted by City agencies.

Section 5. **Effective Date.** This Order shall take effect immediately.

title: ESTABLISHMENT OF AN AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT TASK FORCE
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 39

JUNE 23, 1992

ESTABLISHMENT OF AN AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT TASK FORCE

WHEREAS, Congress enacted the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 to prohibit the exclusion of people with disabilities from jobs, services, activities and other benefits. The Americans with Disabilities Act applies this prohibition of discrimination against people with disabilities to all activities of state and local governments. To ensure the City's compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, it is necessary to facilitate an effective means of cooperation, communication and coordination among the various agencies of the City.

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as the Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

1. <u>Task Force Established.</u> There is hereby established an Americans with Disabilities Act Task Force, to be convened by the Mayor's Office of Operations. The Task Force shall report to and be directly accountable to the First Deputy Mayor.

2. **Membership.** The Task Force shall consist of the Director of the Mayor's Office for People with Disabilities, the Director of the Mayor's Office of Operations, the Corporation Counsel, the Office of the Director of Construction, the Commissioner of the Department of Buildings, the Director of the Mayor's Office of Transportation, the Commissioner of the Department of Transportation, the Chairperson of the City Commission on Human Rights, the City Personnel Director, the Commissioner of the Department of General Services and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget.

3. **Purpose.** The Task Force shall be responsible for formulating City policies regarding compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, and for overseeing the implementation of such policies. The Task Force shall consult with and assist other City agencies when necessary to effectuate compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act.

4. The subjects to be addressed by the Task Force shall include the requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act with respect to:

(a) The hiring of persons with disabilities;

(b) The provision of reasonable accommodations to employees with disabilities;

(c) City agencies' self-evaluations of their services, programs, policies and procedures and their plans to address any problems identified in the self-evaluation process;

(d) City agencies' transition plans for making any structural changes necessary in order to ensure accessibility to people with disabilities; and

(e) City agencies' obligations with respect to City property leased to other persons.

5. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

title: COMMISSION TO INVESTIGATE ALLEGATIONS OF POLICE CORRUPTION AND THE ANTI-CORRUPTION PROCEDURES OF THE POLICE DEPARTMENT
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 42

July 24, 1992

COMMISSION TO INVESTIGATE ALLEGATIONS OF
POLICE CORRUPTION AND THE ANTI-CORRUPTION
PROCEDURES OF THE POLICE DEPARTMENT

WHEREAS, an honest and efficient police force is essential to the well-being of the City and the implementation of the Police Department's innovative community policing strategies; and

WHEREAS, during the next two years the Safe Streets, Safe City Program will add more than two thousand officers to the Police Department of the City of New York, most of whom will be assigned to patrol the streets of the City; and

WHEREAS, allegations of corruption have been made against some members of the Police Department, and the effectiveness of the practices, procedures and methods used by the Police Department to prevent and detect misconduct and to maintain integrity have been questioned; and

WHEREAS, an investigation by the Police Department of those allegations would be subject to question by the public; and

WHEREAS, the misdeeds of a few must not be allowed to sully or taint the reputations and sacrifices of the vast majority of honest and dedicated men and women who serve on the police force;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Establishment of Commission. There is hereby established a Commission to (1) inquire into and evaluate the existing

practices, procedures and methods for investigating specific
allegations of corruption and the existing practices, procedures and
methods designed to prevent corruption and maintain integrity; (2)
recommend improvements in these practices, procedures and methods
and make any additional recommendations that will ensure the
integrity of the Police Department and prevent corruption; (3) take
evidence and hold whatever hearings, public and private, the
Commission may deem appropriate to ascertain the necessary facts.

Section 2. Members. The Commission shall consist of the
following persons, who shall serve without compensation, and who are
hereby appointed, as members thereof: Milton Mollen, Chairperson;
Harold Baer, Jr.; Herbert Evans; Roderick C. Lankler; and Harold
Tyler.

Section 3. Powers. (a) The Commission, its Chair and
such agents as the Chair shall designate, shall have all powers
necessary to conduct as complete an investigation as it finds
necessary, including but not limited to the powers to administer oaths
and affirmations, to examine witnesses in public or private hearings,
to receive evidence and to preside at or conduct such hearings and
investigations.

(b) The Commission, its Chair and such agents as the Chair shall designate shall be designated by the Commissioner of Investigation as agents of the Department of Investigation, pursuant to Section 805 of the City Charter, with all powers to conduct investigations as provided therein.

(c) The Chair of the Commission shall be appointed a Deputy Commissioner of Investigation, pursuant to Section 802 of the City Charter, with all powers pertaining to that office, including but not limited to those specified in Section 805(a) of the City Charter.

(d) The Commission may also cooperate with any criminal
investigation, as may become necessary, pursuant to its powers under
this Order.

(e) Within the scope of the general responsibility of the
Commission set forth in Section 1 of this Order, the Commission shall
have authority to examine and copy any document or other record

¹ Upon his retirement as a Justice of the Supreme Court of the State of New York.

prepared, maintained or held by the Police Department of the City of
New York, and any other agency of the City, except those documents
or other records which cannot be so disclosed according to law.

(f) The Commission shall have authority to require any member of the uniformed force or any other officer or employee or any former member of the uniformed force or any other former officer or employee of the Police Department of the City of New York or of any other agency of the City to attend an examination or hearing concerning any matter related to the performance of his or her official duties, and to require any person dealing with, or who has dealt with, the Police Department of the City of New York or its officers and employees to attend any examination or hearing concerning such dealings, and to require any person who has or may have knowledge relating to any matter within the jurisdiction of the Commission to attend any examination or hearing concerning such matter. If any member of the uniformed force or any other officer or employee of the Police Department of the City of New York or of any other agency of the City, or any person dealing with the Police Department of the City of New York declines to answer any question which is put to him or her, the Commission shall have the authority to advise the person that neither his nor her answer nor any information or evidence derived therefrom will be used against him or her in a subsequent criminal prosecution other than for perjury arising from such testimony. The refusal of any member of the uniformed force or any other officer or employee of the Police Department of the City of New York or of any other agency of the City of New York to answer questions on the condition described in this paragraph shall constitute cause for removal from office or employment, or other appropriate penalty. The refusal of any person dealing with the Police Department of the City of New York to answer questions on the condition described in this paragraph shall, pursuant to the appropriate provision of any contract, constitute cause for cancellation or termination of such contract with the Police Department of the City of New York or the City and its agencies that said person or any firm, partnership or corporation of which he or she is a member, partner, director or officer has entered into. The Police Department of the City of New York and the City and its agencies shall not incur any penalty or damages because of such cancellation or termination.

Section 4. Cooperation with Investigation. (a) Pursuant
to my power as Mayor all heads of departments or agencies of the
City shall make every reasonable effort to insure the full cooperation
of all persons employed or supervised by them with investigations or
inquiries conducted by the Commission.

(b) All departments or agencies of the City shall make available to the Commission such facilities, services, personnel and other assistance as may be necessary for the conduct of its investigations.

(c) All departments or agencies of the City shall provide to the Commission upon request any and all documents, records, reports, files or other information relating to any matter within the jurisdiction of the Commission, except such documents as cannot be so disclosed according to law. To insure full availability of such documents, records, reports, files or other information to the Commission, all City departments and agencies shall make and retain copies of any documents, records, reports, files or other information provided to state or federal prosecutors, or other investigative bodies, pursuant to subpoena or otherwise.

(d) All officers and employees of the City shall cooperate fully with the Commission. Interference with or obstruction of the Commission's investigations or other functions shall constitute cause for removal from office or employment, or other appropriate penalty.

(e) All officers and employees of the City shall have the affirmative obligation to report, directly and without undue delay, to the Commission, any and all information concerning conduct which they know or should reasonably know to involve corrupt or other criminal activity (i) by any member of the uniformed force or any other officer or employee of the Police Department, which concerns his or her office or employment, or (ii) by persons dealing with the Police Department, which concerns their dealing with the Department, and shall proceed in accordance with the Commission's directions. The knowing failure of any officer or employee to so report shall constitute cause for removal from office or employment, or other appropriate penalty.

(f) The obligation to report information regarding corruption or criminal activity to the Commission shall be in addition to the reporting obligations imposed on City officers and employees to report such information to the Department of Investigation, pursuant to Executive Order No. 105, dated December 20, 1986.

Section 5. Construction with Other Laws. Nothing in this Order shall be construed to limit the powers and duties of any department or agency under the City Charter or as otherwise provided by law.

Section 6. Effective Date. This order shall take effect immediately.

David N. Dinkins
MAYOR

title: THE MAYOR’S OFFICE FOR HOMELESS FACILITIES AND SERVICE DEVELOPMENT
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 43

DECEMBER 2, 1992

THE MAYOR'S OFFICE FOR HOMELESS FACILITIES
AND SERVICE DEVELOPMENT

WHEREAS, over the last three years, this administration has allocated extensive resources towards addressing the needs of homeless families and individuals in the City of New York, including the provision of permanent housing to 15,000 homeless families and quadrupling the number of transitional housing units, and

WHEREAS, in furtherance of this commitment and consistent with recommendations made by the New York City Commission on Homelessness established by the Mayor, and in an effort to provide assistance to the homeless in the most effective and efficient manner, the Mayor will propose legislation to create a new agency whose function will be to provide City services to homeless families and individuals, expedite the construction of transitional housing for the homeless, and transfer the operation of such housing to not-for-profit organizations, and

WHEREAS, the creation of this new City agency will require extensive planning and coordination with various City, State and federal entities as well as the enactment of a local law, and

WHEREAS, in order to begin immediately the improvement of the
development of facilities, and provision of services for homeless families and individuals and
to plan for and oversee the transition to the new agency, it is necessary to establish an
interim Mayoral Office;

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the power vested in me as Mayor of the
City of New York, it is hereby ordered;

Section 1. **Office for Homeless Facilities and Service Development.** There
is hereby established in the Office of the Mayor the Office for Homeless Facilities and
Service Development which shall be headed by a Director who shall be appointed by and
serve at the pleasure of the Mayor. The Office shall report to and be directly accountable
to the Deputy Mayor for Health and Human Services.

Section 2. **Responsibilities of the Office.** Until such time as the new agency
is created, the Office shall, in consultation with the Human Resources Administration
(HRA), the Department of Housing Preservation and Development and other agencies
involved in the provision of services for homeless families and individuals, and consistent
with law, (1) oversee and direct on behalf of the Mayor the actions necessary for the
establishment of a new City agency to manage the delivery of services to homeless families
and individuals, (2) participate in the planning and implementation of the redesigning and
restructuring of the current system for the provision of services and facilities for homeless
families and individuals, (3) make recommendations to HRA concerning the planning and
development of and contracting for services and facilities for homeless families and
individuals, and (4) encourage the participation of and receive proposals from the public and

the private sectors for the development of services and facilities for homeless families and individuals, including the evaluation and negotiation of such proposals and the obtaining of the necessary approvals therefor.

Section 3. In carrying out its responsibilities, the Office shall have the following functions:

(1) to oversee the planning, design and siting of all new facilities for homeless families and individuals;

(2) to make recommendations to and assist HRA in the development of all new contracts for the provision of services and facilities for the homeless, including drafting requests for proposals, evaluating the responses thereto, drafting and negotiating contracts with providers, administering contracts and monitoring performance under the contracts;

(3) to participate in the development and coordination of City policy related to homelessness, in consultation with the Mayor's Office on Homelessness and Single Room Occupancy (SRO) Housing Services;;

(4) to assist in the development of programs designed to improve access of homeless families and individuals to existing private sector housing;

(5) to encourage the participation of the private sector in the development of safe and affordable transitional housing for homeless families and individuals; and

(6) to facilitate the acquisition, rehabilitation and construction of transitional housing for homeless families and individuals.

title: DESIGNATION OF THE RESPONSIBLE AGENCY FOR FRANCHISES TO BE AWARDED PURSUANT TO THE CITY CHARTER
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 44

DECEMBER 3, 1992

DESIGNATION OF THE RESPONSIBLE AGENCY FOR FRANCHISES
TO BE AWARDED PURSUANT TO THE CITY CHARTER

By the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is
hereby ordered:

Section 1: Pursuant to §§363 and 378 of the New York City Charter:

(a) The Department of Transportation is designated the responsible agency for the following types of franchises --

(1) Bus lines,

(2) Bus stop shelters,

(3) Electric power distribution systems,

(4) Tramways,

(5) Below grade passenger railroad tacks and tunnels,

(6) Self-cleaning automatic public toilets.

(b) The Department of Business Services is designated the responsible agency for the following types of franchises --

(1) Railroad freight and shipping lines,

(2) Refrigeration distribution systems.

Section 2: Pursuant to Chapter 48 of the New York City Charter, the Department of Telecommunications and Energy shall be the responsible agency for franchises relating to telecommunications as defined in that Chapter.

Section 3: Executive Order No. 8 of 1990 is hereby repealed.

Section 4: This Order shall take effect immediately.

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 47

January 4, 1993

OFFICE OF FILM, THEATRE AND
BROADCASTING

By the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Continuation of Office of Film, Theatre and Broadcasting. There is continued within the Office of the Mayor an Office of Film, Theatre and Broadcasting, to be headed by a commissioner who shall be appointed by and serve at the pleasure of the Mayor. MAYOR

title: DOMESTIC PARTNERSHIP REGISTRATION PROGRAM
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

Executive Order No. 48

January 7, 1993

DOMESTIC PARTNERSHIP REGISTRATION PROGRAM

WHEREAS, significant changes in our society have resulted in the creation of diverse living arrangements and the development of an expanded concept of the family unit; and

WHEREAS, many of these living arrangements involve long-term committed relationships between unmarried persons; and

WHEREAS, it is appropriate to provide a means of recognizing persons with such committed and sharing relationships;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Establishment of a Domestic Partnership Registration Program. A procedure for the registration and termination of domestic partnerships with the City Clerk is hereby established in accordance with the provisions of this Executive Order.

Section 2. Domestic Partnership Defined. Domestic partners are two people, both of whom are eighteen years of age or older, neither of whom is married or related by blood in a

manner that would bar their marriage in New York State, who have
a close and committed personal relationship, who live together
and have been living together on a continuous basis, who have
registered as domestic partners and have not terminated the
domestic partnership in accordance with Section 4 of this
Executive Order.

Section 3. Domestic Partnership Registration. Persons
may register as domestic partners if they are residents of the
City of New York or at least one partner is employed by the City
on the date of registration. In order to register, persons shall
execute a domestic partnership registration certificate and
submit it to the City Clerk, who shall maintain a registry of
domestic partnerships. No person shall be eligible to register
as a domestic partner who at the time of registration or at any
time during the prior six months was registered as a member of
another domestic partnership.

Section 4. Termination of Domestic Partnership. A
domestic partner may terminate a registered domestic partnership
by filing a termination statement with the City Clerk. The
person filing the termination statement shall declare that the
domestic partnership is terminated and if the termination
statement has not been signed by both domestic partners, that the
other domestic partner has been notified of such termination by
registered mail, return receipt requested.

Section 5. Confidentiality of Domestic Partnership
Information. The City Clerk shall establish procedures to ensure

the confidentiality of domestic partnership registrations.
Nothing herein shall be construed to prohibit the publication of
statistics pertaining to domestic partnerships which have been
registered by the City Clerk, provided that appropriate measures
are taken to prevent identification of persons registered.

Section 6. Nothing in this Executive Order shall be deemed to supersede, alter, affect or conflict with any applicable City, State or Federal laws or rules.

Section 7. Executive Order No. 123, dated August 7, 1989, is hereby superseded, provided, however, that "Affidavits of Domestic Partnership for Bereavement Leave" which were previously filed in accordance with prior Executive Order No. 123 shall remain in force and effect unless terminated in accordance with procedures established by the Department of Personnel pursuant to that Executive Order. Registration pursuant to Executive Order No. 123 shall not preclude persons from registering as domestic partners pursuant to this Executive Order.

Section 8. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect March 1, 1993.

title: CITY POLICIES APPLICABLE TO DOMESTIC PARTNERSHIPS
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

Executive Order No. 49

January 7, 1993

CITY POLICIES APPLICABLE TO DOMESTIC PARTNERSHIPS

Section 1. Any person who has registered his or her domestic partnership with the City of New York in accordance with the provisions of Executive Order No. 48, dated January 7, 1993, shall be entitled to benefits in accordance with the provisions of this Order, and with respect to employees of the City, continue to receive existing time and leave benefits afforded pursuant to applicable law, rule or collective bargaining agreement.

Section 2. Bereavement Leave for Domestic Partners
Continued. Any City employee who has registered his or her domestic partnership in accordance with the provisions of Executive Order No. 48, dated January 7, 1993, shall be entitled to bereavement leave in the event of the death of a domestic partner, or the death of a parent or child of such domestic partner, or the death of a relative of such domestic partner residing in the household. Such leave shall be afforded in accordance with existing rules and the terms of that Order. All "Affidavits of Domestic Partnership for Bereavement Leave" which were previously filed in accordance with prior Executive Order

No. 123 shall remain in force and effect unless the domestic partnership established pursuant to that Order has been terminated.

Section 3. Child Care Leave of Absence Without Pay.
Any City employee who has registered his or her domestic partnership in accordance with the provisions of Executive Order No. 48, dated January 7, 1993, shall be entitled to Child Care Leave of Absence Without Pay when his or her domestic partner becomes the parent of a child either by birth or adoption. Such leave shall be granted on the same basis as provided by the child care leave provisions of the Career and Salary Plan, the Citywide Agreement or any other collective bargaining agreement.

Section 4. Visitation Rights in City Correctional and Juvenile Detention Facilities. Any person who has registered his or her domestic partnership in accordance with the provisions of Executive Order No. 48, dated January 7, 1993, and his or her domestic partner, shall have the right to visit each other and each other's family members in accordance with the visitation policies established by the New York City Department of Correction and the New York City Department of Juvenile Justice which are applicable to family members of persons in incarceration or detention facilities operated by either such agency.

Section 5. Visitation Rights in Health Care and Hospitals Facilities. By agreement of the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation, any person who has registered his or

her domestic partnership in accordance with the provisions of Executive Order No. 48, dated January 7, 1993, and his or her domestic partner, shall have the right to visit each other and each other's family members in accordance with the visitation policies established by HHC which are applicable to family members of persons who are patients in health care and hospital facilities operated by HHC.

**Section 6. Occupancy Rights for New York City Housing Authority Tenants.** By agreement of the New York City Housing Authority, registration as a domestic partnership in accordance with the provisions of Executive Order No. 48, dated January 7, 1993, shall be considered evidence in determining whether an eligible person qualifies as a family member entitled to be added to an existing tenancy as a permanent resident, in accordance with the policy of the Authority. When a domestic partner seeks on the basis of the domestic partnership to avail himself or herself of occupancy rights pursuant to such policy, the Authority may require the domestic partner to provide to the agency a certification from the City Clerk that he/she is currently registered as a domestic partner.

**Section 7. Succession Rights for Persons in Buildings Supervised By or Under the Jurisdiction of the New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development.** Registration of a domestic partnership in accordance with the provisions of Executive Order No. 48, dated January 7, 1993, shall be considered evidence in determining whether an eligible person

qualifies as a family member entitled to succeed to the tenancy or occupancy rights of a tenant/cooperator pursuant to rules governing persons in buildings supervised by or under the jurisdiction of the New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development. When a domestic partner seeks on the basis of the domestic partnership to avail himself or herself of tenancy or occupancy rights pursuant to such rules, the Department may require the domestic partner to provide to the agency a certification from the City Clerk that he/she is currently registered as a domestic partner.

Section 8. Nothing in this Executive Order shall be deemed to supersede, alter, affect or conflict with any applicable City, State or Federal law or rules.

Section 9. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect March 1, 1993.

David N. Dinkins
MAYOR

title: INTEGRATED CONTRACT AND PROCUREMENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 50

January 22, 1993

INTEGRATED CONTRACT AND PROCUREMENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM

WHEREAS, the City desires to more effectively manage and streamline the contracting and procurement process for necessary goods, services and construction, and to improve efficiency and cost-effectiveness in procurement; and

WHEREAS, in order to advance these goals it has been determined that a comprehensive automated contract management system, to be known as the Integrated Contract and Procurement Management System (the "ICPMS"), should be created; and

WHEREAS, in order to facilitate the operation of the ICPMS, it is desirable to establish a governing structure to ensure that the ICPMS effectively supports the procurement function:

NOW THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered that:

Section 1. **Integrated Contract and Procurement Management System Established**

a. There shall be established within the Mayor's Office of Contracts an Integrated Contract and Procurement Management System (known as the "ICPMS") which shall, to the maximum extent possible, computerize and automate all aspects of the contracting and procurement processes of City agencies.

b. The Mayor's Office of Contracts shall be responsible for the ICPMS, including operation and maintenance, personnel and staffing, and all other activities necessary for the achievement of its mission.

c. The ICPMS shall provide support for all aspects of City procurement, and shall have the capacity to compile and process information regarding vendor registration, solicitation and award processes, vendor selection, contract registration, contract administration, performance monitoring, vouchering, payments and any other pertinent management information concerning the contracting and procurement activities of City agencies.

d. The ICPMS shall also contain an electronic data interchange component that will permit vendors to access information on contract opportunities, download solicitation documents, submit invoices, and receive payment electronically.

e. The ICPMS shall be accessible to the public at a central location to allow review of such standard information regarding each City contract and contractors as is required to be available for public examination pursuant to Charter Section 1064 and the Rules of the Procurement Policy Board.

Section 2. Integrated Contract and Procurement Management System Policy Board Established

a. There is hereby established an Integrated Contract and Procurement Management System Policy Board (the "ICPMS Board").

b. The ICPMS Board shall consist of six members. Three members shall be appointed by the Mayor, two shall be appointed by the Comptroller, and one ex-officio (non-voting) member shall be a representative of the Procurement Policy Board. Each member shall serve at the pleasure of his or her appointing authority.

c. The Director of the Mayor's Office of Contracts shall serve as Chair of the ICPMS Board.

d. The ICPMS Board shall be responsible for the establishment of policy regarding the design, development and operation of the ICPMS. The ICPMS Board shall act by majority vote of the members entitled to vote, except that the vote of four members entitled to vote shall be necessary for all policy decision concerning: (i) the collection, utilization and reporting of data on City contracts and contractors; (ii) the payment process, and other financial transactions; (iii) linkages with any other relevant automated information systems; and (iv) the internal management controls of the ICPMS.

e. The ICPMS Board, acting in consultation with the Procurement Policy Board as appropriate, shall promulgate such guidelines and procedures as may be necessary and appropriate to effectuate the purposes of this Order.

Section 3. This Order shall take effect immediately.

title: HIV HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES PLANNING COUNCIL
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 51

JANUARY 25 1993

HIV HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES PLANNING COUNCIL

(Amendment of Executive Order No. 23, dated 1/18/91)

By the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby
ordered as follows:

Section 1. Prior Order Amended. Section 3 of Executive Order No. 23, dated January 18, 1991, as amended by Executive Order No. 36, dated February 5, 1992, is hereby amended to read as follows:

Section 3. Membership. (a) The Planning Council shall be appointed by the Mayor and shall consist of not less than 35 and not more than 45 members, exclusive of those non-voting, ex officio members appointed pursuant to subsection (i). The members of the Planning Council and any alternates that are designated to serve as voting participants of the Planning Council pursuant to subsection (g) shall serve at the pleasure of the Mayor. From among the members of the Planning Council, the Mayor shall designate a Chairperson.

(b) Each member of the Planning Council other than those persons enumerated in subsections (e), (f) and (i) shall be appointed for two year terms, except that of the members first appointed, half shall be appointed for terms of one year and half shall be appointed for terms of two years. No such member

shall serve for more than two consecutive two year
terms.

(c) The membership of the Planning Council shall include representatives of health care providers, community-based and AIDS service organizations, social service providers, mental health care providers, local public health agencies, hospital planning agencies or health care planning agencies, affected communities (including individuals with HIV/AIDS), non-elected community leaders, State government, grantees of categorical grants for early intervention services under subpart II of part C of the Ryan White Act and the lead agency of any Health Resources and Services Administration adult and pediatric HIV-related care demonstration project operating in the area to be served. At least one member of the Planning Council shall represent separately each of these specified categories.

(d) Twenty-five (25) percent of the positions on the Planning Council shall be allocated to individuals with HIV/AIDS.

(e) The Mayor also shall appoint one member that is mutually acceptable to the Mayor and the County Executives of Westchester, Rockland and Putnam Counties to represent these political subdivisions or Health Resources and Services Administration grant recipients therein on the Planning Council.

(f) The Planning Council shall also include as members the Commissioner of Mental Health, Mental Retardation, and Alcoholism Services of the City of New York, the Commissioner of Health of the City of New York, the Administrator of the New York City Human Resources Administration, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget of the City of New York, and the President of the Health and Hospital Corporation.

(g) All members of the Planning Council may designate an alternate to serve as a voting participant

in the Planning Council on the occasion of the member's absence. Such alternates must be approved by the Chairperson of the Planning Council.

(h) There must be at least one member of the Planning Council from each of New York City's boroughs.

(i) The following shall serve as non-voting, ex officio members of the Planning Council: Director of Mayor's Office on Special Needs Housing, Director of Mayor's Office on Drug Abuse Policy, Chairperson of the City Human Rights Commission, Commissioner of Aging of the City of New York, Director of Mayor's Office of Operations, Director of Mayor's Office for People with Disabilities, and Director of Mayor's Office on Homelessness and Single Room Occupancy Housing Services.

(j) In the event of a vacancy, the Planning Council may within thirty (30) days after the vacancy occurs recommend to the Mayor the names of three individuals who would satisfy the relevant qualifying criteria to fill that vacancy.

Section 2. Executive Order No. 23, dated January 18, 1991, is amended by renumbering Sections 6 and 7 thereof as Sections 8 and 9, respectively, and adding new Sections 6 and 7 to read as follows:

Section 6. **Reporting Requirements.** The Planning Council shall report all of its decisions and recommendations to the Mayor through the Deputy Mayor for Health and Human Services. In addition, the Planning Council shall submit an annual report to the Mayor on the delivery of services under Title I of the Ryan White Act. Such report shall also contain the Planning Council's recommendations regarding the delivery of such services under Title I of the Ryan White Act as well as the delivery of other HIV/AIDS services needed to effect a comprehensive continuum of care for persons impacted by the HIV/AIDS epidemic.

Section 7. Staff. The Planning Council may
recommend and shall be provided with such paid
staff members as are approved by the Mayor.

Section 3. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

DAVID N. DINKINS
MAYOR

(i) The following shall serve as non-voting, ex officio members of the Planning Council: Director of Mayor's Office on Special Needs Housing, Director of Mayor's Office on Drug Abuse Policy, Chairperson of the City Human Rights Commission, Commissioner of Aging of the City of New York, Director of Mayor's Office of Operations, Director of Mayor's Office for People with Disabilities, and Director of Mayor's Office on Homelessness and Single Room Occupancy Housing Services.

(j) In the event of a vacancy, the Planning Council may within thirty (30) days after the vacancy occurs recommend to the Mayor the names of three individuals who would satisfy the relevant qualifying criteria to fill that vacancy.

Section 2. Executive Order No. 23, dated January 18, 1991, is amended by renumbering Sections 6 and 7 thereof as Sections 8 and 9, respectively, and adding new Sections 6 and 7 to read as follows:

Section 6. **Reporting Requirements.** The Planning Council shall report all of its decisions and recommendations to the Mayor through the Deputy Mayor for Health and Human Services. In addition, the Planning Council shall submit an annual report to the Mayor on the delivery of services under Title I of the Ryan White Act. Such report shall also contain the Planning Council's recommendations regarding the delivery of such services under Title I of the Ryan White Act as well as the delivery of other HIV/AIDS services needed to effect a comprehensive continuum of care for persons impacted by the HIV/AIDS epidemic.

Section 7. Staff. The Planning Council may
recommend and shall be provided with such paid
staff members as are approved by the Mayor.

Section 3. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

DAVID N. DINKINS
MAYOR

title: ESTABLISHMENT OF AN INTERAGENCY TASK FORCE ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF RECYCLING MARKETS AND BUSINESSES
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 52

JANUARY 29 1993

ESTABLISHMENT OF AN INTERAGENCY TASK FORCE ON
THE DEVELOPMENT OF RECYCLING MARKETS AND BUSINESSES

WHEREAS, it is critical to the successful implementation of the City's solid waste management plan, the cornerstone of which is an aggressive recycling program, that sufficient processing capacity and markets exist for the recyclable materials collected by the City and private companies; and

WHEREAS, businesses associated with the re-manufacture of recyclable materials are potentially a significant source of capital investment and new jobs in the City.

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as the Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. **Interagency Task Force**

a. There is hereby established an Interagency Task Force on the Development of Recycling Markets and Businesses. The Task Force shall report to the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development.

b. The Task Force shall be chaired by the Commissioner of the Department of Sanitation, or his or her designee. The Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development shall request the President of the Economic Development Corporation, or his or her designee, to act as co-chair.

c. The following City agencies and divisions of the Office of the Mayor shall participate on the Task Force: the Department of General Services, the Department of Environmental Protection, the Law Department, the Department of Employment, the Office of the Deputy Mayor for Planning and Development, the Mayor's Office of Operations, the Mayor's Office of Management and Budget, the Mayor's Office of Contracts, the Mayor's Office of City Legislative Affairs, and the Office of Economic Planning and Marketing. The head of each participating entity shall designate a senior official to serve on the Task Force.

Section 2. <u>Functions of the Task Force</u>

The Task Force shall be responsible for formulating a coordinated strategy to encourage the growth of markets for the City's recyclables and to attract recycling businesses to New York City, working in consultation with the Mayor's Advisory Council on the Development of Recycling Markets and Businesses established under Section 3 of this Order. The Task Force shall develop a strategy based upon:

a. an assessment of the most effective methods of marketing the City's recyclable materials;

b. an identification of those recycling industries most suited to New York City;

c. an evaluation of the economic incentives that would be most effective in attracting recycling businesses to the City and expanding existing businesses in the City; and

d. an analysis of methods for increasing the City's procurement of products with recycled content.

Section 3. <u>Advisory Council</u>

a. There is hereby established a Mayor's Advisory Council on the Development of Recycling Markets and Businesses. The Advisory Council shall include representatives of the business community, environmental groups, and other organizations having recycling expertise. The members shall be appointed for a term of two years and shall serve without compensation. The City Council shall also be requested to participate on the Advisory Council.

b. The Advisory Council shall be chaired by the Commissioner of the Department of Sanitation, or his or her designee. The Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development shall request the President of the Economic Development Corporation, or his or her designee, to act as co-chair.

c. The Advisory Council shall assist the Mayor and the Task Force on the Development of Recycling Markets and Businesses in formulating the City's coordinated strategy to encourage the growth of markets for the City's recyclables and to attract recycling businesses to New York City.

Section 4. This Order shall take effect immediately.
