THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 53

January 29, 1993

DEPUTY MAYORS AND COUNSEL TO THE MAYOR

(Supersedes Executive Order No. 33, dated 12/27/91)

By the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. There shall be six Deputy Mayors. One shall be designated the First Deputy Mayor, one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development, one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Planning and Development, one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Public and Community Affairs, one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Public Safety, and one shall be designated Deputy Mayor for Health and Human Services.

§2. The First Deputy Mayor shall:

a. Supervise and coordinate the operations of all administrations, departments, agencies, boards, offices, committees, and commissions except as otherwise provided herein.

b. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Mayor's Office of Operations, the Office of City Legislative Affairs, the Office of State Legislative Affairs, and the Mayor's Office in Washington, D.C.

c. Act on behalf of the Mayor, either directly or through the Office of City Legislative Affairs, the Office of State Legislative Affairs, or the Mayor's Office in Washington, D.C., with respect to all City, State and federal legislative matters affecting the City; direct the activities of the Mayor's legislative representatives in New York City, Albany, and Washington, D.C.; represent the Mayor before City Council, Congressional and State legislative committees; and maintain liaison with the Office of the President and all federal departments and agencies, the Office of the Governor and all State departments and agencies, and the City Council.

d. Serve as the Mayor's representative, either directly or through the Offices of City and State Legislative Affairs, on, and maintain liaison with, regional bodies and intergovernmental agencies operating within the New York metropolitan region.

e. Maintain liaison, either directly or through the Mayor's Office in Washington, D.C., with the United States Conference of Mayors, the National League of Cities, the New York Conference of Mayors and other similar bodies.

f. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Board of Education, the New York City School Construction Authority, the City University of New York, and the Metropolitan Transportation Authority.

g. Supervise and coordinate the preparation of the City's Revenue, Expense and Capital Budgets and the operations of the Office of Management and Budget.

h. Develop, supervise and coordinate policies and programs relating to personnel and management practices.

i. Succeed to the powers and duties of the "Deputy Mayor - City Administrator of the City" under section 7384 of the Unconsolidated Laws (Chapter 1016 of the Laws of 1969).

j. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not limited to, full power to execute for and on behalf of the Mayor, any agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.

k. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the Mayor, a certificate approving any borrowing of funds or pledge of assets or revenues by the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation which would require the approval of the Mayor pursuant to the "Memorandum of Agreement Between New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation and The City of New York Relating to Operating Expenditures by the Corporation", dated July 1, 1970.

l. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the City, Official Statements of the City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.

m. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

n. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution of contracts, franchises, revocable consents, deeds and satisfactions.

o. Perform any function, power or duty which the Mayor has (and is authorized to delegate) pursuant to New York City Charter sections 217, 219, and 344, and pursuant to Administrative Code section 5-304.

p. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§3. The First Deputy Mayor is hereby delegated the authority to perform all functions, powers or duties of the Mayor which the Mayor is authorized to delegate, in the event that the Mayor is unable to perform such functions, powers or duties for a reason specified in subdivision a of section 10 of the New York City Charter.

§4. The Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development shall:

a. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning and programs designed to implement and enhance the fiscal operations and financial and business management practices of the City.

b. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning, and programs designed to foster the economic growth of the City, including those relating to: commercial and industrial development; telecommunications; energy; foreign trade and investment; government regulation; film, theatre and broadcasting; air, land and sea freight; revenue enhancement; and tax policy and programs.

c. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Departments of Finance, Employment, Telecommunications and Energy, and Business Services; the Economic Policy and Marketing Group; the Office of Film, Theatre, and Broadcasting; and the New York City Commission for the United Nations and Consular Corps.

d. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Tax Commission and the Industrial Loft Advisory Council.

e. Serve as Chairperson of the Development Funds Steering Committee, the Commercial Incentive Boundary Area Commission, and the Industrial and Commercial Incentive Board.

f. Coordinate the activities of the New York Convention and Visitors Bureau, the Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation, the Economic Development Corporation, and the New York City Industrial Development Agency.

g. Direct and coordinate the activities of all administrations, departments, agencies, boards, offices, committees and commissions with respect to fiscal, telecommunications and energy policies, planning and programs.

h. Maintain liaison with the New York State Department of Economic Development, New York State Urban Development Corporation, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, the Power Authority of the State of New York, the New York State Public Service Commission, the New York State Municipal Assistance Corporation for the City of New York, the New York State Financial Control Board, the New York City Alliance for International Business, Ltd., and State and federal agencies and executive offices with respect to matters of City fiscal operations, economic development, and energy and telecommunications policies and programs.

i. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not limited to, full power to execute for and on behalf of the Mayor, any agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.

j. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the Mayor, a certificate approving any borrowing of funds or pledge of assets or revenues by the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation which would require the approval of the Mayor pursuant to the "Memorandum of Agreement Between New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation and The City of New York Relating to Operating Expenditures by the Corporation," dated July 1, 1970.

k. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the City, Official Statements of the City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.

l. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

m. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution of contracts, franchises, revocable consents, deeds and satisfactions.

n. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§5. The Deputy Mayor for Planning and Development shall:

a. Supervise and coordinate all land use planning and development activities of the City.

b. Coordinate the operations of the Departments of Environmental Protection, Cultural Affairs, Parks and Recreation, City Planning and Housing Preservation and Development; the Office of Housing Coordination; and the Office of Environmental Coordination.

c. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the City Planning Commission; the Landmarks Preservation Commission; the Landmark Hardship Review Panel; the Art Commission; the Board of Standards and Appeals; the Loft Board; the Environmental Control Board; and the New York City Housing Authority.

d. Serve as Chairperson of the Waterfront Management Advisory Board.

e. Review the data analyses and estimates of the 1990 Census Project and maintain liaison with the United States Census Bureau and other federal and State agencies regarding the 1990 Census.

f. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Community Development Block Grant Application Program.

g. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Commission on the Status of Women.

h. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not limited to, full power to execute for and on behalf of the Mayor, any agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.

i. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the Mayor, a certificate approving any borrowing of funds or pledge of assets or revenues by the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation which would require the approval of the Mayor pursuant to the "Memorandum of Agreement Between New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation and The City of New York Relating to Operating Expenditures by the Corporation," dated July 1, 1970.

j. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the City, Official Statements of the City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.

k. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

l. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution of contracts, franchises, revocable consents, deeds and satisfactions.

m. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§6. The Deputy Mayor for Public and Community Affairs shall:

a. Coordinate the formulation and implementation of public education and outreach initiatives regarding City policies and programs in conjunction with the Mayor, the other Deputy Mayors, Agency Heads, and the communications and public affairs offices of Mayoral agencies.

b. Coordinate the operations of the Mayor's Press Office, the Mayor's Scheduling Committee, the Mayor's Office of Speech Writing, the Mayor's Office of Special Projects and Events, and the Mayor's Office of Correspondence Services.

c. Work with the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development to assist in promoting the communications, marketing and programming activities of the Mayor's Office of Partnership Programs, the Department of Business Services, the WNYC Communications Group, the Department of Telecommunications and Energy, the Mayor's Office of Film, Theatre and Broadcasting, and the Economic Policy and Marketing Group.

d. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Community Assistance Unit, the City Volunteer Corps, the Mayor's Voluntary Action Center, the Community Development Agency, the Mayor's Commission on Protocol, and the Increase the Peace Volunteer Corps.

e. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Offices of African-American/Caribbean Affairs, Asian Affairs, Latino Affairs, European-American Affairs, Immigrant Affairs and Veterans Affairs, and the Office for the Lesbian and Gay Community.

f. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Voter Assistance Commission.

g. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not limited to, full power to execute any agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.

h. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the Mayor, a certificate approving any borrowing of funds or pledge of assets or revenues by the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation which would require the approval of the Mayor pursuant to the "Memorandum of Agreement Between New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation and the City of New York Relating to Operating Expenditures by the Corporation," dated July 1, 1970.

i. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the City, Official Statements of the City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.

j. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

k. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution of contracts, franchises, revocable consents, deeds and satisfactions.

l. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§7. The Deputy Mayor for Public Safety shall:

a. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning and programs regarding the criminal justice system.

b. Work with the First Deputy Mayor, in coordination with the Office of Management and Budget and the Office of Operations, to ensure the implementation of Mayoral policies regarding the criminal justice system.

c. Supervise inter-agency initiatives intended to improve the functioning and coordination of agencies involved in the criminal justice system, including the Departments of Police, Correction, Probation and Juvenile Justice, the Courts, and the District Attorneys.

d. Be responsible for the implementation of the Court Facilities Master Plan.

e. Oversee the activities of the Mayor's Arson Strike Force and the Office of Drug Abuse Policy.

f. Oversee the implementation of the City's major criminal justice management information systems.

g. Oversee the use of City funds for legal services to indigent defendants and the funding of programs that provide alternatives to incarceration and detention.

h. Be and perform the duties of the Coordinator of Criminal Justice as provided in section 13 of the New York City Charter.

i. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not limited to, full power to execute for and on behalf of the Mayor, any agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.

j. k. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the City, Official Statements of the City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.

1. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

m. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution of contracts, franchises, revocable consents, deeds and satisfactions.

n. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§8. The Deputy Mayor for Health and Human Services shall:

a. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning and programs regarding health and human services.

b. Work with the First Deputy Mayor, in coordination with the Office of Management and Budget and the Office of Operations, to ensure the implementation of Mayoral policies regarding health and human services.

c. Oversee implementation of all plans and programs for housing and assisting homeless individuals in New York City.

d. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Departments of Youth Services, Health, and Mental Health, Mental Retardation and Alcoholism Services; the Department for the Aging, the Human Resources Administration; the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner; the Office on Homelessness and Single Room Occupancy Housing Services; the Office on Health Policy; the Office for Children and Families Services; and the Office for People With Disabilities.

e. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation.

f. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not limited to, full power to execute any agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.

g. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the Mayor, a certificate approving any borrowing of funds or pledge of assets or revenues by the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation which would require the approval of the Mayor pursuant to the "Memorandum of Agreement Between New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation and The City of New York Relating to Operating Expenditures by the Corporation", dated July 1, 1970.

h. Execute and deliver in the name and on behalf of the City, Official Statements of the City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.

i. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.

j. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution of contracts, franchises, revocable consents, deeds and satisfactions.

k. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§9. The Counsel to the Mayor shall:

a. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the City Commission on Human Rights.

b. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Equal Employment Practices Commission, the Board of Elections and the Campaign Finance Board.

c. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§10. Executive Order No. 40, dated July 20, 1992, sections 1 through 8 of Executive Order No. 33, dated December 27, 1991, and Mayoral Directive No. 92-4 are hereby repealed.

§11. This Order shall take effect immediately.

title: BUSINESS EMERGENCY TASK FORCE
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 54

March 5, 1993

BUSINESS EMERGENCY TASK FORCE

WHEREAS, the economic well-being of New York City is dependent, in part, upon the City's ability to respond to the needs of its businesses and industries in times of emergency; and

WHEREAS, representatives of City agencies involved in the regulation of and delivery of municipal services to businesses must be able to communicate quickly and effectively with one another in times of emergency;

NOW THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. **Creation of Task Force.** There is hereby established the Business Emergency Task Force (the "Task Force"). The Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development or his or her

designee shall serve as a member and as chairperson of the Task Force and shall coordinate and supervise its activities.

§ 2. Business Emergency. For the purposes of this Executive Order, the term "business emergency" means any occasion or instance for which, in the determination of the Mayor, circumstances require special assistance to protect commercial property and aid businesses or to lessen or avert damage to business interests in the City.

§ 3. Membership.

a. The following City officers shall also be members of the Task Force:

(1) the Commissioner of Business Services or his or her designee;

(2) the Commissioner of Buildings or his or her designee;

(3) the Police Commissioner or his or her designee; and

(4) the Fire Commissioner or his or her designee.

Any person designated to sit on the Task Force pursuant to this subdivision shall be a senior official or staff member having experience in and familiarity with matters pertaining to emergency response.

b. In addition to the above-named officers, the Mayor shall invite each of the following entities to designate one representative who shall be a member of the Task Force:

(1) the Metropolitan Transportation Authority;

(2) the New York City Economic Development Corporation;

(3) the New York City Chamber of Commerce;

(4) the New York Telephone Company;

(5) the Consolidated Edison Company of New York, Inc.;

(6) the Brooklyn Union Gas Company; and

(7) the New York Clearing House Association.

c. The Mayor may direct any City agency not specified in subdivision (a) of this section to designate a senior official or staff member to participate in the work of the Task Force for any period of time the Mayor considers appropriate. Each such agency shall notify the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development of such designation.

d. The Mayor may request any other elected official, local development corporation, business improvement district or other business organization to designate an officer or senior staff member to participate in the work of the Task Force for any period of time the Mayor considers appropriate, and to

communicate such designation to the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development.

§ 4. **Functions of Task Force.** The functions and duties of the Task Force shall include:

a. determining what steps should be taken to protect commercial property and aid businesses or to lessen or avert damage to business interests in the City in the event of a business emergency;

b. determining the availability to businesses in the City of emergency assistance funds;

c. notifying members of the business community of a business emergency or of the possibility thereof;

d. in the event that a business emergency is determined to exist, coordinating the assignment of appropriate City personnel to the affected area to assess business related issues and concerns; and

e. undertaking such other activities and measures as may be directed by the Mayor to ensure communication between the City and the business community during a business emergency.

§ 5. **Effective Date.** This Order shall take effect immediately.

title: STREET VENDING ACTION PLAN
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 55

April 12, 1993

STREET VENDING ACTION PLAN

WHEREAS, street vending is a thriving industry in New York City and provides economic opportunity to a broad spectrum of New Yorkers; and

WHEREAS, the vast majority of street vendors are unlicensed and the extent of unlicensed street vending activity has interfered in certain areas with the legitimate interests of small retail business owners and other citizens of the City; and

WHEREAS, each Deputy Mayor and over twenty City agencies have responsibilities regarding various aspects of the street vending industry, and greater coordination of policy is needed; and

WHEREAS, it is the objective of the City to advance an effective and consistent approach to regulation of street vending that will ultimately reduce illegal vending, but will be supportive of an appropriate role for legal vending and vendors in the City's economy;

NOW THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

**Section 1. Street Vendor Steering Committee.** There is hereby established a Street Vendor Steering Committee which shall be responsible for the City-wide coordination of street vendor regulation and policy. The members of the Committee shall be the First Deputy Mayor or his or her designee, the Deputy Mayor for Public Safety or his or her designee, the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development or his or her designee, and the Deputy Mayor for Public and Community Affairs or his or her designee.

**§ 2. Street Vending Coordinators.** The Police Commissioner and the Commissioner of Business Services shall be the City's Street Vending Coordinators. The Police Commissioner or his or her designee shall be responsible for developing and implementing coordinated City-wide strategies to enforce the laws and rules regulating street vending. The Commissioner of Business Services or his or her designee shall be responsible for developing and implementing enhanced services for vendors.

**§ 3. Street Vendor Operating Committee.** There is hereby established a Street Vendor Operating Committee to advise the Street Vending Coordinators with regard to the formulation, implementation and evaluation of street vendor policy and program initiatives. The co-chairs of the Operating Committee shall be the Police Commissioner or his or her designee and the Commissioner of Business Services or his or her designee. The other members of the Operating Committee shall be the Commissioner of Consumer Affairs or his or her designee, the Commissioner of Health or his or her designee, the Executive Director of the Economic Policy and Marketing Group or his or her designee, the Director of the Mayor's Office of City Legislative Affairs or his or her designee, and the Director of the Community Assistance Unit or his or her designee. All city agencies shall be required

to cooperate with the Operating Committee in carrying out its work, as requested by the Committee.

§ 4. Vendor Advisory Board

There is hereby established a Vendor Advisory Board which shall consist of no more than fifteen persons and shall include licensed street vendors and retail business owners who shall advise and make recommendations to the Commissioner of Business Services regarding the needs of street vendors and problems related to street vending.

§ 5. This Order shall take effect immediately.

full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N. Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 57

OCTOBER 24 1993

THE MAYOR'S DOMESTIC VIOLENCE COORDINATING COUNCIL

WHEREAS, it is estimated that domestic violence affects as many as 279,3000 households in New York City every year; and

WHEREAS, domestic violence is a devastating phenomena that respects no boundaries of race, ethnicity, age, gender, sexual orientation, or economic status; and

WHEREAS, the policies and programs of this Administration have been dedicated to assisting children and families in need; and

WHEREAS, during the past four years the City has more than doubled the number of emergency shelter beds for victims of domestic violence and their children, and has for the first time ever designed non-residential services for this population; and

WHEREAS, the City has incorporated domestic violence prevention into the New York City Police Department's community policing program, thereby expanding the "Safe Streets, Safe City" program, into a "Safe Streets, Safe City, Safe Homes" program; and

WHEREAS, the development of an integrated approach to the problem of domestic violence and the coordination of existing systems and services are critical to the success of the City's efforts in this area;

NOW THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Establishment of a Coordinating Council. There is hereby established a Mayor's Domestic Violence Coordinating Council (the "Coordinating Council"). The Director of the Mayor's Office for Children and Families or his or her designee shall serve as chairperson of the Coordinating Council and shall coordinate and supervise its activities. The Coordinating Council shall report to the Deputy Mayor for Health and Human Services and the Deputy Mayor for Planning and Development.

Section 2. Membership.

a. In addition to the Mayor's Office for Children and Families, the following City agencies, commissions and divisions of the Office of the Mayor shall be members of the Coordinating Council:

1. Department of Health

2. Human Resources Administration (Child Welfare Administration, Adult Services Administration, Family Support Administration)

3. Police Department

4. Department of the Aging

5. Department of Housing Preservation and Development

6. Department of Youth Services

7. Department of Probation

8. Department of Mental Health, Retardation and Alcoholism Service

9. Law Department

10. Department of Homeless Services

11. Department of Juvenile Justice

12. Commission on the Status of Women

13. Office of the Deputy Mayor for Public Safety

14. Office of Management and Budget

15. Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs

16. Mayor's Office of Operations

b. The Health and Hospitals Corporation and the New York City Housing Authority shall also be invited to be members of the Coordinating Council.

c. The head of each participating entity shall designate a senior level administrator to attend Coordinating Council meetings and be responsible for carrying out the terms of this Executive Order.

d. The Coordinating Council shall meet at least once each quarter and as otherwise requested by the Chairperson.

Section 3. Purpose. The Coordinating Council shall:

a. Formulate policies and programs relating to all aspects of services and protocols for victims of domestic violence;

b. Develop methods to improve the coordination of systems and services for victims of domestic violence;

c. Create mechanisms to ensure that each affected City agency respond appropriately to domestic violence situations and that there is coordination among the agencies involved; and

d. Launch a public education campaign to heighten awareness of domestic violence and its devastating effects on society.

Section 4. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

title: COMMUNITY ASSISTANCE UNIT
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 59

December 9, 1993

COMMUNITY ASSISTANCE UNIT

(Supersedes E.O. 25, dated July 19, 1991)

Of all levels of government, the municipal level is the most direct provider of public services. These public services should be responsive to the needs of the community and be delivered in a fair and effective manner.

City government can best serve its citizens if city officials understand what citizens need and expect from the city and if citizens understand the operations and limits of municipal government.

Improving the quality of life in the city's communities can best be accomplished by the affirmative action of residents working in participation with their city government.

A cornerstone of this administration is accessibility of government to our residents, responsiveness to suggestions and recommendations and the encouragement of citizen participation in government.

To help meet these goals:

Section 1. There is hereby established within the Office of the Mayor a Community Assistance Unit headed by a director who shall be appointed by and serve at the pleasure of the Mayor.

Section 2. The Community Assistance Unit shall maintain continuous liaison with city officials, public and private agencies, community boards, district service cabinets, district managers, borough boards and cabinets, community groups and communities.

Section 3. The Community Assistance Unit shall be responsible for coordinating the activities of city agencies with respect to the implementation and operation of the provisions of the Charter of the City of New York concerning community boards, district service cabinets, district managers, coterminality and decentralization including, but not limited to, responsibility for:

(a) coordinating, in accordance with Sections 2704 and 2705 of the Charter, (i) the establishment of coterminous service districts by designated agencies, (ii) the assignment by each such agency of a managerial official with operating or line authority over agency programs, personnel and facilities to each service district and (iii) the publication of lists of local service managers and borough officials;

(b) working with the Mayor's Office of Operations to coordinate (i) the assignment by each designated agency of borough officials in accordance with Sections 2704 and 2706 of the Charter, (ii) the design of the Mayor's biennial report on coterminality in accordance with Section 2704 of the Charter and (iii) a format for the Mayor's Management Report and Supplemental Management Report to include, insofar as practicable, performance indicators for each local service district in accordance with Section 12 of the Charter;

(c) assisting the Office of Management and Budget in coordinating (i) the implementation and operation of the provisions of the Charter concerning community board participation in the budget process in accordance with Sections 100, 219, 230 and 238 of the Charter and (ii) agency service statements for community districts in accordance with and to the extent required by Section 2707 of the Charter;

(d) maintaining a continuous liaison with community boards, district service cabinets, district managers, borough boards and service cabinets, city officials and agencies in order (i) to bring to the attention of the Mayor and other appropriate city officials significant problems arising in connection with the activities or operations of such organizations and to propose solutions to such problems, (ii) to foster a cooperative and effective working relationship between city officials and community boards and district managers, and (iii) to ensure that significant Mayoral initiatives and programs are communicated to community boards and communities;

(e) establishing, in conjunction with the Department of Personnel, appropriate personnel guidelines for community board employees in accordance with the Civil Service Law and regulations; and

(f) providing training and technical assistance for implementation of the appropriate Charter provisions to community boards, district service cabinets, district managers and city agencies.

Section 4. The Community Assistance Unit shall be responsible for maintaining a liaison with communities and community groups in order to bring to the attention of the Mayor and other appropriate city officials issues and problems of concern to communities, including, but not limited to, responsibility for the following:

(a) addressing the concerns of community-based groups, including without limitation, block, neighborhood, civic, regional and citywide groups, regarding city services, policies and programs;

(b) fostering greater cooperation between community groups and community boards;

(c) coordinating such other community outreach and liaison activities as the Mayor may direct, including but not limited to scheduling meetings between the Mayor, city officials, community leaders and residents;

(d) representing the Mayor at community meetings when requested to do so by the Mayor; and

(e) administering the Stop the Violence Fund to encourage and assist local anti-crime efforts in cooperation with the Police Department, the District Attorneys and the Department of Youth Services.

Section 5. The Community Assistance Unit shall maintain a liaison available to residents and individuals to serve as a clearinghouse for opinions, ideas, suggestions, complaints, requests and inquiries about municipal issues directed to the Mayor including, but not limited to, responsibility for:

a) making municipal services more accessible and providing the public with information about them;

b) providing individuals with channels to present to the Mayor or appropriate city agencies complaints, requests, inquiries and suggestions regarding municipal services, policies or programs by (i) as appropriate, providing individuals with assistance with relevant agency staff to resolve concerns

and (ii) maintaining a statistical record of
such contacts for analysis and review by
appropriate city officials;

c) working with city agencies to ensure appropriate review and consideration of proposals, suggestions and recommendations;

d) providing, as appropriate, reply and/or follow up to communications; and

e) coordinating complaints and concerns regarding citywide city agency "Hotline" and "Complaint" numbers, including, but not limited to, responsibility for (i) monitoring agency complaint and hotline numbers, (ii) maintaining statistics and preparing reports on calls received regarding agency complaint and hotline numbers for use by appropriate city officials.

Section 6. The Community Assistance Unit shall exercise all functions, powers and duties regarding street activity permits pursuant to Executive Order No. 14 dated July 31, 1990.

Section 7. The Community Assistance Unit shall maintain a Neighborhood Development/SRO Housing Unit to coordinate the City's efforts to prevent homelessness, preserve, improve and expand the single room occupancy housing stock and to protect the rights of individuals living in SRO buildings, with responsibility for:

a) working with city, state and private agencies to prevent homelessness by keeping individuals and families living in their neighborhoods and out of the shelter system;

b) overseeing interagency oversight strategies for code enforcement and inspection activities in SRO hotels and rooming houses, as well as hotels used as temporary housing for displaced families and persons with AIDS, and

c) providing information and referrals to SRO tenants and owners, intervening on behalf of tenants who require assistance, and resolving illegal eviction and harassment complaints.

Section 8. All city agencies, without limitation, are directed to cooperate with the Unit established hereby in order to carry out the objectives of the Charter and of this Order.

Section 9. Executive Order No. 25, dated July 19, 1991, is hereby repealed.

Section 10. This Order shall take effect immediately.

title: CITYWIDE OFFICE FOR SEXUAL HARASSMENT PREVENTION
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 60

December 16, 1993

CITYWIDE OFFICE FOR SEXUAL HARASSMENT PREVENTION

WHEREAS, the City of New York has a strong commitment to equal opportunity for all employees; and

WHEREAS, pursuant to section 813(a)(12) of the Charter, the City has adopted and implemented an Affirmative Employment Plan setting forth policies and procedures for the prevention and remediation of unlawful employment discrimination; and

WHEREAS, sexual harassment is a form of unlawful discrimination that affects both women and men; the law governing this subject is complex and still evolving; and cases of sexual harassment often include related complaints of other forms of discrimination;

WHEREAS, on October 28, 1992 the Mayor appointed a Task Force on Sexual Harassment ("Task Force") to study the City's procedures for preventing and addressing sexual harassment, and to make recommendation as to how such procedures could be improved; and

WHEREAS, the Task Force submitted a report to the Mayor on November 1, 1993, recommending that the City establish, on a pilot basis, a Citywide Office for Sexual Harassment Prevention; and

WHEREAS, while the immediate objective of the establishment of such an office is to enhance the City's ability to address the problem of sexual harassment, the long term goal is to develop approaches, which can be tested by the new office, that will enable the City to address all forms of discrimination with heightened sensitivity;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. **Office Established.** As a pilot project to test the efficiency of a centralized office to address the problem of unlawful sexual harassment, there is hereby established an Office for Sexual Harassment Prevention ("Office"). The Office shall be headed by the Director of the Office for Sexual Harassment, who shall be appointed by the Mayor. For Administrative purposes, the Office shall be located in the Department of Personnel.

Section 2. **Responsibilities of the Office.**

a. The Office shall respond to City employees' requests for information, advice, or counselling on issues related to sexual harassment.

b. The Office shall mediate cases of alleged sexual harassment arising in City agencies.

c. The Office shall investigate formal complaints of alleged sexual harassment filed by City employees with the Office, as well as other complaints of alleged unlawful discrimination filed in connection with such complaints of sexual harassment. Upon completion of such an investigation, the Office shall submit to the head of the relevant agency a report of the findings of the investigation, and recommendations as to any corrective action, including discipline, which should be taken in response to the complaint.

d. The Office shall monitor the responses of City agencies to employees who seek assistance with matters related to sexual harassment, and provide such assistance as it determines necessary to ensure that such matters are addressed in an appropriate and consistent manner.

e. The Office shall evaluate the effectiveness of training in the prevention of sexual harassment that is provided by City agencies, and collaborate with the Department of Personnel to ensure that appropriate training is provided to all employees, and take appropriate action to ensure that such training is consistent, with particular attention to the specialized training needs of high level managers and persons responsible for investigating allegations of sexual harassment.

f. The Office shall assist the Department of Personnel in its efforts to strengthen the complaint procedures developed pursuant to the Citywide Affirmative Employment Plan.

g. The Office, assisted by the Department of Personnel, the Office of Labor Relations, the Commission on Human Rights, and the Law Department, shall compile a summary of precedents and other relevant information to which agency heads may refer in determining the appropriate corrective action to take in response to a complaint of sexual harassment.

h. The Office shall maintain central records of complaints of sexual harassment, including informal complaints.

Section 3. Responsibilities of City Agencies.

a. The Equal Employment Opportunity Office of each agency shall advise the Office whenever an employee has filed a complaint alleging sexual harassment, and shall submit reports to the Office about activities related to the prevention and investigation of sexual harassment, as requested by the Office.

b. Whenever an agency head determines not to take a corrective action recommended by the Office, the agency head shall submit an explanation for such a determination to the Mayor and the Office.

Section 4. Activity Reports. The Office shall submit quarterly reports of its activities to the Mayor.

Section 5. Cooperation of City Agencies. The Commission on the Status of Women, the City Commission on Human Rights, the Department of Personnel, and other relevant City agencies shall consult with the Office and provide support and expertise as required by the Office.

Section 6. Mayoral Oversight Committee. There shall be a Mayoral Oversight Committee, consisting of a Deputy Mayor to be designated by the Mayor, the Corporation Counsel, the Counsel to the Mayor, and the Personnel Director, which shall oversee the work of the Office.

Section 7. Effective Date. This Executive Order shall take effect immediately, and shall remain in effect for two years. Prior to the expiration of this Order, the Mayor shall evaluate the effectiveness of the provisions herein, and determine whether they should be continued, expanded, or otherwise modified and whether the duties of the Office established by this Order should be exercised by the Department of Personnel, together with its Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Employment responsibilities.

title: HARLEM COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT ZONE
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 61

DECEMBER 22, 1993

HARLEM COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT ZONE

WHEREAS, Subchapter C of Title XIII of the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1993, Public Law 103-66 (the "Act") authorizes the establishment of an Empowerment Zone Program under which a community of not more than 200,000 people in New York City may be designated to receive special investment and training credits and major funding for social services which would enhance the economic self-sufficiency of zone residents; and

WHEREAS, the Act allows an area to be nominated for Empowerment Zone status by the local government and State in which it is located or by an economic development corporation chartered by the State; and

WHEREAS, the community of Harlem, defined as the areas of Community Boards 9, 10, and 11, meets the eligibility criteria for designation as an Empowerment Zone under the Act; and

I. Department of Business Services

II. Office of Management and Budget

III. Mayor's Office of Children and Families

IV. Department of City Planning

V. Department of Employment

VI. Mayor's Federal Affairs Office

VII. Economic Policy and Marketing Group

VIII. Department of Housing, Preservation and Development

IX. Human Resources Administration

X. Police Department

The Economic Development Corporation shall be invited to continue
its participation in the Working Group.

d. The membership of the Working Group may be added to, or
modified as necessary, by the deputy mayors responsible for supervision of its activities.

Section 4. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

title: NEW YORK CITY COMMISSION AND MAYOR’S TASK FORCE ON THE REDEVELOPMENT OF NAVAL STATION NEW YORK
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 62

DECEMBER 23, 1993

NEW YORK CITY COMMISSION AND MAYOR'S TASK FORCE ON THE
REDEVELOPMENT OF NAVAL STATION NEW YORK

WHEREAS, despite substantial efforts by the City and its Congressional delegation to keep Naval Station New York (the "Homeport") at Staten Island, the United States government has indicated that it intends to close the Homeport; and

WHEREAS, the City is now faced with the challenge of finding an alternative use for the Homeport in order to redress the impact of the base closure and provide new economic development benefits to the City; and

WHEREAS, a careful assessment of the various alternatives is necessary in order to develop a plan to utilize the Homeport site and its facilities to achieve their potential; and

WHEREAS, development of a plan can best be achieved by involving community and business leaders in the process;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. New York City Commission on the Redevelopment of Naval Station New York.

a. Establishment of Commission. There is hereby established the New York City Commission on the Redevelopment of Naval Station New York (the "Commission"). The Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development or his or her designee shall act as liaison with the Commission.

b. Membership of Commission. The Members of the Commission shall include business leaders, representatives of cultural, civic, and social service organizations, and individuals residing in the community in which the Homeport site is located. The Mayor shall designate the Chair of the Commission.

c. Functions of Commission. The functions and duties of the Commission shall be:

(i) in consultation with the Task Force hereinafter established, to assess various alternatives and recommendations for reuse of the Homeport site and the facilities thereon;

(ii) to develop and recommend to the Task Force and the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development a plan to utilize the Homeport site and the facilities thereon to their full potential; and

(iii) to perform such other related functions as the Mayor may direct.

Section 2. Mayor's Task Force on the Redevelopment of Naval Station New York.

a. Establishment of Task Force. There is hereby established a Task Force on the Redevelopment of Naval Station New York (the "Task Force"). The Task Force shall report to the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development.

b. Membership of Task Force. The following shall participate in the Task Force: The Department of Business Services; the Economic Policy and Marketing Group; the Department of Parks and Recreation; the Department of Environmental Protection; the Department of City Planning; the Department of Transportation; the Department of Sanitation; and the Department of Employment. The New York City Economic Development Corporation has agreed to participate in the Task Force.

c. Functions. The functions and duties of the Task Force shall be:

(i) to assist the Commission in assessing alternatives and recommendations for the reuse of the Homeport site;

(ii) to evaluate on behalf of the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development the plan proposed by the Commission for utilization of the Homeport site and the facilities thereon; and

(iii) to perform such other related functions as the Mayor may direct.

Section 3. Cooperation of City Agencies. All City Agencies are directed to cooperate with the Commission and Task Force in carrying out their activities.

Section 4. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

title: INTERAGENCY TASK FORCE ON SMALL BUSINESS
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N. Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 63

December 30, 1993

Amendment of Executive Order No. 30 (October 2, 1991)

INTERAGENCY TASK FORCE ON SMALL BUSINESS
AND
THE SMALL BUSINESS ADVISORY BOARD

WHEREAS, the economic well-being of New York City is dependent, in part, upon the City's ability to respond to the needs of its businesses and industries; and

WHEREAS, representatives of City agencies involved in the regulation of and delivery of municipal services to small businesses must be able to communicate quickly and effectively with one another in order to ensure productive interaction between the City and the small business community; and

WHEREAS, the economic vitality of the City's small business community is dependent, in part, on the ability of the private sector to communicate with the public sector on ways to improve the economic vitality of the City's small business community;

NOW THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered that Executive Order No. 30 of October 2, 1991, is amended to read as follows:

Section 1. **Creation of Task Force.** There is hereby established within the office of the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development an Interagency Task Force on Small Business ("Task Force").

§ 2. **Functions of Task Force.** The functions and duties of the Task Force shall include:

a. evaluating agency procedures and operations where these may affect segments of New York City's small business community;

b. reviewing relevant City rules and procedures and making recommendations for changes therein designed to promote and foster the growth of small businesses in the City;

c. subject to approval of the Mayor and the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development, making determinations with respect to issues confronting the City which, in the estimation of Task Force participants, may have a significant impact on the small business community; and

d. undertaking other activities and measures as directed by the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development to ensure productive interaction between the City and the small business community.

§ 3. Membership.

a. The following City agencies shall participate in the Task Force: Department of Buildings; Department of Business Services; Department of City Planning; Department of Consumer Affairs; Department of Employment; Department of Environmental Protection; Department of Finance; Fire Department; Department of General Services; Department of Health; Law Department; Police Department; Department of Sanitation; Department of Telecommunications and Energy; Department of Transportation; the Economic Policy and Marketing Group; and such other City agencies as the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development may hereinafter designate. In addition, the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development shall direct the New York City Economic Development Corporation to participate in the Task Force.

b. The head of each participating entity shall designate a deputy commissioner or a senior official occupying a comparable position to serve on the Task Force. The Mayor, the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development and the Commissioner of the Department of Business Services shall be notified of such designation within two weeks of the date of this order.

### § 4. Coordination.
The Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development or his or her designee shall serve as chairperson of the Task Force and shall coordinate and supervise its activities.

### § 5. Creation of Mayor's Small Business Advisory Board.
There is hereby established the Mayor's Small Business Advisory Board (the "Advisory Board") to advise the Mayor and Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development on matters relating to the

small business community. The Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development or his or her designee shall coordinate and supervise the activities of the Advisory Board.

§ 6. **Functions of Advisory Board.** The functions and duties of the Advisory Board shall be limited to:

a. evaluating the regulatory procedures and operations of City agencies that affect New York City's small business community;

b. making recommendations to the Department of Business Services and the Task Force with respect to the City agency rules designed to promote and foster the growth of small businesses in the City;

c. making recommendations to the Department of Business Services and the Task Force with respect to issues which have a significant impact on the small business community; and

d. undertaking other activities and measures to enhance cooperation between the City and the small business community as directed by the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development.

§ 7. **Membership.** Members of the Advisory Board shall be selected by the Commissioner of Business Services upon consultation with the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development. The Advisory Board shall consist of small business owners, including those persons, firms, corporations, or other enterprises which operate small businesses; industry, merchants, and trade associations; and other organizations which represent small businesses in the City. There shall be at least twenty-five and no more than fifty members on the Advisory Board. Advisory Board members shall serve for a term set by the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development.

§ 8. Executive Order No. 30, dated October 2, 1991, is repealed.

§ 9. **Effective Date.** This Order shall take effect immediately.

title: EXECUTIVE ORDERS OF THE MAYOR OF NEW YORK
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDERS OF THE MAYOR OF NEW YORK

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 4

April 4, 1994

Mayor's Advisory Committee On Appointments

By the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Committee Established. The Mayor's Advisory Committee on appointments (hereinafter called the "Committee") hereby is established to assist the Mayor in the recruitment and evaluation of highly qualified candidates of superior ability for appointment, and to evaluate incumbent members for reappointment, to the following commissions and boards: Art Commission, Board of Health (other than the chair), Board of Standards and Appeals, City Planning Commission (other than the chair), Conflicts of Interest Board, Hardship Appeals Panel, Landmarks Preservation Commission, Tax Commission, Taxi and Limousine Commission, the public members of the Environmental Control Board, and the Campaign Finance Board (other than the chair), and any other commission, board or public body as shall be determined by the Mayor, from time to time in his discretion.

Section 2. Committee Membership.

(a) The Committee shall be appointed by the Mayor and shall consist of nine members, including a Chair, each residing or having a principal place of business in the City of New York. The Committee Chair may, in his discretion designate adjunct members who shall function under section three as voting members with regard to appointments and reappointments to specific commissions, boards or other public bodies. Adjunct members, if so designated, shall have such expertise or knowledge as will assist the Committee in making a reasoned, informed and impartial evaluation of candidates for the offices referred to in section two. If so designated, there shall be, in the discretion of the Committee Chair, no more than four adjunct members for each commission board or other public body for which candidates are evaluated.

(b) Members shall be appointed (and reappointed) for two year periods in the discretion of the Mayor, except that the term of the initial nine members appointed hereunder shall expire on December 31, 1995. Any member whose term has expired may continue to serve at the pleasure of the Mayor until such time as the member is reappointed or a successor is appointed. The Mayor shall designate the Committee Chair. Adjunct members shall function under section four as voting members until the appointments or reappointments for which they have been designated become final, and such adjunct members may be redesignated at the discretion of the Committee Chair.

(c) No person shall be considered or evaluated by the Committee for any position covered by this Order while serving as a member of the Committee. In the event that the Committee deter mines to consider any member of the Committee for appointment and the member consents to being considered for appointment, then said member shall resign from the Committee immediately and shall be precluded from participating in the functions of the Committee in any respect. The Mayor shall fill the vacancy created by said resigning member as promptly as reasonably practicable.

Section 3. Functions. The Committee shall:

(a) Recruit for consideration persons of superior abilities who are highly qualified for appointment to the offices referred to in section two, receive recommendations of persons for consideration as provided by law, and accept applications from persons seeking appointment to such offices;

EXECUTIVE ORDERS OF THE MAYOR OF NEW YORK

(b) Evaluate and conduct all necessary inquiry to identify those persons whose character, ability, training, experience, temperament and commitment to public service highly qualify them for such offices;

(c) Refer to the Department of Investigation for screening all persons the Committee proposes to nominate for appointment;

(d) Assist the Mayor in the selection of persons for the offices referred to in section two by nominating for consideration by the Mayor three or more candidates for appointment to any vacancy arising in an office referred to in section two, and submit to the Mayor such information as may be necessary to inform the Mayor of the qualifications of each nominee; provided, that when pursuant to law the Mayor receives nominations for appointments from other persons or bodies, the Committee, at the request of the Mayor, shall consider such nominations and report its recommendation in favor of or against the appointment of such persons to the Mayor; and provided, further, that if there is more than one vacancy on any commission, board or other public body or more than one initial appointment to be made to a new commission, board, or public body, the Committee may submit fewer than three nominations for each vacancy or initial appointment; unless the Mayor specifically requests three nominations;

(c) Evaluate the qualifications of incumbents in offices referred to in section two for reappointment and report the Committee's recommendation to the Mayor, provided that if the Committee shall recommend against reappointment it shall nominate three or more candidates for appointment to the office.

(f) Act expeditiously to assure that nominations are timely made, and begin the process of considering nominees for a vacancy before the term of the incumbent expires.

(g) In the event that the Mayor may choose to make an appointment or reappointment directly to an office referred to in section two, then the Chief of Staff to the Mayor, or such other person acting under authority of the Mayor, promptly shall notify the Chair of the Committee of the Mayor's intention to fill such vacancy directly.

Section 4. Continuing Validity of Nominations. After a nominee is appointed, the remaining nominations shall be valid for appointment to any vacancy occurring in that commission, board or other public body within six months after their sub mission to the Mayor; provided, however, that the Committee may nominate additional persons to fill any such vacancy, and may renominate persons for any such vacancy occurring more than six months after its prior submission.

Section 5. Confidentiality. All Committee communications concerning the qualifications of candidates shall be made and held in confidence, except if disclosure is necessary and proper to the conduct of Committee business.

Section 6. Committee Action and Procedure. The Committee may adopt such procedures and policies as it may deem appropriate to its functions, including standards for evaluating the qualifications of candidates for nomination and criteria for recommending the reappointment of incumbents.

Section 7. Financing and Staff.

(a) Members of the Committee shall receive no compensation for their service as members.

(b) The Committee shall be provided with paid staff and sufficient facilities to carry out its functions.

(c) Members of the Committee shall be reimbursed for necessary expenses incurred in connection with the responsibilities of the Committee.

Section 8. Chief of Staff. The Chief of Staff to the Mayor shall maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Committee, and shall advise the Mayor and the Committee regarding measures which may enhance the ability of the Committee to con-

EXECUTIVE ORDERS OF THE MAYOR OF NEW YORK

sider the best qualified candidates for appointment to commissions, boards and other
public bodies.

Section 9. Prior Orders Revoked. Executive Order No. 5, dated January 23, 1990, and Executive Order No. 19, dated September 19, 1990, hereby are repealed.

Section 10. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

Rudolph W. Giuliani
MAYOR

title: NEW YORK CITY EMPOWERMENT ZONE
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 5

APRIL 7, 1994

NEW YORK CITY EMPOWERMENT ZONE

WHEREAS, Subchapter C of Title XIII of the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1993, Public Law 103-66 (the "Act"), authorizes the establishment of an Empowerment Zone Program under which communities of not more than 200,000 people may be designated to receive special investment and training credits and special funding for social services to enhance the economic self-sufficiency of residents of the zone; and

WHEREAS, the Act authorizes local and state governments, or economic development corporations chartered by the states, to nominate areas for designation as Empowerment Zones; and

WHEREAS, the communities of Harlem and the South Bronx, comprising the areas to be specified further in the application for Empowerment Zone designation, contain numerous residents in need of special investment and training credits and special funding for social services to enhance their economic self-sufficiency, and otherwise meet the eligibility criteria for designation as an Empowerment Zone under the Act; and

WHEREAS, the City of New York and the State of New York have determined to nominate the Harlem and South Bronx communities for designation as an Empowerment Zone under the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act; and

WHEREAS, the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act mandates that the designated community must be a full partner in the strategic planning process leading to submission of an application for designation of Empowerment Zone status; and

WHEREAS, the participation of various City agencies in the strategic planning process is necessary to the preparation of an application for designation of the Harlem and South Bronx communities as an Empowerment Zone;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. Strategic Planning and Application Process.

a. The nominated communities of Harlem and the South Bronx shall be made full partners in the strategic planning process for the application for Empowerment Zone status, and New York City's officials, coordinated by the Executive Director of the Economic Policy and Marketing Group under the direction of the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development, will act appropriately to insure that this condition is met.

b. New York City shall act to ensure that the strategic planning process reflects the views of residents of the Zone, representatives of the business community, and organizations concerned with the economic development and social services needs of the area. The strategic planning process shall include public hearings, solicitation of written proposals, and effective outreach efforts.

Section 2. Empowerment Zone Advisory Committee.

An advisory committee appointed by the Mayor in consultation with locally elected officials shall be established to assist the City in developing the application and the implementation strategies under the strategic plan. The Advisory Committee shall include representatives of the Harlem Urban Development Corporation, the Bronx Overall Economic Development Corporation, the State Department of Economic Development, the New York State Urban Development Corporation, the business community, and other representatives of appropriate social services and economic development organizations.

Section 3. Empowerment Zone Inter-Agency Working Group.

a. The Empowerment Zone Inter-Agency Working Group ("Working Group") is hereby continued in order to act as a liaison to coordinate the participation of City agencies in the strategic planning process.

b. The Working Group shall be coordinated by the Executive Director of the Economic Policy and Marketing Group under the direction of the Deputy Mayor for Finance and Economic Development.

c. The membership of the Working Group shall continue in effect and shall consist of representatives of the following City agencies and divisions of the Office of the Mayor:

I. Department of Business Services;

II. Department of City Planning;

III. Economic Policy and Marketing Group;

IV. Department of Employment;

V. Mayor's Federal Affairs Office;

VI. Department of Housing, Preservation and Development;

VII. Human Resources Administration;

VIII. Office of Management and Budget;

IX. Police Department;

The Economic Development Corporation shall be invited to participate in the Working Group.

Section 4. Cooperation of City Agencies. All City Agencies should provide the Working Group with such information and other assistance as it may require for purposes of the strategic planning process and preparation of the application for designation of Empowerment Zone status.

Section 5. Prior Order Repealed. Executive Order No. 61, dated December 23, 1993, is hereby repealed.

Section 6. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

Rudolph W. Giuliani
Mayor

Section 2. Empowerment Zone Advisory Committee.

An advisory committee appointed by the Mayor in consultation with locally elected officials shall be established to assist the City in developing the application and the implementation strategies under the strategic plan. a. The Empowerment Zone Inter-Agency Working Group ("Working Group") is hereby continued in order to act as a liaison to coordinate the participation of City agencies in the strategic planning process.

I. Department of Business Services;

II. Department of City Planning;

III. Economic Policy and Marketing Group;

IV. Department of Employment;

V. Mayor's Federal Affairs Office;

VI. Department of Housing, Preservation and Development;

VII. Human Resources Administration;

VIII. Office of Management and Budget;

IX. Police Department;

The Economic Development Corporation shall be invited to participate in the Working Group.

Section 4. Cooperation of City Agencies. All City Agencies should provide the Working Group with such information and other assistance as it may require for purposes of the strategic planning process and preparation of the application for designation of Empowerment Zone status.

Section 5. Prior Order Repealed. Executive Order No. 61, dated December 23, 1993, is hereby repealed.

Section 6. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

Rudolph W. Giuliani
Mayor

THE CITY OF NEW YORK

NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 7

April 12, 1994

Special Counsel to the Mayor for the Fiscal Oversight of Education

WHEREAS, City Charter § 106(c) provides that "[t]he mayor shall keep informed, during the course of each fiscal year, of the progress of expenditures and the receipt of revenues, and it shall be the duty of all agencies, when requested by the mayor, to supply all information needed for this purpose", and this section of the Charter applies to the fiscal and budgetary administration of the Board of Education; and

WHEREAS, City Charter § 803(a) authorizes the Mayor to direct the Commissioner of the Department of Investigation to make any investigation, and subdivision (b) of that section authorizes the Commissioner of the Department of Investigation to "...make any study or investigation which in his opinion may be in the best interests of the city, including

but not limited to investigations of the affairs, functions, accounts, methods, personnel or efficiency of any agency", and the exercise of these powers by the Commissioner of the Department of Investigation applies to the Board of Education; and

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Special Counsel to the Mayor for the Fiscal Oversight of Education.

There is hereby created the position of Special Counsel to the Mayor for the Fiscal Oversight of Education (hereafter "Special Counsel"), whose duty it shall be to oversee the budgetary procedures and finances of the Board of Education of the City of New York and of the overall City School District of the City of New York. The Special Counsel shall be a Special Deputy Commissioner of the Department of Investigation, and shall receive no compensation, other than reimbursement for actual and necessary expenses incurred in carrying out the duties of the position.

Section 2. Powers and Duties. (a) The Special Counsel shall issue periodic reports to the Mayor on the budgetary procedures and finances of the Board of Education of the City of New York and of the overall City School District of the City of New York, including an accurate accounting of the allocation of resources and personnel of the City School District of the City of New York.

(b) In carrying out his or her duties, the Special Counsel shall obtain from the City School District of the City of New York, including the Board of Education, the Chancellor, the Community School Boards, the Community Superintendent, and any other officer or employee of the school district, all information and data, including computer records, necessary to prepare the reports provided for in subdivision (a) of this section. The Special Counsel is authorized to consult with and obtain the assistance of foundations, graduate schools of education and other knowledgeable persons or entities in exercising his or her functions, and may retain independent consultants to provide assistance in the performance of his or her duties.

(c) In the exercise of the duties set forth herein, the Special Counsel shall review and analyze the relevant records, information, data bases, reports, plans, projections and any other relevant materials of the City School District of the City of New York.

(d) The Department of Investigation, the Office of Management and Budget and other Mayoral agencies shall provide to the Special Counsel such personnel, facilities and other assistance necessary to enable the Special Counsel to carry out his or her responsibilities.

Section 3. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

title: THE MAYOR’S COMMISSION TO COMBAT FAMILY VIOLENCE
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 8

April 26, 1994

THE MAYOR'S COMMISSION TO COMBAT FAMILY VIOLENCE
(Executive Order No. 58, dated 11/29/93, Repealed)

WHEREAS, it is estimated that family violence affects as many as 279,300 households in New York City every year; and

WHEREAS, family violence is a public health crisis that respects no boundaries of race, ethnicity, age, gender, sexual orientation, or economic status; and

WHEREAS, a priority of this administration is combatting family violence; and

WHEREAS, the City has incorporated family violence prevention into the New York City Police Department's policing programs; and

WHEREAS, the development of an integrated approach to the problem of family violence and the coordination of existing systems and services are critical to the success of the City's efforts in this area;

NOW THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it hereby is ordered;

Section. 1. Prior Order Repealed. Executive Order No. 58 of 1993, dated November 29, 1993, hereby is repealed.

Section 2. Establishment of a Coordinating Commission. There hereby is established in the Mayor's Office for Health Services a Mayor's Family Violence Coordinating Commission (the "Coordinating Commission"). The Director of the Mayor's Office for Health Services and the Criminal Justice Coordinator, or their designees, shall

serve as chairpersons of the Coordinating Commission and shall coordinate and supervise its activities. The Coordinating Commission shall report to the Deputy Mayor for Operations.

Section 3. Membership.

(a) The following City agencies, commissions and divisions of the Office of the Mayor shall be members of the Coordinating Commission:

1. Department of Health

2. Human Resources Administration
(Child Welfare Administration,
Adult Services Administrator,
Family Support Administration)

3. Police Department

4. Department for the Aging

5. Department of Youth Services

6. Department of Probation

7. Department of Mental Health, Retardation and Alcoholism Services

8. Law Department

9. Department of Homeless Services

10. Commission on the Status of Women.

(b) The Health and Hospitals Corporation, the Board of Education and the New York City Housing Authority shall be invited to attend meetings of the Coordinating Commission and to participate in the initiatives of the Coordinating Commission, as may be appropriate in the discretion of the chairpersons. The Coordinating Commission may seek the participation of experts or interested parties, including representatives of the New York City Courts, as the chairpersons may determine in their discretion.

(c) The head of each member entity shall designate a senior level administrator to attend Coordinating Commission meetings and to be responsible for carrying out the terms of this Executive Order.

(d) The Mayor may appoint such other person or persons as the Mayor deems appropriate to serve as Commission members, regardless of whether such persons are employed by the City.

(e) The Coordinating Commission shall meet no less than once each quarter.

Section 4. Purpose. The Coordinating Commission shall:

(a) Formulate policies and programs relating to all aspects of services and protocols for victims of family violence;

(b) Develop methods to improve the coordination of systems and services for victims of family violence;

(c) Develop and maintain mechanisms to ensure that each affected City agency responds appropriately to family violence situations and that there is coordination among the agencies involved; and

(d) Launch public education campaigns to heighten awareness of family violence and its devastating effects on society.

Section 5. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

Rudolph W. Giuliani
Mayor
