title: REPORTING OF NEW ADDRESSES, STREETS, AND OTHER LOCATIONS TO EMERGENCY RESPONSE AGENCIES
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 39
REPORTING OF NEW ADDRESSES, STREETS, AND OTHER LOCATIONS TO EMERGENCY RESPONSE AGENCIES

September 9, 1997

WHEREAS, the Police Department, the Fire Department, and the Emergency Medical Service (the "Emergency Response Agencies") maintain computerized databases of addresses and other locations within the City of New York for purposes of enabling such agencies to respond to emergencies that occur within the City of New York; and

WHEREAS, it is imperative that the computerized databases on which Emergency Response Agencies rely in locating emergencies to which they respond be comprehensive and accurate; and

WHEREAS, the Borough Presidents have agreed to assist in the process of updating the Emergency Response Agencies' computerized databases of addresses and other locations by timely transmitting to such agencies information concerning the construction of new developments and/or streets and official address changes and new house numbers within their respective boroughs;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Definitions:

"Mapped Street": a street that is contained in the current city map referred to in
section 198 of the New York City Charter.

"Unmapped Street": a street that is not contained in the current city map referred
to in section 198 of the New York City Charter.

§2. The Department of Buildings shall require that an applicant for the following
permits and certificates certify that such applicant has provided the Emergency Response
Agencies and the Department of City Planning with a site plan that shows the nearest Mapped
Streets that are open and in use and shows the access route from such Mapped Streets to the
subject building or location:

a. a building permit relating to a new building on either (i) a subdivided zoning lot or (ii) a zoning lot that fronts a private street, an Unmapped Street, or a Mapped Street that is not open;

b. an alteration permit relating to the alteration of an existing building on either (i) a subdivided zoning lot or (ii) a zoning lot that fronts a private street, an Unmapped Street, or a Mapped Street that is not open;

c. a foundation permit, excavation permit, and/or land contour permit relating to work on either (i) a subdivided zoning lot or (ii) a zoning lot that fronts a private street, an Unmapped Street, or a Mapped Street that is not open; and

d. a temporary certificate of occupancy, or a permanent certificate of occupancy if no temporary certificate of occupancy was obtained, relating to a building on either (i) a subdivided zoning lot or (ii) a zoning lot that

fronts a private street, an Unmapped Street, or a Mapped Street that is not
open.

§3. Within five (5) business days of receipt of the information from an applicant referred to in Section 2 hereof, the Emergency Response Agencies shall ensure that the location identified by such information appears in their computer databases of addresses and other locations.

§4. The Department of Transportation shall require that an applicant for a permit relating to a street that does not appear in the Department of Transportation's database of street names certify that such applicant has provided the Emergency Response Agencies and the Department of City Planning with a site plan that includes the nearest Mapped Streets that are open and in use and shows the access route from such Mapped Streets to the subject street.

§5. Within five (5) business days of receipt of the information from an applicant referred to in Section 4 hereof, the Emergency Response Agencies shall ensure that the location identified by such information appears in their computer databases of addresses and other locations.

§6. The Department of City Planning will immediately make available to the Emergency Response Agencies each release of its Geosupport System through such system's installation at the computer service center of the Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications.

§7. The Emergency Response Agencies and the Department of City Planning each shall advise the Department of Transportation and the Department of Buildings of the name, office, address, telephone number, and facsimile transmission number of the person to whom the information required to be transmitted by this Order is to be transmitted.

§8. The Mayor's Office of Emergency Management shall coordinate the implementation of this Order. All agencies shall cooperate with and provide assistance to The Mayor's Office of Emergency Management for the purpose of achieving the objectives of this Order.

§9. This Order shall take effect immediately.

title: NOTIFICATION AND PROCESSING OF CIVILIAN COMPLAINTS
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 40

October 21, 1997

NOTIFICATION AND PROCESSING OF CIVILIAN COMPLAINTS

WHEREAS, the Civilian Complaint Review Board is charged with the legislative mandate to fairly and independently investigate certain allegations of police misconduct toward members of the public; and

WHEREAS, it is of the utmost importance that members of the public and the New York City Police Department have confidence in the professionalism and impartiality of the Civilian Complaint Review Board; and

WHEREAS, pursuant to the Charter, and the Rules of the CCRB the individuals who have filed complaints with the Civilian Complaint Review Board have the right to be kept apprised of both the status and results of their complaints brought against members of the New York City Police Department; and

WHEREAS, it is important to investigate and resolve civilian complaints in a timely manner; and

WHEREAS, the sharing of information between the Civilian Complaint Review Board and the New York City Police Department is essential to the effective investigation of civilian complaints;

NOW THEREFORE, by the power invested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it hereby is ordered:

Section 1. Notice to Civilian Complainants. The Commissioner of the New York City Police Department and the Civilian Complaint Review Board shall expeditiously:

a. Establish standards for providing timely written notice to civilian complainants regarding the status of civilian complaints during the stages of the Civilian Complaint Review Board's review and investigation process, including final Board action on the pending complaint.

b. Establish standards for providing timely written notice to civilian complainants regarding the disposition of all cases referred for disciplinary action by the Civilian Complaint Review Board to the Commissioner for the New York City Police Department, including the result of all such referred cases.

c. The standards established shall require that complainants be given a name, address and telephone number of an individual to contact in order to give or obtain information.

Section 2. The Police Commissioner and the Civilian Complaint Review Board shall establish standards for the timely processing and resolution of civilian complaints and the sharing of necessary information between the agencies.

Section 3. This order shall take effect immediately.

title: MAYOR’S ADVISORY TASK FORCE ON THE CITY UNIVERSITY OF NEW YORK
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 41

May 6, 1998

MAYOR'S ADVISORY
TASK FORCE ON THE
CITY UNIVERSITY OF NEW YORK

WHEREAS, the City University of New York ("CUNY") was established to provide publicly subsidized higher education with a commitment to academic excellence for the residents of the City of New York; and

WHEREAS, recent graduation rates and other measurements of educational quality and performance indicate that CUNY's current policies and practices have not maintained the high level of educational quality that CUNY should be providing to its students; and

WHEREAS, to ensure that the City's financial resources support a meaningful and productive level of college instruction that meets the needs of the students of the City, a detailed examination of CUNY's policies and practices is required;

NOW THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it hereby is ordered:

Section 1. Establishment of the Task Force. There hereby is established the Mayor's Advisory Task Force on the City University of New York (the "Task Force"). The Task Force shall include members appointed by the Mayor, who shall be residents of the City of New York or shall maintain a place of business in the City of New York. The Mayor, at his discretion, may appoint a Chair of the Task Force. Members of the Task Force shall serve without compensation.

2. Purposes of the Task Force. The Task Force shall review, examine, audit and make recommendations regarding: (1) the uses of City funding by CUNY, (2) the effects of open admissions and remedial education on CUNY, and on CUNY's capacity to provide college level courses and curricula of high quality to its students, (3) the best

means of arranging for third-parties to provide remediation services to ensure that prospective CUNY students can perform college level work prior to their admission to CUNY, and (4) the implementation of other reform measures as may be appropriate. No later than 180 days after the effective date of this Order, the Task Force shall report its findings and recommendations to the Mayor.

3. Powers of the Task Force. (a) In carrying out its mandate, the Task Force may consult with third parties as it deems appropriate and may hold public hearings, and shall obtain all information and data necessary to fulfill the purposes identified by section 2 of this Order, including information from CUNY and the colleges in the CUNY system.

(b) Any investigations or hearings described in this section may include the issuance of subpoenas by the Department of Investigation in accordance with DOI's powers under Chapter 34 of the City Charter, to the extent the Commissioner of DOI and the Task Force jointly determine is appropriate.

(c) The Task Force shall be authorized to retain an Executive Director and such other staff, including outside consultants as may be necessary, from appropriations made available therefor.

(d) The Task Force is empowered to act by a majority of its members.

4. Agency Assistance and Cooperation. All City agencies, including the Office of Management and Budget, the Department of Investigation and the Law Department, shall cooperate in providing to the Task Force such personnel, facilities, information and other assistance as is necessary and required by the Task Force to carry out its responsibilities.

5. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 41

May 6, 1998

MAYOR'S ADVISORY
TASK FORCE ON THE
CITY UNIVERSITY OF NEW YORK

WHEREAS, the City University of New York ("CUNY") was established to provide publicly subsidized higher education with a commitment to academic excellence for the residents of the City of New York; and

WHEREAS, recent graduation rates and other measurements of educational quality and performance indicate that CUNY's current policies and practices have not maintained the high level of educational quality that CUNY should be providing to its students; and

WHEREAS, to ensure that the City's financial resources support a meaningful and productive level of college instruction that meets the needs of the students of the City, a detailed examination of CUNY's policies and practices is required;

NOW THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it hereby is ordered:

Section 1. Establishment of the Task Force. There hereby is established the Mayor's Advisory Task Force on the City University of New York (the "Task Force"). The Task Force shall include members appointed by the Mayor, who shall be residents of the City of New York or shall maintain a place of business in the City of New York. The Mayor, at his discretion, may appoint a Chair of the Task Force. Members of the Task Force shall serve without compensation.

2. Purposes of the Task Force. The Task Force shall review, examine, audit and make recommendations regarding: (1) the uses of City funding by CUNY, (2) the effects of open admissions and remedial education on CUNY, and on CUNY's capacity to provide college level courses and curricula of high quality to its students, (3) the best

means of arranging for third-parties to provide remediation services to ensure that prospective CUNY students can perform college level work prior to their admission to CUNY, and (4) the implementation of other reform measures as may be appropriate. No later than 180 days after the effective date of this Order, the Task Force shall report its findings and recommendations to the Mayor.

3. Powers of the Task Force. (a) In carrying out its mandate, the Task Force may consult with third parties as it deems appropriate and may hold public hearings, and shall obtain all information and data necessary to fulfill the purposes identified by section 2 of this Order, including information from CUNY and the colleges in the CUNY system.

(b) Any investigations or hearings described in this section may include the issuance of subpoenas by the Department of Investigation in accordance with DOI's powers under Chapter 34 of the City Charter, to the extent the Commissioner of DOI and the Task Force jointly determine is appropriate.

(c) The Task Force shall be authorized to retain an Executive Director and such other staff, including outside consultants as may be necessary, from appropriations made available therefor.

(d) The Task Force is empowered to act by a majority of its members.

4. Agency Assistance and Cooperation. All City agencies, including the Office of Management and Budget, the Department of Investigation and the Law Department, shall cooperate in providing to the Task Force such personnel, facilities, information and other assistance as is necessary and required by the Task Force to carry out its responsibilities.

5. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

title: DEPARTMENT OF THE HOMELESS
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 42

July 7, 1998

DEPARTMENT OF THE HOMELESS

WHEREAS, prior to the enactment of Local Law No. 51 for the year 1993, services for homeless individuals and families were provided by the Department of Social Services under the direction of the New York City Commissioner of Social Services pursuant to the New York Social Services Law and Chapter 24 of the New York City Charter ("Charter"); and

WHEREAS, Local Law No. 51 for the year 1993 enacted Chapter 24-A of the Charter, which established the Department of Homeless Services and provided for the Commissioner of Homeless Services to have the "powers and perform the duties of a commissioner of social services under the social services law for the purposes of fulfilling his or her responsibilities under this chapter", and also enacted Title 21-A of the Administrative Code, entitled "Department of Homeless Services"; and

WHEREAS, such local law provided for Chapter 24-A of the Charter and Title 21-A of the Administrative Code to expire on July 1, 1995; and

WHEREAS, Local Law No. 61 for the year 1995 amended Local Law No. 51 for the year 1993 to postpone the expiration of Chapter 24-A and Title 21-A until September 6, 1995; and

WHEREAS, Local Law No. 75 for the year 1995 extended the life of Chapter 24-A and provided for such chapter to expire on July 1, 1998, and renumbered Title 21-A of the Administrative Code as Chapter 3 of Title 21 of such Code and provided for such chapter to expire on July 1, 1998; and

WHEREAS, Local Law No. 75 for the year 1995 provided that the Department of Homeless Services should expire on July 1, 1998 and that "the functions, powers and duties of the Department of Homeless Services set forth in chapter 24-A of the New York city charter and chapter 3 of title 21 of the administrative code of the city of New York ... shall devolve upon the department of social services..."; and

WHEREAS, legislation to further extend Chapter 24-A of the Charter and Chapter 3 of Title 21 of the Administrative Code has yet to be enacted into law; and

WHEREAS, the Mayor is committed to continuing and supporting the structure that has provided services to homeless individuals and families and has implemented numerous improvements to such services; and

WHEREAS, the Mayor wishes to prevent any disruption of such services, and to this end has directed the Commissioner of Homeless Services to continue to administer the provision of services to homeless individuals and families as of July 1, 1998;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. There shall be within the Department of Social Services a unit for homeless services, which shall be called the Department of Homeless Services. The unit shall be headed by a Deputy Commissioner of the Department of Social Services who shall have the title Commissioner of Homeless Services, and shall report to the Mayor through the Deputy Mayor designated by the Mayor with regard to all matters relating to this Order. The Commissioner of Homeless Services shall possess the qualifications of a Deputy Commissioner of Social Services as established pursuant to the Social Services Law.

Section 2. The Commissioner of Homeless Services, to the maximum extent consistent with existing law, shall be responsible for:

a. Directing and supervising the management, operations, budget and funding of services for homeless individuals and families;

b. Working directly with the City's Office of Management and Budget with regard to the funding and administration of the City's budget for services to homeless individuals and families;

c. Administering all contracts entered into by the Department of Homeless Services, including contracts entered into prior to the effective date of this Order;

d. Advising and assisting the Mayor with respect to matters pertaining to homeless individuals and families; and

e. Performing such other duties as the Mayor may assign.

Section 3. The Department of Homeless Services within the Department of Social Services shall have the power to continue any business, proceeding or other matter commenced by the Department of Homeless Services heretofore. Any provision in any law, rule, regulation, contract, grant or other document relating to the Department of Homeless Services

described in Chapter 24-A of the Charter and Chapter 3 of Title 21 of the Administrative Code
shall apply to the Department of Homeless Services within the Department of Social Services.

Section 4. This order shall take effect immediately and shall be deemed to have
been in full force and effect as of July 1, 1998.

title: ESTABLISHMENT OF THE OFFICE FOR THE MILLENNIUM
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 45

December 28, 1998

ESTABLISHMENT OF THE OFFICE FOR THE MILLENNIUM

WHEREAS, people throughout the world anticipate celebration of the new millennium with the hope and expectation that it will usher in an era of peace and prosperity; and

WHEREAS, the stature of New York City as the undisputed financial and cultural capital of the world, attracting visitors and tourists from across the nation and around the world, makes it particularly appropriate for the City to host cultural activities and events in celebration of the millennium; and

WHEREAS, it is necessary and appropriate that the City government establish an office within the office of the Mayor to lead the effort to plan and coordinate the activities and events that will take place in the City in celebration of the millennium;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Establishment of the Office for the Millennium. (1) There is hereby established within the Office of the Mayor, the Office for the Millennium.

(2) The Mayor shall appoint a City employee to be the executive director of the Office for the Millennium and such other staff as in his judgment shall be necessary to carry out the functions of such office.

§ 2. Establishment of Committee for NYC 2000. There shall be a committee consisting of not less than twenty persons, which shall be led by one or more chairpersons, to be appointed by the Mayor from among persons in the public and private sectors. The committee shall be responsible for promoting and implementing a public/private partnership effort to be known as "NYC 2000" for the public celebration of the millennium in New York City. The committee shall include an executive sub-committee consisting of not less than three members of the committee, to be designated by the Mayor, at least one of whom shall be a city employee. The executive sub-committee shall be responsible for overseeing and directing the operations of the Office for the Millennium and the committee. The committee may form such other sub-committees as it may deem necessary to carry out its functions and responsibilities. The members of the committee shall serve without compensation.

§ 3. Purpose and functions of the Office for the Millennium. (1) The office shall, in cooperation with city agencies, other government agencies, not-for-profit corporations and persons and businesses in the private sector, encourage, plan and promote cultural activities and public events to celebrate the millennium.

(2) In carrying out its responsibilities the office shall work jointly with New York City Public/Private Initiatives Inc. on fund-raising activities.

§ 4. **Agency Assistance.** All agencies shall cooperate in providing to the office such personnel, facilities, information and other assistance as is necessary and required by the office to carry out its responsibilities.

§ 5. **Effective date.** This order shall take effect immediately.

title: PROCLAMATION OF A STATE OF EMERGENCY
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 47

December 14, 1999

PROCLAMATION OF A STATE OF EMERGENCY

Whereas, Employees of the New York City Transit Authority and the Manhattan and Bronx Surface Transit Operating Authority have threatened to commence an unlawful strike on December 15, 1999, and such strike would effectively cease all subway and bus services provided by the New York City Transit Authority and the Manhattan and Bronx Surface Transit Operating Authority; and

Whereas, It is necessary to insure public safety and the orderly transportation of people and goods in the City of New York; and

Whereas, The threatened strike would cause an increase in the response time of emergency vehicles which will endanger the lives and health of the City's residents, commuters and visitors, the loss of instructional time for more than one million students, wide-scale inability to gain access to routine medical care, massive disruptions in the criminal and civil court systems, the loss of wages for hundreds of thousands of persons, the loss, on a daily basis, of hundreds of millions of dollars for businesses in the City, and millions of dollars per day of lost revenues for the City and the Board of Education, and millions of dollars per day in increased expenditures by the City of New York;

Whereas, These circumstances constitute an imminent peril to the public health and safety requiring the adoption of special rules, regulations, procedures and restrictions as emergency measures; and

Whereas, Executive Law §24 authorizes the Mayor to promulgate local emergency orders upon a finding that the public safety is imperiled by the event of a public emergency or in the event of reasonable apprehension of immediate danger thereof, to protect life and property and to bring an emergency situation under control;

Now, therefore, by the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. State of Emergency. A state of emergency is hereby declared to exist within the City of New York.

§ 2. Manhattan traffic restrictions.

a. During the hours designated by the Commissioner of Transportation or the Director of the Mayor's Office of Emergency Management in consultation with the Police Commissioner, all private passenger vehicles containing fewer than three persons (including the driver) are hereby prohibited from entering that portion of Manhattan situated south of 96th Street from the East River to the Hudson River by any street, highway, bridge or tunnel.

b. Reserved arterial roadways

(1) The following are designated as reserved arterial roadways:

(a) Fifth Avenue between 96th and 23rd Streets

(b) Madison Avenue between 23rd and 57th Streets

(c) Broad Street, from South Street to Wall Street

(d) Nassau Street, from Wall Street to Spruce Street

(e) Liberty Street, from West Street to Maiden Lane

(f) Maiden Lane, Liberty Street to South Street

(g) 29th Street from First Avenue to Twelfth Avenue

(h) 30th Street from First Avenue to Twelfth Avenue

(i) 49th Street from First Avenue to Twelfth Avenue

(j) 50th Street from First Avenue to Twelfth Avenue

(2) During the hours designated by the Commissioner of Transportation or the Director of the Mayor's Office of Emergency Management in consultation with the Police Commissioner, reserved arterial roadways may be used only by buses, taxis and for-hire vehicles, Access-a-Ride vehicles, ambulettes and emergency vehicles.

(3) During the hours designated by the Commissioner of Transportation or the Director of the Mayor's Office of Emergency Management in consultation with the Police Commissioner, all parking privileges within the reserved arterial roadways are suspended, with the exception of privileges granted to persons holding a New York City Special Vehicle Identification permit (unless such permits have been suspended pursuant to paragraph (4) of this section), and the privilege of using truck-loading areas for trucks actually loading and unloading.

(4) The Commissioner of Transportation is authorized to suspend privileges granted to persons holding a New York City Special Vehicle Identification permit with regard to parking on a reserved arterial roadway.

§ 3. Additional occupancy requirements for private passenger vehicles

During the hours designated by the Commissioner of Transportation or the Director of the Mayor's Office of Emergency Management in consultation with the Police Commissioner, private passenger vehicles with fewer than three occupants (including the driver) are prohibited on the following roadways:

(1) Westbound LIE from west of the Grand Central Parkway to the Queens Midtown Tunnel

(2) Westbound Bruckner Expressway from the Bruckner Interchange to the Triboro Bridge

(3) Southbound Harlem River Drive from Dyckman Street to the Triboro Bridge

(4) Southbound FDR Drive from the Harlem River Drive to 73rd Street

(5) Southbound Henry Hudson Parkway from Mosholu Parkway to the George Washington Bridge

(6) Northbound Belt Parkway from 4th Avenue to the merge with the Gowanus Expressway at 60th Street

(7) Northbound Gowanus Expressway from 92nd Street to the interchange with the BQE, provided that the Bus/HOV EZ Pass Lane is designated for Access-a-Ride vehicles, ambulettes, buses or vans carrying 15 or more passengers, and emergency vehicles only

(8) Eastbound BQE from the Gowanus Expressway to the Manhattan Bridge

(9) Northbound Prospect Expressway from Church Avenue to the Gowanus Expressway

§ 4. Restrictions on buses.

a. During the hours designated by the Commissioner of Transportation or the Director of the Mayor's Office of Emergency Management in consultation with the Police Commissioner, private buses having 6 or more wheels and a seating capacity of 15 or more passengers are hereby prohibited from entering Manhattan south of 96th Street except as provided in subdivision b.

b. The following buses shall be permitted to enter Manhattan south of 96th Street:

(1) School buses carrying school students.

(2) Tour buses operating pursuant to a license from the New York City Department of Consumer Affairs.

(3) Interstate common carriers providing normal daily fixed route service authorized by the Federal Highway Administration

(4) Intrastate common carriers providing normal daily fixed route service authorized by the New York State Department of Transportation

(5) Private buses operating pursuant to a franchise or temporary operating authority granted by the City of New York.

(6) Private buses that have been approved to participate in the New York City Transit Strike Contingency Plan and who display an official placard evidencing such approval and participation.

§ 5. Restrictions on ferries.

No private ferry or boat shall be permitted to board or discharge passengers at a City-owned dock or pier unless prior approval has been granted by the Office of Private Ferry Operations of the New York City Department of Transportation.

§ 6. Taxi and for-hire vehicle provisions

The following provisions shall apply to vehicles licensed by the New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission:

(a) All for-hire vehicles and commuter vans licensed as such by the Taxi and Limousine Commission are authorized, for the duration of the emergency, to pick up passengers with or without prearrangement. This shall include but not be limited to the pickup of passengers by street hail.

(b) All commuter vans licensed as such by the Taxi and Limousine Commission are authorized to operate outside of the geographical area set forth in their operation authorization, and are further authorized to accept and discharge passengers on streets which otherwise constitute bus routes and at points which otherwise constitute bus stops.

(c) The Chair of the Taxi and Limousine Commission is authorized, for the duration of the emergency, to suspend the Commission's inspection requirements for any licensed vehicle.

(d) Taxicabs and for-hire vehicles licensed as such by the Taxi and Limousine Commission are directed to pick up passengers from more than one location if such passengers are travelling in the same general direction. Each such passenger, other than a passenger seven years of age or younger or an attendant accompanying a person with a disability, shall pay a fare equal to the difference between the fare applicable when the passenger is discharged and the fare applicable when the passenger enters the vehicle.

(e) Taxicabs, for-hire vehicles and commuter vans licensed as such by the Taxi and Limousine Commission are directed to pick up passengers for group rides at all points designated for that purpose by the Chairperson of the Commission. Buildings designated for business or commercial use shall, notwithstanding the provisions of any lease or similar agreement to the contrary, make arrangements for storage of bicycles within the building or the building's garage, or permit employees working in the building to store bicycles in spaces designated for such purpose by their employers.

§ 8. Any person who knowingly violates any provision of this Order shall be guilty of a class B misdemeanor, which shall be punishable by a fine of $500 or imprisonment not to exceed three months.

Mayor/

OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 47

December 14, 1999

PROCLAMATION OF A STATE OF EMERGENCY

Whereas, Employees of the New York City Transit Authority and the Manhattan and Bronx Surface Transit Operating Authority have threatened to commence an unlawful strike on December 15, 1999, and such strike would effectively cease all subway and bus services provided by the New York City Transit Authority and the Manhattan and Bronx Surface Transit Operating Authority; and

Whereas, It is necessary to insure public safety and the orderly transportation of people and goods in the City of New York; and

Whereas, The threatened strike would cause an increase in the response time of emergency vehicles which will endanger the lives and health of the City's residents, commuters and visitors, the loss of instructional time for more than one million students, wide-scale inability to gain access to routine medical care, massive disruptions in the criminal and civil court systems, the loss of wages for hundreds of thousands of persons, the loss, on a daily basis, of hundreds of millions of dollars for businesses in the City, and millions of dollars per day of lost revenues for the City and the Board of Education, and millions of dollars per day in increased expenditures by the City of New York;

Whereas, These circumstances constitute an imminent peril to the public health and safety requiring the adoption of special rules, regulations, procedures and restrictions as emergency measures; and

Whereas, Executive Law §24 authorizes the Mayor to promulgate local emergency orders upon a finding that the public safety is imperiled by the event of a public emergency or in the event of reasonable apprehension of immediate danger thereof, to protect life and property and to bring an emergency situation under control;

Now, therefore, by the power vested in me as Mayor of The City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. State of Emergency. A state of emergency is hereby declared to exist within the City of New York.

§ 2. Manhattan traffic restrictions.

a. (1) The following are designated as reserved arterial roadways:

(a) Fifth Avenue between 96th and 23rd Streets

(b) Madison Avenue between 23rd and 57th Streets

(c) Broad Street, from South Street to Wall Street

(d) Nassau Street, from Wall Street to Spruce Street

(e) Liberty Street, from West Street to Maiden Lane

(f) Maiden Lane, Liberty Street to South Street

(g) 29th Street from First Avenue to Twelfth Avenue

(h) 30th Street from First Avenue to Twelfth Avenue

(i) 49th Street from First Avenue to Twelfth Avenue

(j) 50th Street from First Avenue to Twelfth Avenue

title: AGENCY INTERNAL AUDIT FUNCTIONS
ESTABLISHMENT OF TRANSIT PASS PROGRAM
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 49
ESTABLISHMENT OF TRANSIT PASS PROGRAM

July 7, 2000

WHEREAS, Federal law authorizes employers to offer their employees the opportunity to elect to use pre-tax earnings to purchase transit passes for use on mass transit facilities; and

WHEREAS, the Office of Labor Relations recently negotiated a citywide collective bargaining agreement with District Council 37 of the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees that offers approximately 160,000 City employees the opportunity to elect to use pre-tax earnings to purchase Metrocards; and

WHEREAS, establishment of a Transit Pass Program that offers City employees who are not represented in collective bargaining the opportunity to elect to use pre-tax earnings to purchase Metrocards would reduce the cost of mass transportation for employees who participate in the Program, thereby making the use of mass transportation by such employees for commuting to and from work and for other purposes a more attractive option; and

WHEREAS, an increase in the use of mass transportation by City employees would reduce automobile use, thereby decreasing automobile emissions in the City as well as wear on City streets;

WHEREAS, City employees who are not represented in collective bargaining
should be offered the opportunity to participate in a Transit Pass Program, both to enjoy the cost
savings and facilitate the environmental benefits associated with a Transit Pass Program, as well
as to achieve equality with the approximately 160,000 City employees who have been offered
the opportunity to elect to use pre-tax earnings to purchase Metrocards;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New
York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Definitions:

"City employees" means elected officials of the City of New York and employees of such officials, including employees of mayoral agencies, provided that such official's or employee's pay is processed by the Office of Payroll Administration, and provided, further, that the term "City employees" shall not include employees who are represented in collective bargaining.

"Transit Pass Program" or "Program" means the program established in
accordance with this Order and other applicable law under which City employees are offered the
opportunity to elect to use pre-tax earnings to purchase Metrocards.

§ 2. <u>Transit Pass Program</u>:

The Office of Payroll Administration, under the direction of the Mayor's Office
of Operations, shall hereby establish and administer a Transit Pass Program.

§ 3. <u>Program Guidelines and Procedures</u>:

The Office of Payroll Administration shall develop appropriate guidelines and procedures to establish and administer the Transit Pass Program including, without limitation, guidelines and procedures that:

a. establish the procedure by which City employees may elect to participate in the Program;

b. establish the amount of earnings that may be used by City employees to purchase Metrocards;

c. establish the commencement date of the Program;

d. establish a fee, if necessary, to be charged to City employees who participate in the Program to cover the cost of establishing and administering the Program; and

e. establish a cost-effective and secure method for multi-point distribution of Metrocards.

§ 4. This Order shall take effect immediately.

Mayor

title: ESTABLISHMENT OF CHARTER SCHOOL IMPROVEMENT FUND COMMITTEE
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 50

NOVEMBER 1, 2000

ESTABLISHMENT OF CHARTER SCHOOL IMPROVEMENT FUND COMMITTEE

WHEREAS, the development and encouragement of charter schools is an important component of efforts to improve the quality of education in New York City, and

WHEREAS, funding has been allocated in the Fiscal Year '01 budget for educational reform strategies and innovations, including the support of charter schools through contributions to capital related and start-up costs of such schools, and

WHEREAS, such funds should be distributed to charter schools that can demonstrate effective and appropriate use of such funds; and

WHEREAS, a committee charged with coordination and oversight of the distribution of such funds, having as its members the Commissioner of the Department of Youth and Community Development, the Commissioner of the Department of Design and Construction and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, can best ensure the success of a charter school grant program;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Establishment of Charter School Improvement Fund Committee. There is hereby established a City of New York Charter School Improvement Fund Committee ("the Committee") reporting to the Mayor, through the Deputy Mayor for Planning, Education and Cultural Affairs. The Committee shall consist of the Commissioner of the Department of Youth and Community Development, who shall serve as Chair, the Commissioner of the Department of Design and Construction and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, or their designees.

Section 2. Functions of the Committee. The Committee shall:

a. Solicit applications from, and at its discretion award grants to, charter schools located in the City of New York for specific capital and start-up projects.

Grants to a charter school in any fiscal year may be in an amount not to exceed $250,000 unless otherwise approved by the Mayor.

b. Consider establishment of performance incentives for the grant program that require the grant recipient charter school, as a condition of receiving its full grant, to meet specific levels of academic achievement and award bonus grants to charter schools that exceed such levels of academic achievement.

c. Require documentation from each charter school grant recipient demonstrating appropriate use of the grant and completion of the project.

Section 3. **Agency Assistance.** All City agencies shall cooperate in providing to the Committee such personnel, facilities, information and other assistance as is necessary and required by the Committee to carry out its responsibilities.

Section 4. **Effective Date.** This order shall take effect immediately.

title: ESTABLISHMENT OF THE OFFICE OF HEALTH INSURANCE ACCESS
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 51

August 29, 2001

ESTABLISHMENT OF THE OFFICE OF HEALTH INSURANCE ACCESS

WHEREAS, the City of New York has a strong commitment to increasing access to and improving health insurance coverage for New Yorkers;

WHEREAS, there are an estimated 900,000 New York City residents eligible for but not enrolled in current or recently enacted public health insurance programs;

WHEREAS, through the City's HealthStat initiative more than 140,000 New Yorkers have been enrolled in available public health insurance programs;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. <u>Office Established</u>

(1) There is hereby established within the Office of the Mayor the Office of Health Insurance Access ("the Office").

(2) The Mayor shall appoint a City employee to be the Executive Director of the Office of Health Insurance Access, and such other staff as in his judgment shall be necessary to carry out the functions of the Office.

Section 2. <u>Purpose and Functions of the Office.</u>

(1) In collaboration with other City agencies, other governmental entities, not-for-profit corporations and persons and businesses from the private sector, the Office shall develop policies and initiatives promoting and improving health insurance coverage in New York City through programs provided by both public and private sector organizations.

(2) In collaboration with City agencies, other government agencies, not-for-profit corporations and persons and businesses from the private sector, the Office shall educate New York City residents about the availability of public health insurance programs, refer potentially eligible residents to enrollers, and/or enroll eligible residents into public health insurance programs.

(3) In cooperation with City agencies and other government agencies, the Office shall work to streamline and simplify the application and re-certifying processes for these programs with the goal of increasing enrollment in these programs while at the same time increasing governmental administrative efficiency.

(4) The Office shall coordinate the administration of the New York Health Purchasing Alliance, a small business purchasing cooperative, established with seed money from the City and offering HealthPass, an insurance option for small businesses. The Office shall explore opportunities for HealthPass to be used as a vehicle for providing additional health insurance access solutions.

Section 3. **Agency Assistance.** All agencies shall cooperate in providing to the Office such personnel, facilities, information and other assistance as is appropriate and may be required by the Office to carry out its responsibilities.

Section 4. **Effective Date.** This order shall take effect immediately.

title: RESTRICTIONS UPON AGENCY EXPENSE BUDGET ADMINISTRATION
full_text:
THE CITY OF NEW YORK
OFFICE OF THE MAYOR
NEW YORK, N.Y. 10007

EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 52

October 9, 2001

RESTRICTIONS UPON AGENCY EXPENSE BUDGET ADMINISTRATION

WHEREAS, the terrorist attack of September 11, 2001 has had an impact upon the City's economy; and

WHEREAS, although certain direct costs of such attack will be reimbursed by the federal and State governments, the City must also address the unanticipated expenditures and reduction in City revenues that have resulted from the attack; and

WHEREAS, it is the responsibility of the City, and in particular of the Mayor, under State law and the City Charter, to ensure the maintenance of a balanced budget and sound fiscal practices, and to set aside necessary reserves in furtherance of such responsibility;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. Establishment of necessary reserves. Pursuant to section 106 of the City Charter, it is hereby determined that necessary reserves of $1,000,000,000 ($1 billion) shall be set aside from agency allotments in the Fiscal Year 2002 expense budget of the City. The Office of Management and Budget (OMB) shall prepare detailed agency schedules for implementation of such reserves. This section shall apply to all agencies for which units of appropriation for personal services and other than personal services (OTPS) are included in such expense budget.

Section 2. Restriction on agency personnel actions. No mayoral agency shall hire any personnel or fill a vacancy in any position except upon the written approval of OMB. OMB may approve such action only upon written submission by the agency proposing such action and a determination by OMB that such proposed action is either:

(a) Directly related to public health or safety;

(b) Necessary to enhance or maintain the City's revenue base, or to prevent additional City expenditures;

(c) Required by law;

11- 8-01; 1:13PM ;

212 788 7649;# 5

(d) Necessary for continuation of critical agency functions; or

(e) Funded by state, federal, other non-City or capital funds.

OMB shall consult with the Office of the Corporation Counsel as necessary in considering agency submissions pursuant to this section.

Section 3. Restriction on agency other than personal service funding commitments. No mayoral agency shall commit funds in excess of $50,000 for OTPS except as set forth in this section. Any such commitment shall require approval of an OTPS Review Committee, which shall consist of representatives of the Office of Management and Budget, the Office of Operations and the Mayor's Office of Contracts. Such committee may approve such commitment only upon written submission by the agency proposing such commitment and a determination by such committee that such proposed commitment meets the criteria set forth in paragraphs (a) through (e) of Section 2 of this Order. Such committee shall consult with the Office of the Corporation Counsel as necessary in considering agency submissions pursuant to this section.

Section 4. Agency head implementation. Heads of mayoral agencies shall promptly take all necessary steps to ensure that their agencies are in compliance with the terms of this Order.

Section 5. Rule of construction. References to "agencies" and "agency heads" in this Order shall be deemed to include boards, commissions and other entities where such boards, commissions and entities administer agency budgets.

Section 6. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

TOTAL P.05

Section 3. Restriction on agency other than personal service funding commitments. No mayoral agency shall commit funds in excess of $50,000 for OTPS except as set forth in this section. Any such commitment shall require approval of an OTPS Review Committee, which shall consist of representatives of the Office of Management and Budget, the Office of Operations and the Mayor's Office of Contracts. Such committee may approve such commitment only upon written submission by the agency proposing such commitment and a determination by such committee that such proposed commitment meets the criteria set forth in paragraphs (a) through (e) of Section 2 of this Order. Such committee shall consult with the Office of the Corporation Counsel as necessary in considering agency submissions pursuant to this section.

Section 4. Agency head implementation. Heads of mayoral agencies shall promptly take all necessary steps to ensure that their agencies are in compliance with the terms of this Order.

Section 5. Rule of construction. References to "agencies" and "agency heads" in this Order shall be deemed to include boards, commissions and other entities where such boards, commissions and entities administer agency budgets.

Section 6. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

TOTAL P.05

title: DEPUTY MAYORS
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 2

JANUARY 1, 2002

DEPUTY MAYORS

By the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby
ordered:
Section 1. There shall be five Deputy Mayors. One shall be designated the Deputy
Mayor for Operations, one shall be designated the Deputy Mayor for Policy, one shall be
designated the Deputy Mayor for Administration, one shall be designated the Deputy
Mayor for Legal Affairs and one shall be designated the Deputy Mayor for Economic
Development and Recovery.
§ 2.
The Deputy Mayor for Operations shall:
a.
Supervise and coordinate the operations of all administrations,
departments, agencies, boards, offices, committees, and commissions
except as otherwise provided herein, provided that, except with respect to
matters pertaining to their departmental budgets, the Law Department, the
Police Department, the Fire Department, the Department of Investigation,
the Office of Management and Budget, the Criminal Justice Coordinator,
and the Office of Communications shall report directly to the Mayor.
b.
Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning and programs
designed to implement and enhance the fiscal operations and financial and
business management practices of the City, including those related to
labor relations.
c.
Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Mayor's Office of
Operations, the Office of City Legislative Affairs, the Office of State
Legislative Affairs, the Mayor's Office in Washington, D.C., the Office of
Labor Relations and the Office of Environmental Coordination.

d.
Serve as the Mayor's representative, either directly or through the Offices
of City and State Legislative Affairs, on, and maintain liaison with,
regional bodies and intergovernmental agencies operating within the New
York metropolitan region.
e.
Maintain liaison, either directly or through the Mayor's Office in
Washington, D.C., with the United States Conference of Mayors, the
National League of Cities, the New York Conference of Mayors and other
similar bodies.
f.
Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Metropolitan
Transportation Authority and the New York State Public Service
Commission.
g.
Supervise and coordinate the preparation of the City's Revenue, Expense
and Capital Budgets.
h.
Develop, supervise and coordinate policies and programs relating to
personnel and management practices.
i.
Succeed to the powers and duties of the "Deputy Mayor – City
Administrator of the City" under section 7384 of the Unconsolidated Laws
(Chapter 1016 of the Laws of 1969).
j.
Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers
and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State
Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the
New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as
the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public
Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New
York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may from
time to time be amended, and the New York City Transitional Authority
Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not
limited to, full power to execute for and on behalf of the Mayor, any
agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant to
such laws.

k.
Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the Mayor, a certificate
approving any borrowing of funds or pledge of assets or revenues by the
New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation which would require the
approval of the Mayor pursuant to the "Memorandum of Agreement
Between New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation and The City
of New York Relating to Operating Expenditures by the Corporation”,
dated July 1, 1970.
l.
Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the City, official
statements of the City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.
m.
Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board,
committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
n.
Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the
execution or authorization of contracts, franchises, revocable consents,
and other agreements.
o.
Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor, including
authorizations and approvals to be made or given by the Mayor pursuant
to sections 384, 824 and 1802 of the Charter, in relation to the
authorization or execution of deeds and satisfactions, leases, easements,
mortgages, and any other grants or estates or interests in real property and
licenses, permits or other agreements affecting the use of real property.
p.
Perform any function, power or duty which the Mayor has and is
authorized to delegate pursuant to New York City Charter sections 217,
219, 329 and 1301(2)(b), and pursuant to Administrative Code section 5-
304.
q.
Approve and sign applications to secure grant funds, submitted pursuant to
provisions of the New York State Environmental Conservation Law or the
rules or regulations of the State Department of Environmental
Conservation, and to sign any other documents as may be necessary to
secure such funds.
r.
Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

§ 3.
The Deputy Mayor for Operations hereby is delegated the authority to
perform all functions, powers or duties of the Mayor which the Mayor is
authorized to delegate in the event that the Mayor is unable to perform such
functions, powers or duties for a reason specified in subdivision a of section 10 of
the New York City Charter.
§ 4.
The Deputy Mayor for Policy shall:
a.
Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning, programs and
initiatives.
b.
Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Mayor's Voluntary Action
Center, the Administration for Children's Services and the Department of
Youth and Community Development.
c.
Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Board of Education,
the New York City School Construction Authority, the City University of
New York, the New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation and the
Mayor's Commission on Youth Empowerment Services.
d.
Succeed to the powers and duties of the "Health Services Administrator"
under section 7384 of the Unconsolidated Laws (Chapter 1016 of the
Laws of 1969) and shall act on behalf of the City of New York, in
accordance with subdivision 1 of section 8 of the Facilities Development
Act (Chapter 359 of the Laws of 1968), for the purpose of executing
amendments to sublease agreements heretofore made by and among the
New York State Housing Finance Agency, the Health and Mental Hygiene
Facilities Improvements Corporation and the City of New York, acting
through the Health Services Administration.
e.
Work with the Deputy Mayor for Operations in coordination with the
Office of Management and Budget and the Office of Operations, to ensure
the implementation of Mayoral policies and initiatives.
f.
Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board,
committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
g.
Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.
§ 5.
The Deputy Mayor for Administration shall:

a.
Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Department of Cultural
Affairs, the Department of Parks and Recreation and the Commission for
the United Nations, Consular Corps and Protocol.
b.
Supervise and coordinate the operations of City Hall and supervise City
sponsored public events of the City.
c.
Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Art Commission, the
Landmarks Preservation Commission, the Central Park Conservancy,
libraries, museums, performing arts organizations, gardens and zoos.
d.
Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board,
committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
e.
Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.
§ 6.
The Deputy Mayor for Legal Affairs shall:
a.
Provide counsel to the Mayor on legal matters.
b.
Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Office for People with
Disabilities, the Office of Immigrant Affairs, the Office to Combat
Domestic Violence, the Commission on the Status of Women and the New
York City Commission on Human Rights.
c.
Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Mayor's Committee
on the Judiciary, the Conflicts of Interest Board, the Office of
Administrative Trials and Hearings, the Voter Assistance Commission and
the Equal Employment Practices Commission.
d.
Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board,
committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
e.
Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.
§ 7.
The Deputy Mayor for Economic Development and Recovery shall:
a.
Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning, and programs
designed to foster the economic growth of the City, including those
relating to the City's overall business climate, the attraction, retention and
expansion of domestic and global business enterprises in the City, efforts
to secure the 2012 Olympic Games, commercial and industrial
development, energy, foreign trade and investment, government

regulation, film, theater and broadcasting, entertainment and sports facility
development, and air, land and sea freight.
b.
Advise and assist the Mayor regarding the City's physical and economic
response to the destruction of the World Trade Center, including plans for
the redevelopment of the financial district and Lower Manhattan.
c.
Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Department of City
Planning and the Office of Film, Theater, and Broadcasting.
d.
Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the City Planning
Commission, the New York City Housing Development Corporation, the
United Nations Development Corp., the New York City Sports
Commission and New York City Sports Development Corporation, the
Board of Standards and Appeals, and the New York City Loft Board.
e.
Serve as Chairperson of the Commercial Incentive Boundary Area
Commission and the Industrial and Commercial Incentive Board.
f.
Direct and supervise the activities of the Department of Business Services,
the Department of Consumer Affairs, the Economic Development
Corporation as provided in the Amended and Restated Contract between
the City and the Economic Development Corporation, and take such
actions thereunder as are reserved to the Deputy Mayor.
g.
Direct and coordinate the activities of all administrations, departments,
agencies, boards, offices, committees and commissions with respect to
energy policies, planning and programs.
h.
Maintain liaison with the New York State Department of Economic
Development, the City Empowerment Zone, the Empire State
Development Corporation, the Port Authority of New York and New
Jersey, the Power Authority of the State of New York, the New York
Convention and Visitors Bureau, the Lower Manhattan Development
Corporation and other governmental agencies and offices with respect to
matters of City economic development, energy policies and programs.
i.
Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor, including
authorizations and approvals to be made or given by the Mayor pursuant

to sections 384, 824 and 1802 of the Charter, in relation to the
authorization or execution of deeds and satisfactions, leases, easements,
mortgages and any other grants of estates or interests in real property and
licenses, permits or other agreements affecting the use of real property by
or involving the Economic Development Corporation, including any such
authorization or approval in relation to real property under the jurisdiction
of the Department of Citywide Administrative Services made for the
purpose of a project of the Economic Development Corporation.
j.
Advise and assist the Mayor regarding tax policies.
k.
Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to any
contracts with or involving the New York City Industrial Development
Agency.
1.
Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers
and duties which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State
Local Finance Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the
New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of New York, as
the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public
Authorities Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the
New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority Act, as the same may
from time to time be amended, and the New York City Transitional
Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including,
but not limited to, full power to execute for and on behalf of the Mayor,
any agreement, amendment to such agreement or other document pursuant
to such laws.
m.
Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the
execution or authorization of such franchises and revocable consents as
relate to the duties of the Deputy Mayor for Economic Development.
n.
Perform any function, power or duty which the Mayor has and is
authorized to delegate pursuant to New York City Charter section
1301(2)(b) and Administrative Code section 5-304.

o.
Approve and sign applications to secure grant funds, submitted pursuant to
provisions of the New York State Environmental Conservation Law or the
rules and regulations of the State Department of Environmental
Conservation, and to sign any other documents as may be necessary to
secure such funds.
p.
Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board,
committee, commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
q.
Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.
§ 8. Executive Order No. 20, dated March 23, 1995, and Executive Order No. 31,
dated August 29, 1996, as amended by Executive Order No. 46, dated
May 27, 1999, are hereby REPEALED.
§ 9.
This Order shall take effect immediately.

______________________
Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

title: PROCLAMATION OF A STATE OF EMERGENCY
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 3

JANUARY 7, 2002

PROCLAMATION OF A STATE OF EMERGENCY

Whereas, Employees of Command Bus Company, Green Bus Company, Jamaica
Buses, New York Bus Service, Queens' Surface Corporation and Triboro Coach
Corporation, all of which companies have contracts with the New York City Department
of Transportation to provide service in areas of the City where bus service is not provided
by the New 'York City Transit Authority, have threatened to commence a strike in
January 2002, and such strike would cause serious disruption of the City's transportation
system; and
Whereas, It is necessary to insure public safety and the orderly transportation of
people and goods in the City of New York; and
Whereas, The threatened strikes would cause an increase in the. response time of
emergency- vehicles which will endanger the lives and health of the City's residents,
commuters and visitors, inability to gain access to routine medical care, the loss of wages
for thousands of persons, the loss of revenue, on a daily basis, for businesses in the City,
and lost revenues for the City and the Board of Education, and significant increased
expenditures by the City of New York;
Whereas, These circumstances constitute. an imminent peril to the public health
and safety requiring the adoption of special rules, regulations, procedures and restrictions
as emergency measures; and
Whereas, Executive Law §24 authorizes the Mayor to promulgate local
emergency orders upon a finding that the public safety is imperiled by the event of a

title: MAYOR'S COMMITTEE ON APPOINTMENTS
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 6

FEBRUARY 8, 2002

MAYOR'S COMMITTEE ON APPOINTMENTS

By the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby
ordered:
Section 1. Committee Established. The Mayor's Committee on Appointments
(hereinafter called the "Committee") hereby is established to assist the Mayor in the
recruitment and evaluation of highly qualified candidates of superior ability for
appointment, and to evaluate incumbent members for reappointment, to agencies, as the
Mayor shall from time to time direct, and to commissions, boards and public bodies.
Section 2. Committee Membership.
(a)
The Committee shall be appointed by the Mayor and shall consist of no
fewer than five or more than nine members, including a Chair. The Committee Chair
may, in his or her discretion, designate adjunct members who shall function under section
three as voting members with regard to appointments and reappointments to specific
agencies, commissions, boards or other public bodies. Adjunct members, if so designated,
shall have such expertise or knowledge as will assist the Committee in making a
reasoned, informed and impartial evaluation of candidates for appointments to agencies,
boards, commissions and other public bodies.
(b)
Members shall be appointed (and reappointed) for two year periods in the
discretion of the Mayor, except that the term of the initial members appointed hereunder
shall expire on December 31, 2003. Any member whose term has expired may continue
to serve at the pleasure of the Mayor until such time as the member is reappointed or a
successor is appointed. The Mayor shall designate the Committee Chair. Adjunct
members shall function under section three as voting members until the appointments or
reappointments for which they have been designated become final, and such adjunct
members may be redesignated at the discretion of the Committee Chair.
(c)
No person shall be considered or evaluated by the Committee for any
position covered by this Order while serving as a member of the Committee. In the event

that the Committee determines to consider any member of the Committee for
appointment and the member consents to be considered for appointment, then said
member shall resign from the Committee immediately and shall be precluded from
participating in the functions of the Committee in any respect. The Mayor shall fill the
vacancy created by said resigning member as promptly as reasonably practicable.
Section 3.
Functions. The Committee shall:
(a)
Recruit for consideration persons of superior abilities who are highly
qualified for appointment to agencies, boards, commissions and other public bodies,
receive recommendations of persons for consideration as provided by law, and accept
applications from persons seeking appointment to such offices;
(b)
Evaluate and conduct all necessary inquiry to identify those persons whose
character, ability, training, experience, temperament and commitment to public service
highly qualify them for such offices;
(c)
Refer to the Department of Investigation for screening persons the
Committee proposes to nominate for appointment, when appropriate;
(d)
Assist the Mayor in the selection of persons for appointments to agencies,
boards, commissions and other public bodies by nominating for consideration by the
Mayor one or more candidates for such appointment, and submit to the Mayor such
information as may be necessary to inform the Mayor of the qualifications of each
nominee; provided that when pursuant to law the Mayor receives nominations for
appointments from other persons or bodies, the Committee, at the request of the Mayor,
shall consider such nominations and report its recommendation in favor of or against the
appointment of such persons to the Mayor;
(e)
Evaluate the qualifications of incumbents in agencies, boards,
commissions and other public bodies for reappointment and report the Committee's
recommendation to the Mayor, provided that it may also nominate one or more
candidates for appointment to the office.
(f)
Act expeditiously to assure that nominations are timely made, and begin
the process of considering nominees for a vacancy before the term of the incumbent
expires.

(g)
In the event that the Mayor may choose to make an appointment or
reappointment directly to an agency, board, commission or other public body, then the
Chief of Staff to the Mayor or a Deputy Mayor promptly shall notify the Chair of the
Committee of the Mayor's intention to fill such vacancy directly.
Section 4. Confidentiality. All Committee communications concerning the
qualifications of candidates shall be made and held in confidence, except if disclosure is
necessary and proper to the conduct of Committee business.
Section 5. Committee Action and Procedure. The Committee may adopt such
procedures and policies as it may deem appropriate to its functions, including standards
for evaluating the qualifications of candidates for nomination and criteria for
recommending the reappointment of incumbents.
Section 6.
Financing and Staff.
(a)
The Committee Chair and members of the Committee shall receive no
compensation for their service on the Committee.
(b)
The Committee shall be provided with staff and sufficient facilities to
carry out its functions.
(c)
The Committee Chair and members of the Committee shall be reimbursed
for necessary expenses incurred in connection with the responsibilities of the Committee.
Section 7. Chief of Staff. The Chief of Staff to the Mayor shall maintain liaison
with and review the activities of the Committee, and shall advise the Mayor and the
Committee regarding measures which may enhance the ability of the Committee to
consider the best qualified candidates for appointments to agencies, commissions, boards
and other public bodies.
Section 8.
Prior Order Revoked. Executive Order No. 4, dated April 4, 1994,
is hereby repealed.
Section 9.
Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

______________________
Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

title: MAYOR'S ADVISORY COMMITTEE ON THE JUDICIARY
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 8

MARCH 4, 2002

MAYOR'S ADVISORY COMMITTEE ON THE JUDICIARY

By the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby
ordered:
Section 1. Committee Established. The Mayor's Advisory Committee on the
Judiciary (hereinafter called the "Committee") hereby is established in the Office of the
Mayor to recruit, to evaluate, to consider and to nominate judicial candidates highly
qualified for appointment and to evaluate the incumbent judges for reappointment to the
following courts within The City of New York: Criminal Court, Family Court and for
interim appointments, Civil Court.
Section 2.
Functions. The Committee shall:
(a)
Take steps to recruit and encourage highly qualified persons for such
appointment to serve as a judge of a court in New York City and to receive from any
source the names of candidates appearing to have the highest qualifications for judicial
office;
(b)
Evaluate and conduct all necessary inquiry to determine those persons
whose character, ability, training, experience, temperament and commitment to equal
justice under law fully qualify them for judicial office;
(c)
Consider all relevant information to determine which of the highly
qualified candidates are best qualified for judicial office, and refer to the Department of
Investigation for screening all persons the Committee proposes to nominate for
appointment;
(d)
Nominate and present to the Mayor three candidates for appointment to
each vacant judicial office, except that if there are numerous vacancies the Committee, in
its discretion, may present less than three nominations (unless the Mayor requests three

nominations) for each vacancy, and provide such information as may be necessary to
inform the Mayor of the qualifications of each nominee; and
(e)
Evaluate the qualifications of each incumbent judge for reappointment to
judicial office and present the Committee's recommendation to the Mayor, provided that
if the Committee finds the incumbent is not highly qualified for reappointment, or if the
Mayor, following receipt of the Committee's recommendation, finds that the incumbent is
not highly qualified for reappointment, the Committee shall nominate and present to the
Mayor three candidates for appointment to the resulting vacancy other than the
incumbent.
Section 3.
Public Hearings.
(a)
The Mayor shall notify the Committee of the name of any person chosen
for appointment from among the nominees submitted by the Committee and shall notify
the Committee of the name of each incumbent judge chosen for reappointment as
recommended by the Committee. The Committee shall promptly thereafter conduct a
public hearing except in the case of the appointment of an incumbent judge. Such
hearings shall be upon reasonable notice and any person may present information
concerning the fitness of the nominee for appointment. Based on the information
received, the Committee may reconsider the nomination. If any reconsideration results in
withdrawal of a nomination, the Mayor shall be notified immediately by the Committee
and the nominee shall not be appointed.
(b)
The Committee. may from time to time conduct public hearings
concerning the process of judicial selection.
Section 4. Appointments by the Mayor.
(a)
The Mayor shall not appoint a judge unless nominated by the Committee,
and shall not reappoint an incumbent judge unless recommended for reappointment by
the Committee.
(b)
Judicial vacancies shall be filled within ninety days unless a longer period
is required in the public interest.
(c) After the Mayor appoints a nominee to fill a judicial vacancy, the remaining
nominations submitted by the Committee for that vacancy shall expire immediately,
unless a vacancy or vacancies exists in the same court. In such case the remaining

nominations shall be valid for appointment to that court for six months after their
submission to the Mayor or until such vacancy or vacancies are filled, whichever is
earlier.
Section 5.
Committee Membership.
(a)
The Committee shall consist of nineteen members, each residing or having
a principal place of business in the City of New York, all of whom shall be appointed by
the Mayor. The Mayor shall select nine members, including the Chairperson who shall
serve in that capacity at the pleasure of the Mayor, and, in the Mayor's discretion,
including one or more Vice Chairpersons who shall serve in that capacity at the pleasure
of the Mayor. The Chief Judge of the New York Court of Appeals shall nominate four
members for appointment to the committee by the Mayor. The Presiding Justices of the
Appellate Division for the First and Second Judicial Departments each shall nominate
two members for appointment to the Committee by the Mayor. Two deans of law schools
within the City of New York shall each nominate one member for appointment to the
Committee by the Mayor, with authority to nominate rotating biannually among eligible
deans. If the Mayor decides not to appoint any person nominated by the Chief Judge, a
Presiding Justice or dean, he shall notify the Chief Judge, Presiding Justice or dean who
made the nomination to submit the name of another nominee. All members shall serve for
terms of two years. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the members first appointed shall
serve until December 31, 2003. Vacancies in the Committee shall be filled in the same
manner as initial appointments, and a member filling a vacancy shall serve for the
remainder of the unexpired term. Any member of the Committee may be removed by the
Mayor for cause.
(b)
Members of the Committee shall be selected in order to ensure that only
candidates with the highest qualifications shall be nominated for appointment to judicial
office. Members of the Committee shall be selected with due consideration for broad
community and borough representation. The membership shall include men and women,
and members of minority and other groups, who are qualified to perform the functions of
the Committee.
(c)
No person shall be considered by the Committee for judicial office while
serving as a member of the Committee or within one year thereafter.

Section 6. Confidentiality. All Committee communications concerning the
judicial qualifications of candidates shall be made and held in confidence, except such
communications as the Committee may submit to the Mayor or receive at public
hearings, or as otherwise may be necessary and proper to the conduct of Committee
proceedings.
Section 7.
Committee Action Procedure. The Committee may adopt such
procedures and policies as it may deem appropriate to its functions, including standards
for evaluating the best qualified candidates for nomination, and criteria for
recommending the reappointment of incumbent judges.
Section 8.
Financing and Staff.
(a)
Members of the Committee shall receive no compensation for their service
as members.
(b)
The Committee shall be provided with paid staff and sufficient facilities to
carry its functions, including the thorough investigation of the qualifications of all
candidates for judicial office.
(c)
Members of the Committee and its staff shall be reimbursed for necessary
expenses incurred in connection with the responsibilities of the Committee.
Section 9. Deputy Mayor for Legal Affairs. The Deputy Mayor for Legal Affairs
shall maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Committee, and shall advise
the Mayor and the Committee regarding measures which may enhance the ability of the
Committee to consider the best qualified candidates for judicial nomination.
Section 10. Prior Order Revoked. Executive Order No. 10, dated July 20, 1994
hereby is repealed, and the Committee on the Judiciary established thereunder hereby is
abolished.
Section 11.
Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

______________________
Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor
