title: PROCLAMATION OF A STATE OF EMERGENCY
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 104

PROCLAMATION OF A STATE OF EMERGENCY

SEPTEMBER 4, 2007

WHEREAS, taxicab drivers have threatened to engage in a strike beginning on or
around September 5, 2007 which may cause disruption to the City’s transportation
system; and

WHEREAS, such a strike may lead to a risk of blocked streets and ground
transportation arteries to the detriment of public safety; and

WHEREAS, the disruption of the City’s transportation system resulting from such
strike may endanger the lives and health of the City’s residents, commuters and visitors
and impair the ability to gain access to routine medical care, may cause loss of revenue
for businesses in the City, and loss of revenues and increased expenditures by the City;
and

WHEREAS, these circumstances constitute an imminent peril to the public health
and safety requiring the adoption of emergency measures; and

WHEREAS, Executive Law § 24 authorizes the Mayor to promulgate local
emergency orders upon a finding that the public safety is imperiled by the event of a
public emergency or in the event of reasonable apprehension of immediate danger
thereof, to protect life and property and to bring an emergency situation under control;
and

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New
York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. State of Emergency. A state of emergency is hereby declared to exist
within the City of New York.

§ 2. Taxi and for-hire vehicle provisions. The following provisions of this
emergency order shall apply to vehicles licensed by the New York City Taxi and
Limousine Commission (“TLC”):

a. The Chair of the TLC (“the Chair”) is authorized to determine that a strike has
commenced. Upon making such determination, the Chair is authorized, for the
duration of the emergency, to:

(1)
 implement, any of the actions enumerated in this section as the
Chair determines necessary. Any such actions may be modified,
continued, or discontinued as the Chair determines necessary;

(2)
establish group ride locations and establish per person or per trip
rates of fare for trips in taxicabs licensed by the TLC originating in such
locations. The Chair may determine whether drivers and/or passengers
shall have the option or shall be required to offer or accept group rides;

(3) permit sharing of rides in all taxicabs, either with or without the

passenger’s consent as the Chair directs, and to set rates of fares, and, if

appropriate, fare zones, for all taxicabs;

(4) permit all for-hire vehicles licensed by the TLC to pick up
passengers with or without pre-arrangement (“street hails”);

(5)
permit sharing of rides, either with or without the passenger’s
consent, as the Chair directs, in all for-hire vehicles licensed by the TLC,
and set rates of fares, and, if appropriate, fare zones, for all such for-hire
vehicles. In such event, all drivers of for-hire vehicles licensed by the
TLC shall display their TLC operator’s license and the name of the
affiliated base or authority inside the vehicle in a manner that is easily
visible or accessible to the passengers; and

(6)
permit all commuter vans licensed as such by the TLC to operate
outside of the geographical area set forth in their operation authorization.

b. No TLC-licensed driver shall charge or permit the charging of any passenger a
fare in excess of the authorized rate of fare for any trip.

§ 3.
This Order shall take effect at 5:00 a.m. on September 5, 2007, and shall
stay in effect for five days thereafter, unless it is terminated earlier.

____________________________________

Michael R. Bloomberg

Mayor

title: COMMUNITY AFFAIRS UNIT
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No.105

COMMUNITY AFFAIRS UNIT

SEPTEMBER 17, 2007

WHEREAS, the City of New York is comprised of diverse communities each
with unique characteristics, concerns and issues;

WHEREAS, to better serve its citizens, the City must be responsive to specific
needs of each community and facilitate effective communication between the City
agencies and different neighborhood groups and individuals;

WHEREAS, government interaction with its citizens is imperative in times of
emergency, and;

WHEREAS, implementation of government initiatives requires input of
community groups and individuals as well as cooperation among different branches of
local government and constituents;

WHEREAS, community service through volunteerism is needed to bring essential
improvements and services to different organizations, neighborhoods, groups and
individuals;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New
York, it is hereby ordered that:

Section 1.
The Community Assistance Unit, established within the Office of
the Mayor, is hereby renamed the Mayor’s Community Affairs Unit.

§ 2.
The Community Affairs Unit shall maintain continuous liaison with City
officials, public and private agencies, community boards, district service cabinets, district
managers, borough boards and cabinets, community groups and communities.

§ 3.
The Community Affairs Unit shall be responsible for coordinating the
activities of City agencies with respect to the implementation and operation of the
provisions of the Charter of the City of New York concerning community boards, district
service cabinets, district managers, coterminality and decentralization including, but not
limited to, responsibility for:

(a) assisting the Office of Management and Budget in coordinating (1) the
implementation and operation of the provisions of the Charter concerning
community board participation in the budget process in accordance with
Sections 100, 230 and 238 of the Charter and (ii) agency service
statements for community districts in accordance with and to the extent
required by Section 2707 of the Charter;

(b) maintaining a continuous liaison with community boards, district service
cabinets, district managers, borough boards and service cabinets, City
officials and agencies in order (i) to bring to the attention of the Mayor
and other appropriate City officials significant problems arising in
connection with the activities or operations of such organizations and to
propose solutions to such problems, (ii) to foster a cooperative and
effective working relationship between City officials and community
boards and district managers , and (iii) to ensure that significant Mayoral
initiatives and programs are communicated to community boards and
communities; and

(c) providing training and technical assistance for implementation of the
appropriate Charter provisions to community boards, district service
cabinets, district managers and City agencies.

§ 4.
The Community Affairs Unit shall be responsible for maintaining liaison
with communities and community groups in order to bring to the attention of the
Mayor and other appropriate City officials issues and problems of concern to
communities, including, but not limited to, responsibility for the following:

(a) addressing the concerns of community-based groups, including without
limitation, block, neighborhood, civic, regional and citywide groups,
regarding city services, policies and programs;

(b) fostering greater cooperation between community groups and community
boards;

(c) coordinating such community out reach and liaison activities as the Mayor
may direct, including but not limited to scheduling meetings between the
Mayor, city officials, community leaders and residents; and

(d) representing the Mayor at community meetings where requested to do so
by the Mayor.

§ 5.
The Community Affairs Unit shall be responsible for maintaining a
Mayor’s Volunteer Center, including, but not limited to, responsibility for the following:

(a) bringing together individuals, corporations, governments agencies and
not-for-profit organizations in order to connect people with volunteer
programs that improve the quality of life in New York City; and

(b) encouraging every New Yorker to serve as a volunteer.

§ 6.
The Community Affairs Unit shall convene a Graffiti Task Force and
implement recommendations made by said Task Force.

§ 8.
All City agencies, without limitation, are directed to cooperate with the
Community Affairs Unit in order to carry out the objectives of the Charter and of this
Order.

§ 7.
The responsibility for exercising all functions, powers and duties
regarding street activity permits shall be undertaken by the Coordinator of Citywide
Special Events and Permitted Activities, as established by Executive Order No. 100 of
2007, and the staff of the Street Activity Permit Office shall be housed within the
Mayor’s Office of Citywide Event Coordination and Management headed by such
Coordinator. The Coordinator shall undertake all appropriate rulemaking to conform the
provisions of Chapter 1 of Title 50 of the Rules of the City of New York with this Order.

§ 9.
Executive Order 59, dated December 9, 1993 and Executive Order 37,
dated July 9, 2003, are hereby repealed.

§ 10. This Order shall take affect immediately.

Michael R. Bloomberg

Mayor
full_text_raw:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No.105

COMMUNITY AFFAIRS UNIT

SEPTEMBER 17, 2007

WHEREAS, the City of New York is comprised of diverse communities each
with unique characteristics, concerns and issues;

WHEREAS, to better serve its citizens, the City must be responsive to specific
needs of each community and facilitate effective communication between the City
agencies and different neighborhood groups and individuals;

WHEREAS, government interaction with its citizens is imperative in times of
emergency, and;

WHEREAS, implementation of government initiatives requires input of
community groups and individuals as well as cooperation among different branches of
local government and constituents;

WHEREAS, community service through volunteerism is needed to bring essential
improvements and services to different organizations, neighborhoods, groups and
individuals;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New
York, it is hereby ordered that:

Section 1.
The Community Assistance Unit, established within the Office of
the Mayor, is hereby renamed the Mayor’s Community Affairs Unit.

§ 2.
The Community Affairs Unit shall maintain continuous liaison with City
officials, public and private agencies, community boards, district service cabinets, district
managers, borough boards and cabinets, community groups and communities.

§ 3.
The Community Affairs Unit shall be responsible for coordinating the
activities of City agencies with respect to the implementation and operation of the
provisions of the Charter of the City of New York concerning community boards, district
service cabinets, district managers, coterminality and decentralization including, but not
limited to, responsibility for:

(a) assisting the Office of Management and Budget in coordinating (1) the
implementation and operation of the provisions of the Charter concerning
community board participation in the budget process in accordance with
Sections 100, 230 and 238 of the Charter and (ii) agency service
statements for community districts in accordance with and to the extent
required by Section 2707 of the Charter;

(b) maintaining a continuous liaison with community boards, district service
cabinets, district managers, borough boards and service cabinets, City
officials and agencies in order (i) to bring to the attention of the Mayor
and other appropriate City officials significant problems arising in
connection with the activities or operations of such organizations and to
propose solutions to such problems, (ii) to foster a cooperative and
effective working relationship between City officials and community
boards and district managers , and (iii) to ensure that significant Mayoral
initiatives and programs are communicated to community boards and
communities; and

(c) providing training and technical assistance for implementation of the
appropriate Charter provisions to community boards, district service
cabinets, district managers and City agencies.

§ 4.
The Community Affairs Unit shall be responsible for maintaining liaison
with communities and community groups in order to bring to the attention of the
Mayor and other appropriate City officials issues and problems of concern to
communities, including, but not limited to, responsibility for the following:

(a) addressing the concerns of community-based groups, including without
limitation, block, neighborhood, civic, regional and citywide groups,
regarding city services, policies and programs;

(b) fostering greater cooperation between community groups and community
boards;

(c) coordinating such community out reach and liaison activities as the Mayor
may direct, including but not limited to scheduling meetings between the
Mayor, city officials, community leaders and residents; and

(d) representing the Mayor at community meetings where requested to do so
by the Mayor.

§ 5.
The Community Affairs Unit shall be responsible for maintaining a
Mayor’s Volunteer Center, including, but not limited to, responsibility for the following:

(a) bringing together individuals, corporations, governments agencies and
not-for-profit organizations in order to connect people with volunteer
programs that improve the quality of life in New York City; and

(b) encouraging every New Yorker to serve as a volunteer.

§ 6.
The Community Affairs Unit shall convene a Graffiti Task Force and
implement recommendations made by said Task Force.

§ 8.
All City agencies, without limitation, are directed to cooperate with the
Community Affairs Unit in order to carry out the objectives of the Charter and of this
Order.

§ 7.
The responsibility for exercising all functions, powers and duties
regarding street activity permits shall be undertaken by the Coordinator of Citywide
Special Events and Permitted Activities, as established by Executive Order No. 100 of
2007, and the staff of the Street Activity Permit Office shall be housed within the
Mayor’s Office of Citywide Event Coordination and Management headed by such
Coordinator. The Coordinator shall undertake all appropriate rulemaking to conform the
provisions of Chapter 1 of Title 50 of the Rules of the City of New York with this Order.

§ 9.
Executive Order 59, dated December 9, 1993 and Executive Order 37,
dated July 9, 2003, are hereby repealed.

§ 10. This Order shall take affect immediately.

_____________________

Michael R. Bloomberg

Mayor

title: ENTERPRISE BILLING, PAYMENT AND COLLECTION
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 106

ENTERPRISE BILLING, PAYMENT AND COLLECTION

OCTOBER 2, 2007

WHEREAS, the City is committed to an enterprise approach to government that
leverages central technologies across organizational lines to improve the quality and
efficiency of the services it provides to its citizens; and

WHEREAS, the size of the City’s population, and the City’s commitment to
sound fiscal management practices require a unified and modern system of payment
options for municipal fees, permits and fines, as well as an efficient, state-of-the art
system of municipal bill processing and collection; and

WHEREAS, implementation of a unified billing, payment and collection policy
requires cooperation and coordination among City agencies and administrative tribunals;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New
York, it is hereby ordered that:

Section 1.
The Mayor’s Office of Operations (“Office of Operations”) is
hereby responsible for developing and implementing an enterprise billing, payment and
collections strategy.

§ 2.
All City agencies shall establish and implement a system for accepting
credit and debit card payments for fees, fines, sale of products and any other suitable
transactions no later than December 31, 2008. The Office of Operations shall provide the
technical assistance needed for the development and implementation of credit and debit
card payment capability.

§ 3.
The Office of Operations shall create and implement a strategy for the
collection of delinquent debts that enhances the existing debt collection methods of City
agencies by eliminating redundancies and outdated processes and practices. This
collection strategy shall utilize existing and new technologies in order to develop, where
appropriate, a unified customer bill that reflects multiple, suitable payments due to the
City regardless of agency or payment type.

§ 4.
All City agencies and administrative tribunals, without limitation, are
directed to cooperate with the Office of Operations in order to carry out the objectives of
this Order.

§ 5.
The Order shall take effect immediately.

_______________________
Michael R. Bloomberg

Mayor

title: CONTINUITY OF OPERATIONS PLANNING
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 107

CONTINUITY OF OPERATIONS PLANNING

OCTOBER 2, 2007

WHEREAS, City agencies currently employ a variety of contingency planning
approaches to maintain essential operations during an emergency or other incident that may
disrupt normal agency operations; and

WHEREAS, City agencies must have comprehensive and effective plans in place to
continue such essential operations, as well as to support Citywide emergency response; and

WHEREAS, New York City Charter § 497 authorizes the Office of Emergency
Management (“OEM”) to, among other things, coordinate the City’s response to all emergency
conditions and potential incidents that require a multi-agency response and prepare plans for
responding to emergency conditions and potential incidents; and

WHEREAS, New York City Charter § 1072 directs the Department of Information
Technology & Telecommunications (“DoITT”) to, among other things, plan, formulate,
coordinate and advance information technology policies for the City, including support for
disaster recovery; and

WHEREAS, a Continuity of Operations (“COOP”) Plan establishes a plan for the
continuity of essential operations during an emergency or other incident that may disrupt normal
agency operations; and

WHEREAS, a pilot project to develop a standardized COOP planning methodology
across City agencies was initiated in October 2006 through OEM and DoITT; and

WHEREAS, OEM and DoITT selected three City agencies for this pilot project and
provided them with the tools and assistance required to complete a COOP plan; and

WHEREAS, based upon the lessons learned from the COOP pilot project, remaining City
agencies will be able to develop and implement a COOP plan to suit their particularized needs
and to continue essential operations during an emergency or other incident that may disrupt
normal agency operations;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is
hereby ordered:

Section 1. Upon completion of the pilot project, OEM and DoITT shall establish a
standardized COOP planning methodology, agency planning guide and software tool for use by
City agencies to develop and implement an individualized COOP plan, which may build on any
existing agency contingency plans.

§ 2. The COOP planning methodology, guide and software tool shall be introduced to
City agencies by a COOP Management Team, which shall be co-chaired by the Commissioner of
Emergency
Management
and
the
Commissioner
of
Information
Technology
and
Telecommunications. Each such commissioner may designate a senior manager from his or her
agency to act as co-chair in his or her stead. The COOP Management Team shall consist of
employees of OEM and DoITT designated by the co-chairs. All members of the COOP
Management Team shall serve without additional compensation.

§ 3. The COOP Management Team shall provide training to City agencies on the
creation and/or migration of existing agency contingency plans and the use of the software tool
to develop an agency-wide COOP plan. The COOP Management Team shall provide oversight
and guidance to City agencies as they fulfill their responsibility to develop a COOP plan to
enable them to continue essential operations during an emergency or other incident that may
disrupt normal agency operations. To support this effort, each City agency shall designate a
project planning team within such agency that shall include the following: a deputy
commissioner or other senior official responsible for internal COOP executive management; a
project liaison to serve as the day-to-day COOP project manager for the agency and liaison to the
COOP Management Team; and a project analyst to provide support services for the liaison and
project planning team.

§ 4. All City agencies shall cooperate in providing the COOP Management Team with
information and other assistance as may be necessary and appropriate for the COOP
Management Team to carry out its responsibilities pursuant to this Order.

§ 5. Each City agency shall have a COOP plan in place no later than December 31, 2009.

§ 6. This Order shall take effect immediately.

______________________________

Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 108

PROCLOMATION OF A STATE OF EMERGENCY

October 19, 2007

WHEREAS, taxicab drivers have threatened to engage in a strike beginning on or
around October 22, 2007 which may cause disruption to the City’s transportation system;
and

WHEREAS, taxicab drivers previously engaged in a strike on September 5 and
September 6, 2007; and

WHEREAS, such a strike may lead to a risk of blocked streets and ground
transportation arteries to the detriment of public safety; and

WHEREAS, the disruption of the City’s transportation system resulting from such
strike may endanger the lives and health of the City’s residents, commuters and visitors
and impair the ability to gain access to routine medical care, may cause loss of revenue
for businesses in the City, and loss of revenues and increased expenditures by the City;
and

WHEREAS, these circumstances constitute an imminent peril to the public health
and safety requiring the adoption of emergency measures; and

WHEREAS, Executive Law §24 authorizes the Mayor to promulgate local
emergency orders upon a finding that the public safety is imperiled by the event of a
public emergency or in the event of reasonable apprehension of immediate danger
thereof, to protect life and property and to bring an emergency situation under control;
and

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New
York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. State of Emergency. A state of emergency is hereby declared to exist
within the City of New York.

§ 2. Taxi and for-hire vehicle provisions. The following provisions of this
emergency order shall apply to vehicles licensed by the New York City Taxi and
Limousine Commission (“TLC”):

a. The Chair of the TLC (“the Chair”) is authorized to determine that a strike has
commenced. Upon making such determination, the Chair is authorized, for the
duration of the emergency, to

(1)
implement any of the actions enumerated in this section as the
Chair determines necessary. Any such actions may be modified,
continued, or discontinued as the Chair determines necessary;

(2)
establish group ride locations and establish per person or per trip
rates of fare for trips in taxicabs licensed by the TLC originating in such
locations. The Chair may determine whether drivers and/or passengers
shall have the option or shall be required to offer or accept group rides;

(3)
permit sharing of rides in all taxicabs, either with or without the
passenger’s consent as the Chair directs, and to set rates of fares, and, if
appropriate, fare zones, for all taxicabs;

(4)
permit all for-hire vehicles licensed by the TLC to pick up
passengers with or without pre-arrangement (“street hails”);

(5)
permit sharing of rides, either with or without the passenger’s
consent, as the Chair directs, in all for-hire vehicles licensed by the TLC,
and set rates of fares, and, if appropriate, fare zones, for all such for-hire
vehicles. In such event, all drivers of for-hire vehicles licensed by the
TLC shall display their TLC operator’s license and the name of the
affiliated base or authority inside the vehicle in a manner that is easily
visible or accessible to the passengers; and

(6)
permit all commuter vans licensed as such by the TLC to operate
outside of the geographical area set forth in their operation authorization.

b. No TLC-licensed driver shall charge or permit the charging of any passenger a
fare in excess of the authorized rate of fare for any trip.

§3. This Order shall take effect at 5:00 a.m. on October 22, 2007, and shall stay
in effect for five days thereafter, unless it is terminated earlier.

________________________________

Michael R. Bloomberg

Mayor

2

title: ENERGY SAVINGS AND REDUCTION OF GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS IN CITY BUILDINGS AND OPERATIONS
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 109

ENERGY SAVINGS AND REDUCTION OF GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS IN CITY
BUILDINGS AND OPERATIONS

October 22, 2007

WHEREAS, providing municipal services and fulfilling the obligations and duties of
New York City government require the use of energy resources; and

WHEREAS, the generation and use of energy have a significant impact on the
environment, including the emission of greenhouse gases that contribute to global warming; and

WHEREAS, under PlaNYC, New York City has a goal of reducing its Citywide
greenhouse gas footprint by 30% by 2030; and

WHEREAS, City government consumes more than 6% of all energy used in New York
City, but has succeeded in stabilizing its greenhouse gas emissions through the use of energy-conscious policies such as retrofitting buildings to make them more energy efficient and
installing LED traffic lights; and

WHEREAS, in PlaNYC and the Mayor’s FY2008 executive budget, the City has
expressed its commitment to reduce energy consumption by City government, committed 10% of
its FY2008 energy expenses to fund energy-saving investments in City buildings and operations,
and proposed committing that amount each year going forward; and

WHEREAS, it is imperative for each City agency to significantly reduce its energy use to
realize this Citywide mandate; and

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New
York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Carbon Reduction Goal. The City shall implement cost-effective programs
and energy-efficient practices designed to reduce the City government’s energy consumption and
CO2e emissions by 30% from 2006 levels, as measured by the Inventory of New York City
Greenhouse Gas Emissions of April 2007, within ten years of the effective date of this Executive
Order. All agency heads are responsible for reducing energy consumption in the facilities that
they manage.

§ 2. Energy Conservation Steering Committee. An Energy Conservation Steering
Committee (“Steering Committee”) shall be established, consisting of representatives of the
Office of the Deputy Mayor for Administration, the Department of Citywide Administrative
Services, the Mayor’s Office of Operations, the Mayor’s Office of Management and Budget
(“OMB”), the Department of Design and Construction, and the New York City Economic
Development Corporation, to oversee and manage the development and implementation of the
City’s plan to reduce its carbon emissions. The Steering Committee shall be chaired by the
Deputy Mayor for Administration or his designee, and represented agencies shall provide staff
support. The Steering Committee shall also advise City agencies on all uses of funds allocated to
carbon-reduction efforts in City government.

§ 3. Energy Reduction Plans. a. By December 1, 2007, the Steering Committee shall
issue a short-term action plan for the use of the $80,000,000 budgeted in FY2008 for energy and
greenhouse gas emission reduction purposes. Projects that reduce the City’s energy consumption
and/or greenhouse gas footprint will be considered plan-eligible, including but not limited to
building retrofits, process and plug-load improvements, methane capture projects, and vehicle
retrofits or replacements. All buildings for which the City pays energy costs shall be considered
plan-eligible, and all forms of energy consumed, whether purchased centrally or not, shall be
considered plan-eligible. Return on investment and overall energy savings shall be the primary
bases for selecting and prioritizing projects. The Steering Committee shall allocate
approximately 30% of the budgeted allocation for FY2008 to assist in the planning and
management of energy-saving efforts in the future, such as additional staffing needs,
benchmarking studies, training efforts, and management systems.

b. By June 30, 2008, the Steering Committee shall issue a long-term action plan for the
achievement of the full 30% reduction in the City’s energy consumption and CO2 emissions by
2017. To the extent not already addressed by the short-term action plan to be established
pursuant to subdivision (a), the plan shall address:

i. Benchmarking of the energy consumption of all City buildings
(and any building for which the City pays energy costs),
reporting CO2 emissions and all types of energy use on a per
square foot or other unit basis over time;

ii. Identification of existing resources to be integrated into this
plan, including contract resources and information systems
(such as the Asset Information Management Survey);

iii. Identification of energy savings opportunities, including
establishment of an energy audit program to rank potential
sources of savings in buildings, and assessment of the
opportunity to utilize more efficient vehicles in the City’s fleet
and to reduce the overall use of non-emergency response
vehicles by City employees;

2

iv. Timelines to procure and implement program resources,
including but not limited to programs such as operations and
maintenance, building retrofits, real-time metering and
monitoring, water conservation, central management systems,
training of City facilities managers and others in energy-saving
maintenance, co-generation and standard specifications for
small-scale renovations;

v.
Measurement and verification protocols that will track
program savings;

vi. Pilot projects to assess the feasibility and economic potential
of new energy-saving technologies and methods;

vii. A structure through which agencies that manage facilities
will identify their own opportunities to reduce energy
consumption in an ongoing manner and contribute those
opportunities to an inter-agency plan for carbon reduction;

viii. Accountability and enforcement policies that will ensure that
agency heads undertake the energy savings for which they
are responsible;

ix. Any
staffing
or
other
organizational
needs
that
implementation of the plan may require; and

x. Any other energy-related projects that may contribute to the
goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

§ 4. Implementation. City agencies shall provide all necessary assistance to members of
the Steering Committee for the purpose of developing and implementing the short-term and
long-term plans.

§ 5. This Order shall take effect immediately.

_____________________________
Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

3

issue a short-term action plan for the use of the $80,000,000 budgeted in FY2008 for energy and
greenhouse gas emission reduction purposes. Projects that reduce the City’s energy consumption
and/or greenhouse gas footprint will be considered plan-eligible, including but not limited to
building retrofits, process and plug-load improvements, methane capture projects, and vehicle
retrofits or replacements. All buildings for which the City pays energy costs shall be considered
plan-eligible, and all forms of energy consumed, whether purchased centrally or not, shall be
considered plan-eligible. Return on investment and overall energy savings shall be the primary
bases for selecting and prioritizing projects. The Steering Committee shall allocate
approximately 30% of the budgeted allocation for FY2008 to assist in the planning and
management of energy-saving efforts in the future, such as additional staffing needs,
benchmarking studies, training efforts, and management systems.

b. By June 30, 2008, the Steering Committee shall issue a long-term action plan for the
achievement of the full 30% reduction in the City’s energy consumption and CO2 emissions by
2017. To the extent not already addressed by the short-term action plan to be established
pursuant to subdivision (a), the plan shall address:

i. Benchmarking of the energy consumption of all City buildings
(and any building for which the City pays energy costs),
reporting CO2 emissions and all types of energy use on a per
square foot or other unit basis over time;

ii. Identification of existing resources to be integrated into this
plan, including contract resources and information systems
(such as the Asset Information Management Survey);

iii. Identification of energy savings opportunities, including
establishment of an energy audit program to rank potential
sources of savings in buildings, and assessment of the
opportunity to utilize more efficient vehicles in the City’s fleet
and to reduce the overall use of non-emergency response
vehicles by City employees;

2

iv. Timelines to procure and implement program resources,
including but not limited to programs such as operations and
maintenance, building retrofits, real-time metering and
monitoring, water conservation, central management systems,
training of City facilities managers and others in energy-saving
maintenance, co-generation and standard specifications for
small-scale renovations;

v.
Measurement and verification protocols that will track
program savings;

vi. Pilot projects to assess the feasibility and economic potential
of new energy-saving technologies and methods;

vii. A structure through which agencies that manage facilities
will identify their own opportunities to reduce energy
consumption in an ongoing manner and contribute those
opportunities to an inter-agency plan for carbon reduction;

viii. Accountability and enforcement policies that will ensure that
agency heads undertake the energy savings for which they
are responsible;

ix. Any
staffing
or
other
organizational
needs
that
implementation of the plan may require; and

x. Any other energy-related projects that may contribute to the
goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

§ 4. Implementation. City agencies shall provide all necessary assistance to members of
the Steering Committee for the purpose of developing and implementing the short-term and
long-term plans.

§ 5. This Order shall take effect immediately.

_____________________________
Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

title: COORDINATION OF CITYWIDE SERVICES FOR VETERANS
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 110

COORDINATION OF CITYWIDE SERVICES FOR VETERANS

January 17, 2008

WHEREAS, veterans have played a crucial role in creating and protecting the
freedoms that all New Yorkers enjoy; and
WHEREAS, a large segment of the City’s population consists of either veterans,
or active duty or reserve members of the Armed Forces of the United States, and their
families; and
WHEREAS, a significant number of veterans are employed by the City; and
WHEREAS, the Mayor’s Office of Veterans’ Affairs (“MOVA”) was created by
Local Law No. 53 for the year 1987 to better assess the needs of the City’s veteran
population, and better coordinate service delivery to veterans and their families; and
WHEREAS, certain Mayoral agencies are responsible for providing a variety of
health and human services to address the needs of our citizens, such as public assistance,
employment and training, housing, health, medical and rehabilitation services; and
WHEREAS, the Commissioner of MOVA coordinates City services and develops
new strategies to address the needs of veterans;
NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New
York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Agency Coordinators for Veterans’ Services. The heads of all City
agencies shall appoint a senior level staff member of appropriate managerial authority
whose duty (in addition to his or her other responsibilities) it shall be:
a. to become familiar with personnel policies affecting veterans, reservists,
and National Guardsmen, and the special needs of and services available to
such persons and family members. The appointed staff members shall make
themselves available to the Commissioner of MOVA on an as needed basis
for advice, consultation, periodic training and information-sharing; and
b. to identify all services provided by their agencies that are available to
servicemembers, veterans and their families and inform MOVA of such
services in order to establish coherent and effective service delivery
mechanisms.
§ 2. Annual Plan. The Commissioner of MOVA shall set forth an annual plan
assessing the needs of the City’s veterans community, and methods by which MOVA
shall coordinate existing, or develop new, services and partnerships to address those
needs with the appropriate City agencies, community-based organizations, and the private
sector. The annual plan shall be submitted no later than July 1 of each year.
§ 3. Veterans’ Memorial Hall. The City shall provide appropriate office space to
be utilized for veterans’ service organizations. The Commissioner shall oversee such
space which shall be known as Veterans’ Memorial Hall and ensure that the occupants
thereof utilize and maintain their offices in a manner consistent with an operational
directive to be set forth by the Commissioner of Veterans’ Affairs to be followed by all
such veterans’ service organizations.

2

§ 4. Executive Order No. 22, dated November 28, 1990, is hereby REPEALED.
§ 5. Effective Date. This order shall take effect immediately.

___________________________

Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

title: DEPUTY MAYORS
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 111
DEPUTY MAYORS
February 20, 2008
By the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:
Section 1. There shall be seven Deputy Mayors. One shall be designated the First Deputy
Mayor, one shall be designated the Deputy Mayor for Education and Community Development,
one shall be designated the Deputy Mayor for Legal Affairs, one shall be designated the Deputy
Mayor for Economic Development, one shall be designated the Deputy Mayor for Operations,
one shall be designated the Deputy Mayor for Government Affairs and one shall be designated
the Deputy Mayor for Health and Human Services.
§ 2. The First Deputy Mayor shall:
a. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Department of Cultural Affairs, the
Department of Parks and Recreation, the Department of Design and Construction, the
Department of Consumer Affairs, the Commission for the United Nations, Consular Corps and
Protocol, the Commission on Women’s Issues and all administrations, departments, agencies,
boards, offices, committees and commissions except as otherwise provided herein, provided that
the Law Department, the Police Department, the Fire Department, the Office of Emergency
Management, the Department of Investigation, the Office of Management and Budget and the
Office of Labor Relations shall report directly to the Mayor.

b. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Mayor’s Offices of Correspondence,
Fiscal and Administrative Management, Appointments, Scheduling and Advance, Special
Projects and Community Events, and Citywide Event Coordination and Management and
supervise City sponsored public events of the City.
c. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Art Commission, the Landmarks
Preservation Commission, the Mayor’s Fund to Advance New York City, the Gracie Mansion
Conservancy, the Central Park Conservancy, libraries, museums, performing arts organizations,
gardens and zoos.
d. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee,
commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
e. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.
§ 3. The First Deputy Mayor hereby is delegated the authority to perform all functions,
powers or duties of the Mayor which the Mayor is authorized to delegate in the event that the
Mayor is unable to perform such functions, powers or duties for a reason specified in subdivision
a of section 10 of the New York City Charter.
§ 4. The Deputy Mayor for Education and Community Development shall:
a. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning, programs and initiatives.
b. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Department of Youth and Community
Development.
c. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Department of Education, the
New York City School Construction Authority, the New York City Educational Construction
Fund, the City University of New York, the City University Construction Fund and the New
York City Housing Authority.

2

d. Work with the other Deputy Mayors in coordination with the Office of Management
and Budget and the Office of Operations, to ensure the implementation of Mayoral policies and
initiatives.
e. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee,
commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
f. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.
§ 5. The Deputy Mayor for Legal Affairs shall:
a. Provide counsel to the Mayor on legal matters.
b. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Coordinator of Administrative Justice,
the Commission on Human Rights, the Office to Combat Domestic Violence, the Office for
People with Disabilities, the Office of Immigrant Affairs and the Office of Veterans Affairs.
c. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Mayor's Committee on the
Judiciary, the Conflicts of Interest Board, the Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings, the
Voter Assistance Commission, the Civilian Complaint Review Board, the Commission to
Combat Police Corruption and the Equal Employment Practices Commission.
d. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee,
commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
e. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.
§ 6. The Deputy Mayor for Economic Development shall:
a. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning, and programs designed to
foster the economic development or growth of the City, including those relating to the City's
overall business climate, the attraction, retention and expansion of domestic and global business
enterprises in the City, efforts to secure unique events, commercial, industrial and residential

3

development, waterfront development, energy, foreign trade and investment, government
regulation, film, theater and broadcasting, entertainment and sports facility development,
infrastructure, tourism and air, land and sea freight.
b. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Department of City Planning and the
Office of Film, Theater, and Broadcasting.
c. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the City Planning Commission, the
Housing Development Corporation, the United Nations Development Corporation, the Sports
Commission and Sports Development Corporation, the Board of Standards and Appeals, NYC &
Company, the Marketing Development Corporation, the Rent Guidelines Board, the Tax
Commission, the Tax Appeals Tribunal and the Loft Board.
d. Serve as Chairperson of the Commercial Incentive Boundary Area Commission and
the Industrial and Commercial Incentive Board.
e. Supervise and coordinate the activities of the Department of Small Business Services,
the Department of Housing Preservation and Development, the Department of Finance, the
Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications, the Business Integrity
Commission, and the Economic Development Corporation as provided in the Amended and
Restated Contracts between the City and the Economic Development Corporation, and take such
actions thereunder as are reserved to the Deputy Mayor.

f. Maintain liaison with the Police Pension Fund, Fire Department Pension Fund, New
York City Employees’ Retirement System, Teachers’ Retirement System and the Board of
Education Retirement System.
g. Maintain liaison with the New York State Department of Economic Development, the
City Empowerment Zone, the Empire State Development Corporation and its subsidiaries,

4

including the Lower Manhattan Development Corporation, the Port Authority of New York and
New Jersey, NYC and Company and other governmental and non-governmental agencies and
offices with respect to matters of City economic development and programs.
h. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor, including authorizations and
approvals to be made or given by the Mayor pursuant to sections 384, 824 and 1802 of the
Charter, in relation to the authorization or execution of deeds and satisfactions, leases,
easements, surrenders, restrictive declarations, mortgages and any other grants or acquisitions of
estates or interests in real property and licenses, permits or other agreements affecting the use of
real property.
i. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding tax policies.
j. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to any contracts with or
involving the New York City Industrial Development Agency or any other entity created for the
purpose of issuing bonds for, or managing, any project relating to any matter described in this
section.
k. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties
which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may
from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of
New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public Authorities
Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water
Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City
Transitional Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not
limited to, full power to execute for and on behalf of the Mayor, any agreement, amendment to
such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.

5

l. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution or
authorization of such franchises, concessions and revocable consents and other agreements as
relate to the duties of the Deputy Mayor for Economic Development.
m. Perform any function, power or duty which the Mayor has and is authorized to
delegate pursuant to New York City Charter sections 217, 219, 329 and 1301(2)(b) and
Administrative Code section 5-304.
n. Approve and sign applications to secure grant funds, submitted pursuant to provisions
of the New York State Environmental Conservation Law or the rules and regulations of the State
Department of Environmental Conservation, and to sign any other documents as may be
necessary to secure such funds.
o. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in negotiating, executing and
delivering any and all agreements, instruments and other documents necessary or desirable to
effectuate any of the matters referred to in this section or any of the programs, projects and
activities of any of the entities referred to in this section.
p. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee,
commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
q. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.
§ 7. The Deputy Mayor for Operations shall:
a. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Department of Buildings, Department of
Citywide Administrative Services, the Department of Environmental Protection, Department of
Sanitation, the Department of Transportation, the Criminal Justice Coordinator and the Mayor’s
Offices of Contract Services, Operations, Environmental Coordination, Long Term Planning and
Sustainability, and Special Enforcement..

6

b. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Taxi and Limousine Commission.
c. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning and programs related to
the management of the agencies that report directly to the Mayor, except for the Department of
Investigation and Law Department.
d. Develop, supervise and coordinate policies and programs relating to personnel and
management practices.
e. Direct and coordinate the activities of all administrations, departments, agencies,
boards, offices, committees and commissions with respect to energy policies, planning and
programs.
f. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties
which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may
from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of
New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public Authorities
Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, the New York City Municipal Water
Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City
Transitional Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not
limited to, full power to execute for and on behalf of the Mayor, any agreement, amendment to
such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.
g. Approve and sign applications to secure grant funds, submitted pursuant to provisions
of the New York State Environmental Conservation Law or the rules and regulations of the State
Department of Environmental Conservation, and to sign any other documents as may be
necessary to secure such funds.

7

h. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the City, official statements of the
City relating to the issuance of the City's obligations.
i. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution or
authorization of contracts, franchises, concessions, revocable consents, and other agreements.
j. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor, including authorizations and
approvals to be made or given by the Mayor pursuant to sections 384, 824 and 1802 of the
Charter, in relation to the authorization or execution of deeds and satisfactions, leases,
easements, surrenders, restrictive declarations, mortgages, and any other grants or acquisitions of
estates or interests in real property and licenses, permits or other agreements affecting the use of
real property.
k. Perform any function, power or duty which the Mayor has and is authorized to
delegate pursuant to New York City Charter sections 217, 219, 329 and 1301(2)(b), and pursuant
to Administrative Code section 5-304.
l. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Metropolitan Transportation
Authority, the Power Authority of the State of New York, and the New York State Public
Service Commission.
m..Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in negotiating, executing and
delivering any and all agreements, instruments and other documents necessary or desirable to
effectuate any of the matters referred to in this section or any of the programs, projects and
activities of any of the entities referred to in this section.
n. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee,
commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
o. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.

8

§ 8. The Deputy Mayor for Government Relations shall:
a. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Office of Intergovernmental Affairs, the
Office of City Legislative Affairs, the Office of State Legislative Affairs, the Office of Federal
Affairs and the Department of Records and Information Services.
b. Serve as the Mayor's representative, either directly or through the Offices of City and
State Legislative Affairs, on, and maintain liaison with, regional bodies and intergovernmental
agencies operating within the New York metropolitan region.
c. Maintain liaison, either directly or through the Office of Federal Affairs with the
United States Conference of Mayors, the National League of Cities, the New York Conference of
Mayors and other similar bodies.
d. Develop and implement the Mayor’s city, state and federal legislative agenda, serve as
the Mayor’s primary liaison to city, state and federal legislators and staff, supervise and
coordinate the legislative agenda of Mayoral agencies and develop, supervise and coordinate
policies and programs to secure funds from the federal and state governments.
e. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee,
commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
f. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.
§ 9. The Deputy Mayor for Health and Human Services shall:
a. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Department of Health and Mental
Hygiene,
the
Department
of
Homeless
Services,
the
Human
Resources
Administration/Department of Social Services, the Department of Correction, the Department of
Probation, the Department of Juvenile Justice, the Administration for Children’s Services, the
Department for the Aging and the Office of Health Insurance Access.

9

b. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Health and Hospitals Corporation
and the HIV Health and Human Services Planning Council
c. Succeed to the powers and duties of the “Deputy Mayor – City Administrator of the
City” under section 7384 of the Unconsolidated Laws (Chapter 1016 of the Laws of 1969).
d. Execute and deliver, in the name and on behalf of the Mayor, a certificate approving
any borrowing of funds or pledge of assets or revenues by the New York City Health and
Hospitals Corporation which would require the approval of the Mayor pursuant to the
“Memorandum of Agreement Between New York City Health and Hospitals Corporation and
The City of New York Relating to Operating Expenditures by the Corporation”, dated July 1,
1970.
e. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee,
commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
f. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.
§ 10. Executive Order No. 85, dated February 6, 2006, is hereby REPEALED.
§ 11. This Order shall take effect immediately.

_____________________________
Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

protection of the municipal water supply pursuant to section 4-106(9) of the Administrative Code
and section 384 of the Charter.

Easements. The Director of the Mayor's Office of Contract Services, and staff of such Office
designated by such Director, are hereby authorized to arrange and administer any public

hearings, including required public notice thereof, to be held in connection with the acquisition
of real property outside of the City of New York for water supply purposes pursuant to section 5-
358 of the Administrative Code, and in connection with the granting of easements for the
protection of the municipal water supply pursuant to section 4-106(9) of the Administrative Code
and section 384 of the Charter.

title: HHS-CONNECT
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No.114

HHS-CONNECT

March 18, 2008

WHEREAS, this Administration is committed to improving the delivery of services to
New Yorkers with state-of-the-art technology; and

WHEREAS, the City provides a wide range of health and human services to a diverse
client population; and

WHEREAS, among the agencies providing such services are the Administration for
Children’s Services, Department for the Aging, Department of Correction, Department of Health
and Mental Hygiene, Department of Homeless Services, Department of Juvenile Justice,
Department of Probation, Health and Hospitals Corporation, and Human Resources
Administration, referred to collectively herein as “HHS agencies;” and

WHEREAS, many New Yorkers qualify for and participate in multiple programs
provided by different HHS agencies; and

WHEREAS, sharing of client data among HHS Agencies will provide a more complete
understanding of clients’ needs and enable more efficient and effective service delivery; and

WHEREAS, the City has committed to launching HHS-Connect, a technology solution
that connects clients, agencies, and providers, and will utilize ground-breaking and innovative
technologies to improve the City’s ability to serve its population;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as the Mayor of the City of New York
it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. HHS-Connect is hereby established to facilitate data integration and exchange
between existing agency-based information management systems through the following:

a. Innovative technology tools. HHS-Connect shall implement innovative tools to
provide City workers with cutting-edge technologies to improve the speed and accuracy
of services.

b. Common data model. HHS-Connect shall support data integration and exchange,
including creation of a common data model for HHS-Connect.

c. Data sharing strategy. HHS-Connect shall employ a data sharing strategy to enable
relevant agencies to exchange client and program data.

d. Enterprise case management. HHS-Connect shall provide requesting HHS agencies
with a common technology platform for case management.

e. Integrated case folder. HHS-Connect shall oversee the creation of a virtual integrated
case file for clients, using a common client index to locate clients in separate systems and
document image management tools to electronically capture and share client documents.
This case folder shall be available online.

f. Business process reengineering. HHS-Connect shall ensure streamlined business
processes to improve and coordinate case management practices across agencies.

g. Performance measurement and outcome evaluation. HHS-Connect shall enable the
City to measure client outcomes based on a holistic view of clients across agencies.

h. Confidentiality. HHS-Connect shall ensure the protection of the confidentiality of
information as required by applicable law.

§2. All agencies are directed to identify appropriate programs, data and technology
assets that can expand and enhance HHS-Connect. To the greatest possible extent, HHS-
Connect shall leverage existing Citywide technology assets to accelerate the pace of the project
and increase the effectiveness and efficiency of the services delivered to the Agencies, their
clients, and external service providers.

§ 3. Data Sharing. For the purposes of HHS-Connect, agencies shall consider all data for
data sharing while ensuring compliance with all applicable Federal, State and local laws and
regulations. To facilitate data sharing, agencies shall work with the HHS-Connect team to
identify data sharing needs, as well as sources and types of data. Data sharing shall occur in a
timely fashion and agencies shall facilitate real-time data exchanges whenever possible, as set
forth by the HHS-Connect data sharing strategy.

§ 4. Alignment with Citywide IT Strategy. HHS-Connect shall be aligned with and
further the Citywide Information Technology strategy, including security requirements and
enterprise architecture standards, as set forth by the Department of Information Technology and
Telecommunications (“DOITT”).

§ 5. HHS-Connect shall be implemented by a Chief Information Officer for Health and
Human Services (“CIO for HHS”) who shall report to the Deputy Mayor for Health and Human
Services, or other appropriate senior level official, and shall provide oversight and coordination
of the technology strategy and architecture of HHS agencies, in conjunction with DOITT.

§6. Cooperation and Assistance: The heads of all agencies shall cooperate with and
assist the CIO for HHS in the implementation of HHS-Connect as requested.

§7. This Order shall take effect immediately.

___________________________
Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

title: CUSTOMER SERVICE
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 115

CUSTOMER SERVICE

May 15, 2008

WHEREAS, New York City’s residents, businesses, employees and visitors are
the customers of City government; and

WHEREAS, the City’s customers should expect a consistent high level of service
when they interact with City agencies, and deserve meaningful and timely responses to
their inquiries, service requests or other applications for governmental action; and

WHEREAS, the City is committed to serving its customers in a responsive,
efficient, transparent and accountable manner; and

WHEREAS, a centralized, strategic approach, through proper cooperation and
coordination among City agencies, is required to fulfill this commitment; and

WHEREAS, the Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications
(“DOITT”), through the 311 Customer Service Center (“311”), has successfully provided
New Yorkers with uniformly rapid and centralized access to City services; and

WHEREAS, applying this uniform approach and high-level of customer service
to agency operations is essential to fostering confidence in government operations and
equal access to City services for all eligible customers.

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New
York, it is hereby ordered that:

Section 1. There is created within the Mayor’s Office of Operations (“Office of
Operations”) a Customer Service Office.

§ 2. The Customer Service Office shall be responsible for:

(a) developing, implementing and assuring the quality of a citywide customer
service strategy to establish standards and policies for customer-facing
functions within City agencies including: agency call centers; appropriate

greeting and directional signage in areas where customers interact with agency
staff; reasonable, well-communicated wait times and queuing processes for
customer service; appropriate systems for follow-up after the customer’s
initial inquiry or interaction with a City agency, and all other appropriate areas
of customer interaction;

(b) working to ensure consistency in service delivery and transparency of agency
processes across all service delivery channels whether services are provided in
person, by 311 or the web; and

(c) working with 311 to develop a strategy to provide callers and customers with
the highest level of customer service.

§ 3. All City agencies shall establish by June 1, 2008, or as soon as practicable
thereafter, a Service Level Agreement (“SLA”) for each service request taken by 311
without regard for the means, methods or systems used to capture and process such
service requests. Each agency SLA shall reflect a reasonable representation of the time
frame in which an agency can give a status message to a customer about a request. The
reasonableness of each agency SLA shall be subject to review by DOITT and the Office
of Operations.

§ 4. As individual agency work order systems are phased-out consistent with the
customer-service strategy required by this Order, they may only be replaced with a
common work-order system or a compatible system approved by DOITT and the Office
of Operations.

§ 5. All agencies and administrative tribunals shall cooperate with the Office of
Operations in implementing the provisions of this Order.

§ 6. This Order shall take effect immediately.

___________________________
Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

title: COORDINATOR OF FAMILY SERVICES
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 116

COORDINATOR OF FAMILY SERVICES

June 13, 2008

WHEREAS, the City’s system of providing vital health and human services to
children and families is divided among many agencies; and

WHEREAS, the City is committed to enhancing these services by investing
significant resources, including for the recruitment of additional caseworkers, as well as
strengthening training and supervision of staff overseeing children’s and family services;
and

WHEREAS, agencies tasked with identifying vulnerable children and families
have adopted comprehensive policies and procedures to investigate potential abuse and
neglect; and

WHEREAS, the collection of statistics and the dissemination of information to
the appropriate agencies is necessary for the successful delivery of services to vulnerable
children and families; and

WHEREAS, economic opportunities must be available to reduce the number of
people living in poverty, and the City has established a coordinated multi-agency policy
to create communities of economic opportunity and financial independence for
vulnerable children and families; and

WHEREAS, there is an ongoing need for improvement in technology,
communication, coordination and cooperation among the various agencies involved in
serving the needs of vulnerable children and families; and

WHEREAS, the position of Coordinator of Family Services was first established
in 2006 to facilitate the necessary inter-agency communication and cooperation to ensure
that New York City’s most vulnerable children and families are well-served and
protected;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New
York, it is hereby ordered that:

§ 1.
The position of Coordinator of Family Services is hereby continued in the
Office of the Mayor. With regard to children’s and family services, the Coordinator
shall, in consultation with affected agencies:

(a)
coordinate, implement and monitor improvements in the dissemination of
information about children and family services;

(b)
request and receive reports concerning agency performance,
including appropriate use of technology, and recommend and facilitate
implementation of policies to improve agency efficiency with respect to
children and family services. The content of such reports and any such
policies for reform shall be established by the Coordinator;

(c)
expand agency partnerships with Community Based Organizations
that advocate for child safety;

(d)
aid in the development of medical standards utilized by New York
City hospitals to diagnose child abuse and neglect;

(e)
develop, coordinate and implement programs and services for
youth in the foster care system, youth aging out of the foster care system
and youth in the juvenile detention system;

(f)
foster the increase, utilization and expansion of Child Advocacy
Centers throughout the City;

(g)
design and implement a Citywide public awareness campaign and
website to prevent and stop child abuse and child neglect;

(h)
 coordinate agency efforts to improve access to early intervention
public health insurance for children in City-funded programs, subsidized
child care and head start;

(i)
develop, coordinate and implement plans to increase access to
quality mental health services for children in foster care and the juvenile
justice system;

(j)
develop, with the Department of Juvenile Justice, prevention,
aftercare, and alternatives to detention programs;

(k)
develop an overall accountability model for social services
agencies providing services to children, families and individuals;

(l)
implement a family services website to provide information to
agency clients and personnel on programs, policies and procedures, as

2

well as to conduct eligibility screening;

(m)
implement an enhanced 311 system for City residents seeking
health and human services;

(n)
develop partnerships with other branches and levels of
government, including with the Office of the Speaker of the City Council
to increase food stamp utilization, better school meal participation and
access to healthy foods in high needs communities;

(o)
implement a “one-stop” service center for benefits and case
assistance;

(p)
facilitate a case coordination partnership with the Criminal Justice
Coordinator and the Family Court case coordinator; and

(q)
establish a network of agency liaisons, to be designated
individually by each human services agency, to facilitate service
coordination.

§ 2.
Affected agencies shall provide such assistance and cooperation as
deemed appropriate by the Mayor and the Coordinator.

§ 3.
For purposes of Sections 1 and 2 of this Order, the term “affected
agencies” shall include, but not be limited to, the following agencies: Department of
Health and Mental Hygiene, Human Resources Administration, Administration for
Children’s Services, Department of Youth and Community Development, Department of
Homeless Services, Department for the Aging, Health and Hospitals Corporation,
Department of Correction, Department of Probation, Department of Juvenile Justice,
Department of Education, New York City Housing Authority, Mayor’s Office to Combat
Domestic Violence, Mayor’s Office of Adult Education, Office of Citywide Health
Insurance Access and the HIV Health and Human Services Planning Council.

§ 4. This Order shall take effect immediately.

EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 116

COORDINATOR OF FAMILY SERVICES

June 13, 2008

WHEREAS, the City’s system of providing vital health and human services to
children and families is divided among many agencies; and

WHEREAS, the City is committed to enhancing these services by investing
significant resources, including for the recruitment of additional caseworkers, as well as
strengthening training and supervision of staff overseeing children’s and family services;
and

WHEREAS, agencies tasked with identifying vulnerable children and families
have adopted comprehensive policies and procedures to investigate potential abuse and
neglect; and

WHEREAS, the collection of statistics and the dissemination of information to
the appropriate agencies is necessary for the successful delivery of services to vulnerable
children and families; and

WHEREAS, economic opportunities must be available to reduce the number of
people living in poverty, and the City has established a coordinated multi-agency policy
to create communities of economic opportunity and financial independence for
vulnerable children and families; and

WHEREAS, there is an ongoing need for improvement in technology,
communication, coordination and cooperation among the various agencies involved in
serving the needs of vulnerable children and families; and

WHEREAS, the position of Coordinator of Family Services was first established
in 2006 to facilitate the necessary inter-agency communication and cooperation to ensure
that New York City’s most vulnerable children and families are well-served and
protected;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New
York, it is hereby ordered that:

§ 1.
The position of Coordinator of Family Services is hereby continued in the
Office of the Mayor. With regard to children’s and family services, the Coordinator
shall, in consultation with affected agencies:

(a)
coordinate, implement and monitor improvements in the dissemination of
information about children and family services;

(b)
request and receive reports concerning agency performance,
including appropriate use of technology, and recommend and facilitate
implementation of policies to improve agency efficiency with respect to
children and family services. The content of such reports and any such
policies for reform shall be established by the Coordinator;

(c)
expand agency partnerships with Community Based Organizations
that advocate for child safety;

(d)
aid in the development of medical standards utilized by New York
City hospitals to diagnose child abuse and neglect;

(e)
develop, coordinate and implement programs and services for
youth in the foster care system, youth aging out of the foster care system
and youth in the juvenile detention system;

(f)
foster the increase, utilization and expansion of Child Advocacy
Centers throughout the City;

(g)
design and implement a Citywide public awareness campaign and
website to prevent and stop child abuse and child neglect;

(h)
 coordinate agency efforts to improve access to early intervention
public health insurance for children in City-funded programs, subsidized
child care and head start;

(i)
develop, coordinate and implement plans to increase access to
quality mental health services for children in foster care and the juvenile
justice system;

(j)
develop, with the Department of Juvenile Justice, prevention,
aftercare, and alternatives to detention programs;

(k)
develop an overall accountability model for social services
agencies providing services to children, families and individuals;

(l)
implement a family services website to provide information to
agency clients and personnel on programs, policies and procedures, as

2

well as to conduct eligibility screening;

(m)
implement an enhanced 311 system for City residents seeking
health and human services;

(n)
develop partnerships with other branches and levels of
government, including with the Office of the Speaker of the City Council
to increase food stamp utilization, better school meal participation and
access to healthy foods in high needs communities;

(o)
implement a “one-stop” service center for benefits and case
assistance;

(p)
facilitate a case coordination partnership with the Criminal Justice
Coordinator and the Family Court case coordinator; and

(q)
establish a network of agency liaisons, to be designated
individually by each human services agency, to facilitate service
coordination.

§ 2.
Affected agencies shall provide such assistance and cooperation as
deemed appropriate by the Mayor and the Coordinator.

§ 3.
For purposes of Sections 1 and 2 of this Order, the term “affected
agencies” shall include, but not be limited to, the following agencies: Department of
Health and Mental Hygiene, Human Resources Administration, Administration for
Children’s Services, Department of Youth and Community Development, Department of
Homeless Services, Department for the Aging, Health and Hospitals Corporation,
Department of Correction, Department of Probation, Department of Juvenile Justice,
Department of Education, New York City Housing Authority, Mayor’s Office to Combat
Domestic Violence, Mayor’s Office of Adult Education, Office of Citywide Health
Insurance Access and the HIV Health and Human Services Planning Council.

§ 4. This Order shall take effect immediately.

_____________________

Michael R. Bloomberg

Mayor

title: CENTER FOR ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 117

CENTER FOR ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY

June 13, 2008

WHEREAS, New York City government has studied the nature of poverty in the
City and devised a blueprint to reduce it and increase access to opportunity for the poor;
and

WHEREAS, the City is pinpointing concrete ways in which it can act to ensure
the poor have the protections and resources they need to help themselves move ahead;
and

WHEREAS, it is critical that the City’s policies, programs and public/private
partnerships in the areas of education, health and human services, housing and
community development, workforce development, economic development, consumer
protection, and criminal justice are well-coordinated and embrace common principles
designed to create opportunities to advance the poor; and

WHEREAS, the City is committed to a continuous and well-coordinated inter-agency strategy to achieve these goals and is developing new policies, programs and
public/private partnerships; and

WHEREAS, the Center for Economic Opportunity was initially established in the
Office of the Mayor in 2006 to further develop and implement this strategy and has
already launched anti-poverty pilot programs, including Opportunity NYC which is the
nation’s first conditional cash transfer program; and

WHEREAS, the need for the continuation of the Center for Economic
Opportunity is necessary to ensure full communication, cooperation, ownership and
success in the development, implementation and evaluation of new policies, programs
and public/private partnerships;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New
York, it is hereby ordered that:

Section 1.
The Center for Economic Opportunity (“CEO”) is continued in the
Office of the Mayor and shall be headed by an Executive Director.

§ 2.
CEO shall undertake the following activities:

a.
Poverty Research. CEO shall research poverty in terms of its
measure and impacts on certain populations as appropriate.

b.
Innovation Fund. CEO shall manage an Innovation Fund of City
resources dedicated to developing and supporting new anti-poverty
programs with City Agencies. City funds may be augmented by
other government and private resources.

c.
Developing and evaluating anti-poverty strategies. CEO shall
develop and evaluate the City’s new anti-poverty programs,
ensuring that City funds are targeted and programs are evaluated
for impact. Programs will be closely monitored and independently
evaluated. If programs do not achieve their intended results,
resources will be dedicated to more promising strategies. CEO
shall manage external consultants in evaluating all City agency
programs funded through the Innovation Fund

d.
Opportunity NYC. CEO shall be responsible for identifying
private funding for anti-poverty pilot programs, including
Opportunity NYC. CEO shall work to develop, fund and evaluate
these programs. The funds shall be deposited with the Mayor’s
Fund to Advance New York City. CEO shall have oversight of,
and responsibility for, all external contracts for design, operation
and evaluation of Opportunity NYC and will act as the designee of
the Mayor’s Fund for Opportunity NYC funds held by the Mayor’s
Fund as per the agreements of July 16, 2007 and November 16,
2007 and contracts with each private foundation.

e.
Findings and Evaluation of Results. CEO shall publish findings,
where appropriate, on program results and poverty in the City.

§ 3.
The heads of all agencies shall provide such assistance and cooperation as
deemed appropriate by the Mayor and the Executive Director.

§ 4.
This order shall take effect immediately.

___________________________
Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor
