title: REPEAL OF PRIOR EXECUTIVE ORDERS RELATING TO THE INDIGENT DEFENSE PLAN FOR THE CITY OF NEW YORK
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 136

July 13, 2010

REPEAL OF PRIOR EXECUTIVE ORDERS RELATING TO THE INDIGENT DEFENSE
PLAN FOR THE CITY OF NEW YORK

WHEREAS, pursuant to the provisions of Article 18-B of the County Law (“18-B”), the
City of New York (“the City”) is required to provide counsel to persons charged with a crime or
who are entitled to counsel pursuant to Family Court Act §§ 262 or 1120, Correction Law article
6-C or Surrogate’s Court Procedure Act § 407, and who are financially unable to obtain counsel
within the meaning of County Law § 722; and

WHEREAS, the Office of the Criminal Justice Coordinator has promulgated rules, set
forth in chapter 13 of Title 43 of the Rules of the City of New York, that establish a plan for
representation of such persons pursuant to the above statutory provisions; and

WHEREAS, such rules constitute full and sufficient legal authority for the present
Indigent Defense Plan for the City of New York,

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New
York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Repeal of Executive Orders. Executive Order No. 132 of 2010 and Executive
Order No. 118 of 2008, both entitled “Indigent Defense Plan for the City of New York,” are
hereby repealed. Further, Executive Order No. 178 of 1965, entitled “Furnishing Counsel to
Indigent Criminal Defendants Within the City of New York,” is hereby repealed, except that
Criminal Defense Panels created under the authority of Executive Order 178 of 1965 and
pursuant to the plan submitted by bar associations in accordance with subdivision 3 of section
722 of the County Law shall continue to exist and shall be administered in accordance with the
rules of the Appellate Division, First and Second Judicial Departments.

§ 2. This Order shall take effect immediately.

Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

title: MAYOR’S OFFICE OF MEDIA AND ENTERTAINMENT
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No.138

July 26, 2010

MAYOR’S OFFICE OF MEDIA AND ENTERTAINMENT

WHEREAS New York City is an international center of new and traditional media, and
the continued health and development of all forms of media are vital to the economic success of
the City; and

WHEREAS, there is a need for uniform operation of the City’s diverse media functions,
including operation of the City’s media assets, encouragement of local economic activity by the
film, broadcasting, cable, theatre and digital industries and encouragement and development of
new media technologies; and

WHEREAS, to ensure the City’s media services are well-coordinated to maximize
opportunities in the most efficient and cost effective manner, the functions of New York City
Media Group (NYC Media), Mayor’s Office of Film Theatre and Broadcasting (“MOFTB”), and
certain digital and new media functions should be operated jointly; and

WHEREAS, Charter § 1072(p) grants the Department of Information Technology and
Telecommunications (“DOITT”) the power to perform such responsibilities with respect to
information technology and telecommunications as the Mayor shall direct; and

WHEREAS, DOITT is the license holder for the City’s television and radio stations,
which, together with its cable assets, comprise NYC Media; and

WHEREAS, MOFTB currently resides in the Department of Small Business Services
(“DSBS”) and was established by Executive Order No. 47 dated January 4, 1993, as amended by
Executive Order No. 49, dated September 13, 2004, to issue required permits for film, television
and still photography production in the City and to provide information, assistance, programming
and other necessary activities to facilitate and encourage film, theatre and television activities in
the City;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is
hereby ordered:

Section 1.
Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment. The Mayor’s Office of
Media and Entertainment is hereby established.

§2.
Scope of Duties. The Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment (“MOME”)
shall consist of NYC Media, MOFTB and the Office of Digital Coordination, and shall be
headed by a commissioner, to be appointed by and serve at the pleasure of the Mayor. The
commissioner shall report to the Deputy Mayor for Economic Development and work closely
with the commissioner of DOITT on administrative and operational priorities and policies. The
commissioner of MOME shall also serve as the commissioner of MOFTB. The commissioner
shall take all appropriate steps to integrate staff functions and titles of the units operated under
MOME.

§ 3.
NYC Media. NYC Media shall:

a.
Serve as the official television, radio and online network of the City.

b.
Develop, produce, broadcast and otherwise distribute programmatic
content about the City.

c.
Perform such other functions as are deemed necessary by the
commissioner of the Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment to facilitate the
development and dissemination of programmatic content about the City.

§ 4. Continuation of MOFTB. Nothing in this Order shall affect the jurisdiction of
MOFTB as set forth in Executive Order No. 47, dated January 4, 1993, as amended by Executive
Order No. 49, dated September 13, 2004. Staffing and other assistance to the Mayor’s Office of
Film, Theatre and Broadcasting may be provided by the DOITT, DSBS or by any other
appropriate agency. MOFTB’s function of issuing all permits required for film and television
production and for still photography shoots in the City shall remain in DSBS. To preserve the
regulatory jurisdiction of MOFTB, the Commissioner of MOME shall be an SBS employee and
shall manage all appropriate DOITT staff.

§ 5. Office of Digital Coordination. The Office of Digital Coordination shall work with
DOITT’s Office of Web and New Media Operations to coordinate the City’s digital media, and
shall have responsibility for the design and direction of the City’s message across all channels of
the City’s website, social media, mobile and other digital media initiatives in order to enhance
communications between City government and the public.

§ 6.
Effective as of the date of this order, or as soon as practicable thereafter, the
following functions currently performed by DSBS shall be transferred to DOITT and supervised
and/or managed by the Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment:

a.
Provision of information and assistance necessary to enable filmmakers
and broadcasters to operate in the City;

2

b.
Development of programs and activities designed to encourage theatrical
production and attendance in the City;

c.
Coordination of assistance from other City agencies for films and
television productions in the City;

d.
Marketing of the City as a location for film, theater, and television
production; and

e.
Provision of support services for the issuance of all permits required for
film and television production and for still photography shoots in the City.

§ 7. The personnel of the Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment shall be employees
of DOITT, except as otherwise provided by this executive order. DOITT shall provide
administrative and technical support to the Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment,
including staffing, human resources and labor relations; legal services; general financial services
support including budget, payroll, procurement and payables/receivables; and technical support
including desktop, network and fiber/wireless communications.

§ 8. The Department of Citywide Administrative Services, DOITT, and DSBS shall take
all steps necessary, consistent with applicable law, to implement this Order, including ensuring
the transfer, pursuant to section 70(2) of the Civil Service Law, of employees substantially
engaged in the performance of the functions described in section 4. Employees who are subject
to pending disciplinary charges on the date of the functional transfer, or against whom a
disciplinary penalty has been assessed but not yet served or paid, on or prior to such date, shall
be retained in the employment of DSBS until the resolution of the adjudicative or administrative
proceedings and until any outstanding disciplinary penalty has been served or paid.

§ 9.
This Order shall take effect immediately.

Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

title: CHIEF INVESTMENT ADVISOR
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 139

September 2, 2010

CHIEF INVESTMENT ADVISOR

WHEREAS, the City has five pension systems that offer defined benefit retirement plans to
more than 350,000 City employees and 275,000 retirees or their beneficiaries: the New York City
Employees’ Retirement System (“NYCERS”), the Police Pension Fund (“PPF”), the Fire Pension
Fund (“Fire”), the Teachers Retirement System (“TRS”) and the Board of Education Retirement
System (“BERS”) (collectively “the Systems”); and

WHEREAS, the Comptroller, through the Bureau of Asset Management, is the investment
advisor to, and custodian of, the five system funds; and

WHEREAS, the City offers a defined contribution plan to its employees, known as the
Deferred Compensation Plan (the “Plan”), which is administered by the Office of Labor Relations;
and

WHEREAS, each of the Systems and the Plan has a Board of Trustees to fulfill its
investment and administrative functions, and such Trustees have a fiduciary responsibility to ensure
that all investment and administrative decisions are made in the best interests of their respective
system and the Plan; and

WHEREAS, in addition to the Comptroller and various union leaders, the Mayor and/or
members of the Administration, including the Police Commissioner, Fire Commissioner, Finance
Commissioner, Chancellor of Education and members of the Panel on Educational Policy hold exofficio seats on one or more System boards; and

WHEREAS, the Mayor and members of the Administration, including the Commissioner of
Labor Relations, Corporation Counsel, Director of the Office of Management and Budget,
Commissioner of Citywide Administrative Services, and Finance Commissioner hold ex-officio seats
on the Board of the Deferred Compensation Plan; and

WHEREAS, pension benefits are defined by law and paid by the Systems to retirees and their
beneficiaries regardless of whether annual investment income and employee contributions are
sufficient to meet these obligations – that is because the City must make contributions to cover any
system shortfalls; and

WHEREAS, because of adverse market conditions, enhancements in statutory benefits, and
increases in the number of disability pensions granted, the City’s pension contributions to cover such
shortfalls have increased dramatically in recent years; and

WHEREAS, in order to preserve tax dollars for pension and non-pension related expenses,
and to ensure appropriate investment opportunities are offered to employees participating in the
Deferred Compensation Plan, the Administration’s representatives on the Systems’ boards and the
Plan must have an independent source of financial advice, available to guide them in their work with
other trustees and the Bureau of Asset Management, at all times in making investment decisions
among all asset classes;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is
hereby ordered that:

Section 1. Chief Investment Advisor. There is hereby established the position of Chief
Investment Advisor. The Chief Investment Advisor shall:

(a) Direct all activities of, and be responsible for staffing, the Mayor’s Office of Pensions
and Investments, formerly known as the Mayor’s Pension Unit;

(b) Serve as a financial advisor to all members of the Administration serving on the pension
boards or the Deferred Compensation Plan Board, on all respective investment activities
before the boards;

(c) Recommend sound investment policies that balance the City's goals of generating higher
returns on pension assets while managing economic, capital markets and liquidity related
risks within the portfolios, and reducing long-term costs of benefit payments;

(d) Monitor the performance of investments and investment managers for all asset classes
held by the Systems and the Plan;

(e) Serve as the principal liaison with the Comptroller's Bureau of Asset Management to
ensure that all appropriate information regarding investments is analyzed and integrated
into the performance reviews of investment managers, as well as the analysis and
development of investment strategies, and provided timely and accurately to all Trustees;

(f) Serve as a liaison to the Chief Actuary;

(g) Conduct research on all relevant investment issues that impact the portfolios;

(h) Provide the Administration’s Trustees on the pension boards, and the members of the
Deferred Compensation Plan board, any appropriate investment reviews, reports and
presentations;

(i) Make recommendations to Trustees on asset allocation, investment strategy,
selection and termination for and among investments in all asset classes;

2

(j) Evaluate non-traditional investment opportunities, including in the private equity market
sector, hedge funds, and real estate and assist in assessing their appropriateness for
investment by the Systems and Plan;

(k) Meet and report on meetings with consultants and potential investment partners in
connection with prospective investment opportunities;

(l) Evaluate current methodologies and technology for effective risk analysis and identify
and analyze new and innovative risk management tools and/or strategies; and

(m) Work with Office of Management and Budget, Chief Actuary and others to evaluate
interactions between market conditions, statutory benefits and pension contributions
to improve funding levels for the Systems, as well as predictability and stability in costs
of benefit payments;

(n) Assist in negotiating the terms and conditions of investment contracts with
investment managers and banks;

(o) Assist in monitoring legislative efforts concerning City pensions to reduce
unnecessary economic and administrative burdens on the Systems;

(p) Work in cooperation with the all non-Administration Trustees to achieve the
goal of maximizing investment returns within acceptable risk tolerances.

§ 2. Oversight. The CIA shall report to the Commissioner of Finance. The Deputy Mayor
for Economic Development shall oversee the Department of Finance for the purposes of reviewing
the activities of the CIA and the Office. The CIA shall consult regularly with the Office of
Management and Budget, Corporation Counsel, the Deputy Mayor for Economic Development, and
the Deputy Mayor for Operations regarding the potential fiscal impacts and legal liabilities of
investment and policy matters coming before the Boards, as well as any efforts to reform the City’s
pension systems.

§ 3. Cooperation and Assistance. All affected agencies shall cooperate and provide
appropriate assistance to the CIA upon request.

§ 4. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

____________________________________
Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

 3

investment and policy matters coming before the Boards, as well as any efforts to reform the City’s

§ 3. Cooperation and Assistance. All affected agencies shall cooperate and provide
appropriate assistance to the CIA upon request.

§ 4. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

Michael R. Bloomberg

title: AUTHORIZING THE DEPARTMENT OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS TO CONSOLIDATE THE INFRASTRUCTURE OF AND ESTABLISH COORDINATED CITYWIDE POLICIES FOR INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS FOR THE CITY OF NEW YORK
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 140

October 20, 2010

AUTHORIZING THE DEPARTMENT OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AND
TELECOMMUNICATIONS TO CONSOLIDATE THE INFRASTRUCTURE OF AND
ESTABLISH COORDINATED CITYWIDE POLICIES FOR INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS FOR THE CITY OF NEW YORK

WHEREAS, innovations in technology improve service to the City’s 8.4 million
customers and increase agency efficiency; and

WHEREAS, the City of New York has been and will continue to be a leader in using
technology to improve the delivery of City services to its customers; and

WHEREAS, Information Technology (IT) for the City is currently managed in a
decentralized manner across dozens of City agencies and entities with limited Citywide policies,
standards or protocols; and

WHEREAS, technology advancements now enable significant cost savings and improved
efficiency, security and service through a consolidated infrastructure and a coordinated approach
to Citywide IT policies; and

WHEREAS, a consolidated IT infrastructure and a coordinated approach to Citywide IT
policies will enable the City to standardize hardware and software platforms, improve IT service
delivery to agencies, better leverage technology investments, implement best practices, reduce IT
costs, enable agencies to focus on their core competencies, and reduce the environmental impact
associated with IT infrastructure; and

WHEREAS, City agencies are dependent upon IT to carry out their respective missions
and, therefore, should participate in and contribute to the process of consolidating IT
infrastructure and the establishment of Citywide IT policies; and

WHEREAS, New York City Charter section 1072, which directs that the Department of
Information Technology and Telecommunications (DoITT) “Plan, formulate, coordinate and
advance information technology and telecommunications policies for the City” and “perform
such other responsibilities with respect to information technology and telecommunications
matters…as the Mayor shall direct,” makes DoITT the appropriate agency to consolidate and
manage IT infrastructure and establish and enforce coordinated Citywide IT policies;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is
hereby ordered:

Section 1. DoITT shall be responsible for establishing and enforcing Citywide IT policies
and for ensuring that such policies are aligned with the City’s business needs and investments, as
well as the individual business needs of each agency;

(a) Citywide IT policies shall include, but not be limited to:

1. the acquisition and provision of datacenter sites and similar IT facilities;

2. the acquisition and provision of wired and wireless networks;

3. the assessment and standardization of IT applications that have a multiagency or citywide impact, and evaluation of how applications can be
coordinated among City agencies;

4. the maintenance of an interoperable Geographic Information Systems
platform and related systems;

5. the provision of IT security services and standards;

6. the development and application of enterprise architecture standards;

7. all other areas deemed appropriate by the Strategic Governance Board.

(b) Agencies shall review IT investments with DoITT prior to final approval by the
Office of Management and Budget to avoid duplicative efforts between agencies and
ensure alignment with Citywide IT policies. This shall apply to all IT investments,
regardless of funding source;

(c) DoITT shall expand its enterprise contract portfolio for suitable hardware, software
and services to realize economies of scale and maximize the benefits of the City’s
investments; agencies must use these contracts unless they and DoITT find such
contracts unsuitable for a particular business need, and are further responsible for
working with DoITT and the Mayor’s Office of Contract Services (MOCS) to
develop contracts that meet their business needs.

§ 2. DoITT shall ensure that technology policies and investments are aligned with the
City’s business priorities by working with two governance bodies.

(a) Within 30 days of the signing of this Executive Order, a Strategic Governance Board
chaired by the Deputy Mayor of Operations and consisting of the other Deputy
Mayors, the Commissioner of DoITT, the Director of Management and Budget, the
Director of Operations, and any other Mayor’s Office representative designated by

the Deputy Mayor for Operations shall be convened to develop the Citywide IT
strategy;

(b) Within 30 days of the signing of this Executive Order, a Technology Governance
Board consisting of at least one agency representative designated by each
Commissioner and chaired by an appointee from DoITT shall be convened to develop
technology-enabled business solutions, develop technology standards, rationalize
business-driven exceptions to those standards, and make recommendations to the
Strategic Governance Board concerning IT strategic direction for the City;

(c) Agency Commissioners shall designate a senior executive as a liaison to work with
DoITT to ensure the execution of the obligations of this Executive Order; DoITT
shall likewise designate a liaison to each agency.

§ 3. DoITT shall consolidate IT infrastructure and related operations and services in order
to provide a Citywide shared services IT environment.

(a) DoITT shall work collaboratively with each agency to determine its respective IT
service needs and requirements in connection with its incorporation into the shared
services environment. Each agency will be consolidated into the shared services
environment after its written IT needs and requirements assessment is completed and
agreed to by DoITT and the agency. Agencies shall work with DoITT to achieve
deadlines and deliverables, providing relevant information and the access necessary
to evaluate agency IT infrastructure, including level of investment and existing
service level;

(b) DoITT shall establish and execute a Citywide plan to transfer datacenters and
networks from individual agency management to a shared services environment.
Datacenters and networks shall be operated in place by each City agency, with DoITT
coordination, until such time as they are physically consolidated and
decommissioned, or operated in place by DoITT;

(c) To support a shared services environment, the DoITT Commissioner, each respective
agency Commissioner and the Director of Management and Budget, in consultation
with the Commissioner of Labor Relations and the Commissioner of Citywide
Administrative Services, shall collectively determine the necessary fiscal, IT staffing
and facility resources to transfer from that agency to DoITT;

(d) DoITT shall work with the Office of Management and Budget and the Strategic
Governance Board to determine the appropriate funding mechanism to sustain the
consolidated shared services environment, maximizing the use of non-City funding;

(e) All City agencies shall transition to DoITT-managed email service by December 31,
2011;

(f) All City agencies shall transition to DoITT-managed service desk services by June
30, 2012;

(g) IT services that are not consolidated, including application development, shall
continue to be managed by agencies, subject to review by the Strategic Governance
Board.

§ 4. DoITT shall be responsible for regularly reporting performance metrics with respect
to infrastructure management and process timeframes in accordance with ISO/IEC 20000 and
other industry-recognized standards, and for establishing and achieving service level agreements
with each agency.

§ 5. There are Public Safety technology initiatives and systems that fall outside the
purview of this Executive Order. Such determinations shall be made jointly by the
Commissioner of DoITT and, respectively, the Commissioner of the New York City Police
Department or the Commissioner of the Fire Department of New York.

§ 6. This Order shall not apply to IT systems administered and operated by the State
and/or Federal Government, including local systems identified to be tightly coupled to these
systems during the assessment process, or to IT systems involved in classroom instruction.

§ 7. All agency heads are directed to cooperate fully with DoITT in implementing and
complying with this Order.

§ 8. This Order shall supersede any provisions of prior orders or directives that are
inconsistent with the policy objectives set forth herein.

§ 9. Executive Order 98, dated December 20, 2006 is hereby REVOKED.

§ 10. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

title: TRANSPORTATION BENEFIT PROGRAM
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 141

October 29, 2010

TRANSPORTATION BENEFIT PROGRAM

WHEREAS, federal law authorizes employers to offer their employees the opportunity to
elect to use pre-tax earnings to purchase transit passes for use on mass transit facilities and other
qualified modes of mass transportation, as well as qualified parking benefits; and

WHEREAS, Executive Order No. 49, dated July 7, 2000, as continued by Executive
Order No. 1, dated January 1, 2002, established a transit pass program that allowed City
employees not represented in collective bargaining the opportunity to elect to use pre-tax
earnings to purchase Metrocards; and

WHEREAS, the transit pass program established by Executive Order No. 49 reduced the
cost of mass transportation within the City for employees participating in that program, thereby
making the use of such transportation by City employees for commuting and other purposes a
more attractive option; and

WHEREAS, an expansion of the City’s transit pass program to include other forms of
mass transportation, including regional mass transportation such as commuter railroads and
buses, and qualified parking in conjunction with such mass transportation would further reduce
the cost of transportation for participating City employees, as well as greatly reduce automobile
congestion and resulting emissions in the City;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is
hereby ordered:

Section 1. Definitions.

“City employees” means employees of the City of New York whose pay is processed by
the Office of Payroll Administration; provided, however, that the term “City employees” shall
not include employees who are represented in collective bargaining.

“Qualified parking” means qualified parking as defined in 26 U.S.C. § 132(f) and
applicable federal regulations, provided that such qualified parking is used by a City employee in
conjunction with a transit pass.

“Transit pass” means a transit pass as defined in 26 U.S.C. § 132(f) and applicable
federal regulations, provided that such transit pass is for use on the following types of mass
transportation:

a. City subways and buses, including express buses;

b. the Metropolitan Transportation Authority’s paratransit service;

c. regional commuter railroads; and

d. licensed or otherwise properly authorized regional commuter bus lines, regional
ferries, water taxis and paratransit services for disabled employees.

“Transportation Benefit Program” means the program established in accordance with this
Order pursuant to which City employees are offered the opportunity to elect to use pre-tax and
post-tax earnings to purchase transit passes and qualified parking benefits.

§ 2. Transportation Benefit Program. The Office of Payroll Administration shall hereby
continue and administer a Transportation Benefit Program.

§ 3. Transportation Benefit Program Guidelines and Procedures. The Office of Payroll
Administration shall develop appropriate guidelines and procedures to administer the
Transportation Benefit Program including, without limitation, guidelines and procedures to:

a. establish the procedure by which City employees may elect to participate in the
Transportation Benefit Program;

b. establish the amount of earnings that may be used by City employees to purchase
transit passes and qualified parking benefits;

c. establish a fee, if necessary, to be charged to City employees who participate in the
Transportation Benefit Program to cover the cost of administering such program;

d. establish a cost-effective and secure method for distribution of transit passes and
qualified parking benefits;

e. establish a reimbursement plan for transit passes and qualified parking benefits, if
appropriate;

f. procure any vendors necessary to assist with the implementation of the Transportation
Benefit Program; and

g. establish an appropriate implementation schedule for all aspects of the Transportation
Benefit Program.

§ 4. Employees Represented in Collective Bargaining. The opportunity to elect to use
pre-tax and post-tax earnings to purchase transit passes and qualified parking benefits by
employees who are represented in collective bargaining shall be pursuant to and in accordance
with the collective bargaining process.

§ 5. Prior Executive Order Repealed. Executive Order No. 49, dated July 7, 2000, is
hereby repealed.

§ 6. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

title: DEPUTY MAYORS
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 142
December 10, 2010
DEPUTY MAYORS
By the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:
Section 1. There shall be seven Deputy Mayors. One shall be designated the First Deputy
Mayor, one shall be designated the Deputy Mayor for Education and Community Development,
one shall be designated the Deputy Mayor for Legal Affairs, one shall be designated the Deputy
Mayor for Economic Development, one shall be designated the Deputy Mayor for Operations,
one shall be designated the Deputy Mayor for Government Affairs and Communications, and
one shall be designated the Deputy Mayor for Health and Human Services. All Deputy Mayors
shall collaborate with one another to ensure well coordinated policies, operations, and
administration of government.
§ 2. The First Deputy Mayor shall:
a. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Department of Cultural Affairs, the
Department of Parks and Recreation, the Department of Design and Construction, the
Department of Consumer Affairs, the Commission for the United Nations, Consular Corps and
Protocol, the Commission on Women’s Issues, Office of Veterans’ Affairs, and all
administrations, departments, agencies, boards, offices, committees and commissions except as
otherwise provided herein, provided that the Law Department, the Police Department, the Fire

Department, the Office of Emergency Management, the Department of Investigation, the Office
of Management and Budget, the Office of Labor Relations, and the Office of the Criminal Justice
Coordinator shall report directly to the Mayor.
b. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Mayor’s Offices of Administrative
Services, Appointments, Scheduling and Advance, Correspondence, Special Projects and
Community Events, NYC Service, and Citywide Event Coordination and Management and
supervise City sponsored public events.
c. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Public Design Commission the
Landmarks Preservation Commission, the Mayor’s Fund to Advance New York City, the Gracie
Mansion Conservancy, the Central Park Conservancy, the Governors Island Corporation, the
Brooklyn Bridge Park Corporation, libraries, museums, performing arts organizations, gardens
and zoos.
d. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee,
commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
e. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor, including authorizations and
approvals to be made or given by the Mayor pursuant to sections 384, 824 and 1802 of the
Charter, in relation to the authorization or execution of deeds and satisfactions, leases,
easements, surrenders, restrictive declarations, mortgages and any other grants or acquisitions of
estates or interests in real property and licenses, permits or other agreements affecting the use of
real property.
f. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.
§ 3. The First Deputy Mayor hereby is delegated the authority to perform all functions,
powers or duties of the Mayor which the Mayor is authorized to delegate in the event that the

2

Mayor is unable to perform such functions, powers or duties for a reason specified in subdivision
a of section 10 of the New York City Charter.
§ 4. The Deputy Mayor for Education and Community Development shall:
a. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning, programs and initiatives.
b. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Department of Youth and Community
Development and the Office of Adult Education.
c. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Department of Education, the
New York City School Construction Authority, the New York City Educational Construction
Fund, the City University of New York, the City University Construction Fund and the New
York City Housing Authority.
d. Work with the other Deputy Mayors in coordination with the Office of Management
and Budget and the Office of Operations, to ensure the implementation of Mayoral policies and
initiatives.
e. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee,
commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
e. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.
§ 5. The Deputy Mayor for Legal Affairs shall:
a. Provide counsel to the Mayor on legal matters.
b. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Office of the Administrative Justice
Coordinator, the Commission on Human Rights, the Office to Combat Domestic Violence, the
Office for People with Disabilities, and the Office of Immigrant Affairs.
c. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Mayor's Committee on the
Judiciary, the Conflicts of Interest Board, the Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings, the

3

Environmental Control Board, the Civilian Complaint Review Board, the Commission to
Combat Police Corruption, and the Equal Employment Practices Commission.
d. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee,
commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
e. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.
§ 6. The Deputy Mayor for Economic Development shall:
a. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning, and programs designed to
foster the economic development or growth of the City, including those relating to the City's
overall business climate, the attraction, retention and expansion of domestic and global business
enterprises in the City, efforts to secure unique events, commercial, industrial and residential
development, waterfront development, energy, foreign trade and investment, government
regulation, film, theater and broadcasting, entertainment and sports facility development,
infrastructure, tourism and air, land and sea freight.
b. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Department of City Planning and the
Office of Media and Entertainment.
c. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the City Planning Commission, the
Housing Development Corporation, the United Nations Development Corporation, the Board of
Standards and Appeals, NYC & Company, and the Rent Guidelines Board.
d. Serve as Chairperson of the Commercial Incentive Boundary Area Commission and
the Industrial and Commercial Incentive Board.
e. Supervise and coordinate the activities of the Department of Small Business Services,
the Department of Housing Preservation and Development, Department of Transportation, the
Business Integrity Commission, the Mayor’s Office of Pensions and Investments, and the

4

Economic Development Corporation as provided in the Amended and Restated Contracts
between the City and the Economic Development Corporation, and take such actions thereunder
as are reserved to the Deputy Mayor.

f. Maintain liaison with the New York State Department of Economic Development, the
City Empowerment Zone, the Empire State Development Corporation and its subsidiaries,
including the Lower Manhattan Development Corporation, the Port Authority of New York and
New Jersey, NYC and Company and other governmental and non-governmental agencies and
offices with respect to matters of City economic development and programs.
g. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor, including authorizations and
approvals to be made or given by the Mayor pursuant to sections 384, 824 and 1802 of the
Charter, in relation to the authorization or execution of deeds and satisfactions, leases,
easements, surrenders, restrictive declarations, mortgages and any other grants or acquisitions of
estates or interests in real property and licenses, permits or other agreements affecting the use of
real property.
h. Collaborate with the Deputy Mayor for Operations to advise and assist the Mayor
regarding tax and pension policies.
i. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to any contracts with or
involving the New York City Industrial Development Agency or any other entity created for the
purpose of issuing bonds for, or managing, any project relating to any matter described in this
section.
j. Act for and on behalf of the Mayor in the exercise of all functions, powers and duties
which the Mayor may have pursuant to the New York State Local Finance Law, as the same may
from time to time be amended, the New York State Financial Emergency Act for the City of

5

New York, as the same may from time to time be amended, Article 10 of the Public Authorities
Law, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City Municipal Water
Finance Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, and the New York City
Transitional Authority Act, as the same may from time to time be amended, including, but not
limited to, full power to execute for and on behalf of the Mayor, any agreement, amendment to
such agreement or other document pursuant to such laws.
k. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in relation to the execution or
authorization of such franchises, concessions and revocable consents and other agreements as
relate to the duties of the Deputy Mayor for Economic Development.
l. Perform any function, power or duty which the Mayor has and is authorized to delegate
pursuant to New York City Charter sections 217, 219, 329 and 1301(2)(b) and Administrative
Code section 5-304.
m. Approve and sign applications to secure grant funds, submitted pursuant to provisions
of the New York State Environmental Conservation Law or the rules and regulations of the State
Department of Environmental Conservation, and to sign any other documents as may be
necessary to secure such funds.
n. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor in negotiating, executing and

title: CONTINUING THE LOWER MANHATTAN CONSTRUCTION COMMAND CENTER
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 143

December 16, 2010

CONTINUING THE LOWER MANHATTAN CONSTRUCTION COMMAND
CENTER

WHEREAS, the Lower Manhattan Construction Command Center (“the Command
Center”) was jointly created by New York City Executive Order No. 53, and New York
State Executive Order No. 133; and

WHEREAS, the Command Center was created to coordinate construction in Lower
Manhattan and ensure that projects move forward expeditiously and with the utmost
integrity, while minimizing the impact of such construction on residents, businesses,
workers, commuters, pedestrians, and vehicles; and

WHEREAS, all parties involved in the rebuilding recognize the continuing need for an
entity to coordinate construction projects in Lower Manhattan; and

WHEREAS, all agencies involved in the rebuilding must maintain the ability to manage
their own projects, and an entity coordinating the projects improves their ability to
successfully manage their own projects;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is
hereby ordered:

Section 1. Continuation of the Lower Manhattan Construction Command Center.
The Lower Manhattan Construction Command Center, established by Executive Order
53, shall continue. The Command Center shall coordinate between all construction
located in Lower Manhattan. Lower Manhattan is defined as the area on the island of
Manhattan south of Canal Street and southwest of Rutgers Street from the Hudson River
to the East River. Construction includes all construction work requiring governmental
action or permit, and any construction requiring work directly in City or State streets or
highways.

§2. Lower Manhattan Construction Command Center Executive Director. The
Command Center will be managed by the Lower Manhattan Construction Command
Center Executive Director ("the Executive Director"). Such Executive Director shall be

appointed in a manner to be determined jointly by, and shall report directly to, the
Governor and the Mayor of the City of New York. The Executive Director, and one or
more deputies, will be charged with the day-to-day responsibility for coordinating
construction work in Lower Manhattan with a focus on mitigating impacts on mobility,
maintaining and improving access, and alleviating congestion of any kind related to
construction.

§3. City Operations. A Director of City Operations, appointed by the Mayor after
consultation with the Command Center Executive Director, will ensure the quality of life
of residents and businesses of Lower Manhattan, coordinate City services as they
interface with the construction projects and ensure that logistics and traffic management
plans are appropriately enforced. The Director of City Operations will serve as the
liaison between the Executive Director of the Command Center and all City agencies.

§4. Participation by Public and Private Partners. The Command Center will
coordinate between high level construction personnel from the key participants in the
rebuilding process including the New York City Department of Transportation, the New
York City Department of Design and Construction, the New York City Department of
Buildings, the New York City Economic Development Corporation, the New York City
Department of Environmental Protection, the New York City Department of Sanitation,
the New York City Police Department , the New York City Fire Department, the New
York City Office of Emergency Management, the Port Authority of New York and New
Jersey, the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the New York State Department of
Transportation, the Lower Manhattan Development Corporation, Silverstein Properties,
Verizon, Con Edison, the Alliance for Downtown New York, the Battery Park City
Authority, the Real Estate Board of New York, other public and private partners, and
representatives of such other entities as the Executive Director shall determine
appropriate in carrying out the duties and responsibilities of the Command Center.

§5. Lower Manhattan Construction Executive Committee. The Lower Manhattan
Construction Executive Committee, which includes senior managers designated by the
heads of the New York City Department of Transportation, the New York City Economic
Development Corporation, the New York City Department of Environmental Protection ,
the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, the Metropolitan Transportation
Authority, the New York State Department of Transportation, and the Lower Manhattan
Development Corporation (each in a number to be determined by the Command Center
Executive Director) will advise and consult with the Command Center Executive
Director on the management of the Command Center. This group shall meet as
determined by the Command Center Executive Director (in any event no less than
quarterly) and will be chaired by the Command Center Executive Director.

§6. Traffic Coordination. The New York City Department of Transportation
Lower Manhattan Office, working in consultation with the New York City Police
Department and the New York State Department of Transportation, will be responsible
for all traffic coordination issues and will provide all required Lower Manhattan
construction and lane closure permits in a manner consistent with the law. The Borough

Commissioner of the New York City Department of Transportation Lower Manhattan
Office will coordinate directly with the Executive Director with regard to traffic
management, street permitting, and enforcement.

§7. Functions of the Command Center. The Command Center shall work
collaboratively with public agencies and the private sector to set strategy, facilitate
decision making, provide technical assistance and resolve conflicts to ensure effective
construction coordination, project completion and construction mitigation. The functions
of the Command Center shall include:

a. Construction Coordination: To ensure effective construction coordination the
Command Center shall:

(i) Collaborate with City, State, and Federal regulatory agencies and
managing agencies, as well as with private sector construction
management owners and firms, to develop a construction coordination
plan that addresses: traffic and pedestrian flow, utility work and outages,
construction staging and access, material deliveries and construction
mitigation for numerous construction projects;

(ii) Work with implementing agencies and construction managers to
review and recommend sequencing of construction and resolution of
problems and conflicts to minimize costs, and enable concurrent progress
on jobs;

(iii) Facilitate communication and decision making between key agencies
to address project issues, permitting and site logistics;

(iv) Conduct high-level master scheduling, including tracking major
monthly milestones, with an emphasis on notice to proceed dates,
contractual completions and phasing plans, and adjustments to project
milestones and sequencing;

(v) Evaluate project schedules to determine if there are impediments to
progress and completion, anticipate and resolve potential problems based
on project schedules, and provide recommendations and facilitate
collaborative discussion on the most efficient construction sequencing and
resolution on technical issues; and

(vi) Hold regular Lower Manhattan Construction Progress meetings,
facilitated by a top-level engineering and construction management
consultant and including relevant construction managers, owners, agencies
and utility companies to address progress of jobs and resolve conflicts.

b. Expedite Construction Completion. To facilitate progress and completion of
future and ongoing construction projects the Command Center shall:

(i) Monitor the implementation and completion of ongoing construction in
Lower Manhattan according to scope, schedule and mitigation plan;

(ii) Provide technical assistance on project issues including construction
planning, field conditions or permitting in order to expedite projects and to
address possible delay;

(iii) Highlight critical issues on projects and recommend a course of action
to State and City managing agencies;

(iv) Publicly recognize project milestones to promote the overall
development and increase agency accountability; and

c. Construction Impact Mitigation. To mitigate the impact of construction on
Lower Manhattan the Command Center shall:

(i) Assist with the development, implementation and oversight of
construction mitigation plans. Mitigation plans shall address site
conditions, dust control, noise, traffic, quality of life issues, utilities,
public notices, signage, air quality and other issues;

(ii) Conduct frequent site inspections with regulatory agencies to monitor
site conditions and address issues;

(iii) Hold regular meetings of the Construction Permit Enforcement Task
Force, which includes supervisors from the New York City Department of
Buildings, the New York City Department of Transportation, the New
York City Department of Environmental Protection, the New York City
Police Department, the New York City Fire Department and the New
York City Department of Sanitation to coordinate permit, enforcement,
mitigation and quality of life issues in Lower Manhattan.

(iv) Receive, investigate and respond to citizen’s complaints and inquiries
regarding site conditions, cleanliness, signage, pedestrian access, traffic,
noise, air quality, safety and other issues, and make referrals to appropriate
regulatory agencies;

(v) Work with managing agencies, hold informal training workshops with
prospective contractors to address ways to mitigate construction impacts
on the job sites, and highlight aspects of working in Lower Manhattan;
and

(vi) Assist contractors on ways to comply with regulations or performance
specifications and establish a “tool box” of mitigation strategies to be used
as a resource.

d. Communicate and Report. To communicate to the Governor’s Office, Mayor’s
Office, public and private partners, and the general public, the Command Center
shall:

(i) Maintain and update a public web site with updated construction
information, progress and advisories;

(ii) Give regular presentations and updates on the status of planning,
design and construction progress;

(iii) Draft regular progress reports on projects and identify
recommendations made and implemented by State and City agencies or
private contractors; and

(iv) Attend Community Board meetings to address construction progress
and related concerns.

§8. Agency Assistance and Cooperation. All departments and units of City
government are directed to cooperate fully with the Command Center Executive Director
and to provide such level of assistance as is agreed to by all parties as reasonable and
necessary in fulfilling the obligations of the Command Center, including but not limited
to participation in the construction mitigation and construction coordination task forces,
and the provision of information on project scope, budget, schedule, status of permitting
and mitigation plans.

§9. Project Responsibility. The existence of the Command Center does not
relieve any agency or public or private entity from its responsibility for full management
of its construction project or projects in Lower Manhattan. All aspects of each project
will be the responsibility of the entity building that project.

§10. Powers and Duties of Agencies. Nothing in this Order shall serve as a
limitation on the powers and duties of any State or City agency.

11. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately and shall replace
Executive Order 53 of 2004, which is hereby revoked. This Order shall expire on
December 31, 2013.

Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor
full_text_raw:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 143

December 16, 2010

CONTINUING THE LOWER MANHATTAN CONSTRUCTION COMMAND
CENTER

WHEREAS, the Lower Manhattan Construction Command Center (“the Command
Center”) was jointly created by New York City Executive Order No. 53, and New York
State Executive Order No. 133; and

WHEREAS, the Command Center was created to coordinate construction in Lower
Manhattan and ensure that projects move forward expeditiously and with the utmost
integrity, while minimizing the impact of such construction on residents, businesses,
workers, commuters, pedestrians, and vehicles; and

WHEREAS, all parties involved in the rebuilding recognize the continuing need for an
entity to coordinate construction projects in Lower Manhattan; and

WHEREAS, all agencies involved in the rebuilding must maintain the ability to manage
their own projects, and an entity coordinating the projects improves their ability to
successfully manage their own projects;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is
hereby ordered:

Section 1. Continuation of the Lower Manhattan Construction Command Center.
The Lower Manhattan Construction Command Center, established by Executive Order
53, shall continue. The Command Center shall coordinate between all construction
located in Lower Manhattan. Lower Manhattan is defined as the area on the island of
Manhattan south of Canal Street and southwest of Rutgers Street from the Hudson River
to the East River. Construction includes all construction work requiring governmental
action or permit, and any construction requiring work directly in City or State streets or
highways.

§2. Lower Manhattan Construction Command Center Executive Director. The
Command Center will be managed by the Lower Manhattan Construction Command
Center Executive Director ("the Executive Director"). Such Executive Director shall be

appointed in a manner to be determined jointly by, and shall report directly to, the
Governor and the Mayor of the City of New York. The Executive Director, and one or
more deputies, will be charged with the day-to-day responsibility for coordinating
construction work in Lower Manhattan with a focus on mitigating impacts on mobility,
maintaining and improving access, and alleviating congestion of any kind related to
construction.

§3. City Operations. A Director of City Operations, appointed by the Mayor after
consultation with the Command Center Executive Director, will ensure the quality of life
of residents and businesses of Lower Manhattan, coordinate City services as they
interface with the construction projects and ensure that logistics and traffic management
plans are appropriately enforced. The Director of City Operations will serve as the
liaison between the Executive Director of the Command Center and all City agencies.

§4. Participation by Public and Private Partners. The Command Center will
coordinate between high level construction personnel from the key participants in the
rebuilding process including the New York City Department of Transportation, the New
York City Department of Design and Construction, the New York City Department of
Buildings, the New York City Economic Development Corporation, the New York City
Department of Environmental Protection, the New York City Department of Sanitation,
the New York City Police Department , the New York City Fire Department, the New
York City Office of Emergency Management, the Port Authority of New York and New
Jersey, the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the New York State Department of
Transportation, the Lower Manhattan Development Corporation, Silverstein Properties,
Verizon, Con Edison, the Alliance for Downtown New York, the Battery Park City
Authority, the Real Estate Board of New York, other public and private partners, and
representatives of such other entities as the Executive Director shall determine
appropriate in carrying out the duties and responsibilities of the Command Center.

§5. Lower Manhattan Construction Executive Committee. The Lower Manhattan
Construction Executive Committee, which includes senior managers designated by the
heads of the New York City Department of Transportation, the New York City Economic
Development Corporation, the New York City Department of Environmental Protection ,
the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, the Metropolitan Transportation
Authority, the New York State Department of Transportation, and the Lower Manhattan
Development Corporation (each in a number to be determined by the Command Center
Executive Director) will advise and consult with the Command Center Executive
Director on the management of the Command Center. This group shall meet as
determined by the Command Center Executive Director (in any event no less than
quarterly) and will be chaired by the Command Center Executive Director.

§6. Traffic Coordination. The New York City Department of Transportation
Lower Manhattan Office, working in consultation with the New York City Police
Department and the New York State Department of Transportation, will be responsible
for all traffic coordination issues and will provide all required Lower Manhattan
construction and lane closure permits in a manner consistent with the law. The Borough

Commissioner of the New York City Department of Transportation Lower Manhattan
Office will coordinate directly with the Executive Director with regard to traffic
management, street permitting, and enforcement.

§7. Functions of the Command Center. The Command Center shall work
collaboratively with public agencies and the private sector to set strategy, facilitate
decision making, provide technical assistance and resolve conflicts to ensure effective
construction coordination, project completion and construction mitigation. The functions
of the Command Center shall include:

a. Construction Coordination: To ensure effective construction coordination the
Command Center shall:

(i) Collaborate with City, State, and Federal regulatory agencies and
managing agencies, as well as with private sector construction
management owners and firms, to develop a construction coordination
plan that addresses: traffic and pedestrian flow, utility work and outages,
construction staging and access, material deliveries and construction
mitigation for numerous construction projects;

(ii) Work with implementing agencies and construction managers to
review and recommend sequencing of construction and resolution of
problems and conflicts to minimize costs, and enable concurrent progress
on jobs;

(iii) Facilitate communication and decision making between key agencies
to address project issues, permitting and site logistics;

(iv) Conduct high-level master scheduling, including tracking major
monthly milestones, with an emphasis on notice to proceed dates,
contractual completions and phasing plans, and adjustments to project
milestones and sequencing;

(v) Evaluate project schedules to determine if there are impediments to
progress and completion, anticipate and resolve potential problems based
on project schedules, and provide recommendations and facilitate
collaborative discussion on the most efficient construction sequencing and
resolution on technical issues; and

(vi) Hold regular Lower Manhattan Construction Progress meetings,
facilitated by a top-level engineering and construction management
consultant and including relevant construction managers, owners, agencies
and utility companies to address progress of jobs and resolve conflicts.

b. Expedite Construction Completion. To facilitate progress and completion of
future and ongoing construction projects the Command Center shall:

(i) Monitor the implementation and completion of ongoing construction in
Lower Manhattan according to scope, schedule and mitigation plan;

(ii) Provide technical assistance on project issues including construction
planning, field conditions or permitting in order to expedite projects and to
address possible delay;

(iii) Highlight critical issues on projects and recommend a course of action
to State and City managing agencies;

(iv) Publicly recognize project milestones to promote the overall
development and increase agency accountability; and

c. Construction Impact Mitigation. To mitigate the impact of construction on
Lower Manhattan the Command Center shall:

(i) Assist with the development, implementation and oversight of
construction mitigation plans. Mitigation plans shall address site
conditions, dust control, noise, traffic, quality of life issues, utilities,
public notices, signage, air quality and other issues;

(ii) Conduct frequent site inspections with regulatory agencies to monitor
site conditions and address issues;

(iii) Hold regular meetings of the Construction Permit Enforcement Task
Force, which includes supervisors from the New York City Department of
Buildings, the New York City Department of Transportation, the New
York City Department of Environmental Protection, the New York City
Police Department, the New York City Fire Department and the New
York City Department of Sanitation to coordinate permit, enforcement,
mitigation and quality of life issues in Lower Manhattan.

(iv) Receive, investigate and respond to citizen’s complaints and inquiries
regarding site conditions, cleanliness, signage, pedestrian access, traffic,
noise, air quality, safety and other issues, and make referrals to appropriate
regulatory agencies;

(v) Work with managing agencies, hold informal training workshops with
prospective contractors to address ways to mitigate construction impacts
on the job sites, and highlight aspects of working in Lower Manhattan;
and

(vi) Assist contractors on ways to comply with regulations or performance
specifications and establish a “tool box” of mitigation strategies to be used
as a resource.

d. Communicate and Report. To communicate to the Governor’s Office, Mayor’s
Office, public and private partners, and the general public, the Command Center
shall:

(i) Maintain and update a public web site with updated construction
information, progress and advisories;

(ii) Give regular presentations and updates on the status of planning,
design and construction progress;

(iii) Draft regular progress reports on projects and identify
recommendations made and implemented by State and City agencies or
private contractors; and

(iv) Attend Community Board meetings to address construction progress
and related concerns.

§8. Agency Assistance and Cooperation. All departments and units of City
government are directed to cooperate fully with the Command Center Executive Director
and to provide such level of assistance as is agreed to by all parties as reasonable and
necessary in fulfilling the obligations of the Command Center, including but not limited
to participation in the construction mitigation and construction coordination task forces,
and the provision of information on project scope, budget, schedule, status of permitting
and mitigation plans.

§9. Project Responsibility. The existence of the Command Center does not
relieve any agency or public or private entity from its responsibility for full management
of its construction project or projects in Lower Manhattan. All aspects of each project
will be the responsibility of the entity building that project.

§10. Powers and Duties of Agencies. Nothing in this Order shall serve as a
limitation on the powers and duties of any State or City agency.

11. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately and shall replace
Executive Order 53 of 2004, which is hereby revoked. This Order shall expire on
December 31, 2013.

Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

title: PROCESS FOR RESPONDING TO WINTER WEATHER EMERGENCIES
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 144

January 11, 2011

PROCESS FOR RESPONDING TO WINTER WEATHER EMERGENCIES

WHEREAS, a severe snow storm may constitute an imminent peril to the
public health and safety; and

WHEREAS, the adoption of a clear decision making process for
responding to winter weather emergencies will ensure a coordinated response among City
agencies; and

WHEREAS, New York City Charter § 497(c) and (d) authorize the New
York City Office of Emergency Management to coordinate and prepare plans for
responding to emergency conditions and potential incidents.

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as the Mayor of the City
of New York, it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. OEM shall monitor winter weather forecasts and if snow, a
blizzard or other similar extreme winter weather event is forecast, the OEM
Commissioner shall immediately organize an inter-agency call, which shall include the
Commissioners of the Department of Transportation, Department of Sanitation, Police
Department, Fire Department, any other relevant agency head, and may include the
Deputy Mayor for Operations, to evaluate the forecasted conditions.

§ 2. OEM shall lead the discussion on whether or not the forecast
conditions warrant recommendation of any formal order, declaration, warning, advisory,
or other action. The participants on the inter-agency call shall propose warnings and
restrictions, if any, to be communicated to or imposed on the public.

§ 3. If the Deputy Mayor for Operations did not participate in the call, it
shall be the responsibility of the OEM Commissioner to immediately advise him or her of
the recommendation.

§ 4. Once the Deputy Mayor for Operations reviews and approves the
recommendation, he or she, in conjunction with any other appropriate agency head, shall

advise the Mayor. Based on the recommendation and underlying factors, the Mayor shall
make the final determination as to appropriate actions to be taken.

§ 5. The Deputy Mayor for Operations, and the OEM, Police,
Transportation, and Sanitation Commissioners are hereby ordered to exercise all
appropriate legal authority, including the declaration of a snow emergency, and take all
other steps necessary, to implement the Mayor’s final determination.

§ 6. This Order shall take effect immediately.

Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

title: TRANSFER TO NEW YORK CITY DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND MENTAL HYGIENE OF CERTAIN FUNCTIONS AT THE NEW YORK CITY HEALTH AND HOSPITALS CORPORATION
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 145

February 23, 2011

TRANSFER TO NEW YORK CITY DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND MENTAL HYGIENE OF
CERTAIN FUNCTIONS AT THE NEW YORK CITY HEALTH AND HOSPITALS
CORPORATION

By the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York it is hereby ordered:

Section 1. Effective May 15, 2011, or as soon as practicable thereafter as a transfer may be
effectuated pursuant to the terms and conditions of a duly executed memorandum of understanding
between the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (“DOHMH”) and the New
York City Health and Hospitals Corporation (“HHC”), all HHC staff who are substantially engaged
in the function of assisting DOHMH in its administration of the Assisted Outpatient Treatment
Program in accordance with sections 9.60 and 41.13 of the Mental Hygiene Law and sections 552
and 556 of the New York City Charter shall be transferred to DOHMH.

§ 2.
The Commissioner of Citywide Administrative Services and the Commissioner of
DOHMH shall take all steps necessary, consistent with applicable law, to implement this Order,
including ensuring the transfer of necessary employees substantially engaged in the performance of
the functions to be assumed pursuant to this Order. Employees who are subject to pending
disciplinary charges on the date of the functional transfer, or against whom a disciplinary penalty has
been assessed but not yet served or paid on or prior to such date, shall be retained in the employment
of HHC until the resolution of the adjudicative or administrative proceedings and until any
outstanding disciplinary penalty has been served or paid.

§ 3.
With the purpose of ensuring continuity in operation of the functions described in
section 1, DOHMH and HHC may make appropriate arrangements, prior to the date of the functional
transfer, with respect to appropriate disposition of contracts and agreements entered into by HHC in
relation to the functions being transferred and other appropriate matters, including but not limited to
budgetary arrangements.

§4.
This Order shall take effect immediately.

Michael R. Bloomberg

Mayor

title: CHIEF PENSION ADMINISTRATOR
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 146

April 1, 2011

CHIEF PENSION ADMINISTRATOR

WHEREAS, the City has five pension systems that offer defined benefit retirement plans to
more than 350,000 City employees and 275,000 retirees or their beneficiaries: the New York City
Employees’ Retirement System, the Police Pension Fund, the Fire Pension Fund, the Teachers
Retirement System, and the Board of Education Retirement System (collectively “the Systems”); and

WHEREAS, the Comptroller, through the Bureau of Asset Management, is the investment
advisor to, and custodian of, the five system funds; and

WHEREAS, the City offers a defined contribution plan to its employees, known as the
Deferred Compensation Plan (the “Plan”), which is administered by the Office of Labor Relations;
and

WHEREAS, each of the Systems has a Board of Trustees to fulfill its investment and
administrative functions, including making disability pension determinations, and such Trustees have
a fiduciary responsibility to ensure that all disability determinations and administrative decisions are
made in the best interests of their respective system and the Plan; and

WHEREAS, in addition to the Comptroller and various union leaders, the Mayor and/or
members of the Administration, including the Police Commissioner, Fire Commissioner, Finance
Commissioner, Chancellor of Education and members of the Panel on Educational Policy hold exofficio seats on one or more System boards; and

WHEREAS, pension benefits are defined by law and paid by the Systems to retirees and their
beneficiaries regardless of whether annual investment income and employee contributions are
sufficient to meet these obligations – that is because the City must make contributions to cover any
system shortfalls; and

WHEREAS, because of adverse market conditions, enhancements in statutory benefits, and
increases in the number of disability pensions granted, the City’s pension contributions to cover such
shortfalls have increased dramatically in recent years; and

WHEREAS, to ensure that tax dollars for pension and non-pension related expenses are
used appropriately, it is necessary that the laws, policies and processes that govern pension

determinations and administration are rational and fair both to members of the pension systems
and taxpayers alike;

NOW, THEREFORE, by the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is
hereby ordered that:

Section 1. Chief Pension Administrator. There is hereby established the position of Chief
Pension Administrator. The Chief Pension Administrator (“CPA”) shall:

(a) Serve as the central coordinator and advisor to the Administration's Trustees
("Trustees"), including the Mayor, Finance Commissioner, Police Commissioner, Fire
Commissioner, Schools Chancellor, or their representatives, on the five New York City
Retirement System Boards of Trustees (New York City Employees' Retirement System,
Police Pension Fund, Fire Department Pension Fund, Teachers Retirement System and
Board of Education Retirement System), and the Deferred Compensation Plan Board, on
all administrative and eligibility determinations before the Boards;

(b) Focus on eligibility standards for disability pensions, develop initiatives working with
the Mayoral representatives, other elected officials’ representatives and union trustees to
bring all relevant facts to the pension boards’ attention before pensions are voted,
including exploring new methods to explore the factual basis for disability pension
applications and to advance the administration’s interest in ensuring that applicants for
disability pensions meet the statutory standards;

(c) Work with the Law Department and the Mayor’s legislative and labor relations teams
to develop statutory and administrative reforms and implement all existing statutory
remedies to ensure that proper safeguards are in place to monitor the continuing
eligibility of disability pensioners;

(d) Provide Trustees with analysis of proposed spending initiatives by the Boards and
develop proposals to advance the administration’s interest in increasing operational
efficiency of the City pension funds, reducing administrative costs where possible and
prevent redundant system development;

(e) Interact and communicate with senior officials associated with the governance and
administration of the systems including plan staff, Actuary and Trustee representatives of
Labor and City government;

(f) Consult regularly with the Office of Management and Budget and the Corporation
Counsel regarding the potential fiscal impacts and legal liabilities of matters coming
before the Boards.

(g) Coordinate activities with the Chief Investment Advisor and the Mayor’s Office of
Pensions and Investments.

§ 2. Oversight. The CPA shall report to the Commissioner of Finance. CPA shall consult
regularly with the Office of Management and Budget, Corporation Counsel, the Deputy Mayor for

2

Operations, and the Deputy Mayor for Economic Development, regarding the potential impacts and
legal liabilities of disability and pension policy matters coming before the Boards, as well as any
efforts to reform the City’s pension systems.

§ 3. Cooperation and Assistance. All affected agencies shall cooperate and provide
appropriate assistance to the CPA upon request.

§ 4. Effective Date. This Order shall take effect immediately.

Michael R. Bloomberg
Mayor

title: DEPUTY MAYORS
full_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 147
April 25, 2011
DEPUTY MAYORS
By the power vested in me as Mayor of the City of New York, it is hereby ordered:
Section 1. There shall be six Deputy Mayors. One shall be designated the First Deputy
Mayor, one shall be designated the Deputy Mayor for Legal Affairs, one shall be designated the
Deputy Mayor for Economic Development, one shall be designated the Deputy Mayor for
Operations, one shall be designated the Deputy Mayor for Government Affairs and
Communications, and one shall be designated the Deputy Mayor for Health and Human
Services. All Deputy Mayors shall collaborate with one another to ensure well coordinated
policies, operations, and administration of government.
§ 2. The First Deputy Mayor shall:
a. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Department of Cultural Affairs, the
Department of Parks and Recreation, the Department of Design and Construction, the
Department of Consumer Affairs, the Commission for the United Nations, Consular Corps and
Protocol, the Commission on Women’s Issues, Office of Veterans’ Affairs, and all
administrations, departments, agencies, boards, offices, committees and commissions except as
otherwise provided herein, provided that the Department of Education, Law Department, the
Police Department, the Fire Department, the Office of Emergency Management, the Department

of Investigation, the Office of Management and Budget, the Office of Labor Relations, and the
Office of the Criminal Justice Coordinator shall report directly to the Mayor.
b. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Mayor’s Offices of Administrative
Services, Appointments, Scheduling and Advance, Correspondence, Special Projects and
Community Events, NYC Service, and Citywide Event Coordination and Management and
supervise City sponsored public events.
c. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Public Design Commission the
Landmarks Preservation Commission, the Mayor’s Fund to Advance New York City, the Gracie
Mansion Conservancy, the Central Park Conservancy, the Governors Island Corporation, the
Brooklyn Bridge Park Corporation, libraries, museums, performing arts organizations, gardens
and zoos.
d. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee,
commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
e. Perform any function, power or duty of the Mayor, including authorizations and
approvals to be made or given by the Mayor pursuant to sections 384, 824 and 1802 of the
Charter, in relation to the authorization or execution of deeds and satisfactions, leases,
easements, surrenders, restrictive declarations, mortgages and any other grants or acquisitions of
estates or interests in real property and licenses, permits or other agreements affecting the use of
real property.
f. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.
§ 3. The First Deputy Mayor hereby is delegated the authority to perform all functions,
powers or duties of the Mayor which the Mayor is authorized to delegate in the event that the

2

Mayor is unable to perform such functions, powers or duties for a reason specified in subdivision
a of section 10 of the New York City Charter.
§ 4. The Deputy Mayor for Legal Affairs shall:
a. Provide counsel to the Mayor on legal matters.
b. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Office of the Administrative Justice
Coordinator, the Commission on Human Rights, the Office to Combat Domestic Violence, the
Office for People with Disabilities, and the Office of Immigrant Affairs.
c. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the Mayor's Committee on the
Judiciary, the Conflicts of Interest Board, the Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings, the
Environmental Control Board, the Civilian Complaint Review Board, the Commission to
Combat Police Corruption, and the Equal Employment Practices Commission.
d. Represent the Mayor, when so directed by the Mayor, on any board, committee,
commission or corporation of which the Mayor is a member.
e. Perform such other duties as the Mayor may direct.
§ 5. The Deputy Mayor for Economic Development shall:
a. Advise and assist the Mayor regarding all policies, planning, and programs designed to
foster the economic development or growth of the City, including those relating to the City's
overall business climate, the attraction, retention and expansion of domestic and global business
enterprises in the City, efforts to secure unique events, commercial, industrial and residential
development, waterfront development, energy, foreign trade and investment, government
regulation, film, theater and broadcasting, entertainment and sports facility development,
infrastructure, tourism and air, land and sea freight.

3

b. Supervise and coordinate the operations of the Department of City Planning and the
Office of Media and Entertainment.
c. Maintain liaison with and review the activities of the City Planning Commission, New
York City Housing Authority, the Housing Development Corporation, the United Nations
Development Corporation, the Board of Standards and Appeals, NYC & Company, and the Rent
Guidelines Board.
d. Serve as Chairperson of the Commercial Incentive Boundary Area Commission and
